# hackbuild-browser-ai

> hackbuild-browser-ai is a set of ESM packages under @hackbuild that run language, vision and speech models in a browser tab: one chat interface over local runtimes (WebLLM, wllama, transformers.js, the Chrome Prompt API) and remote endpoints, a resumable weight store, structured output for small models, memory with a Rust wasm core, speech in and out, transcription, vision, image generation, character cards and an agent loop. Runtimes are optional peers that you load and pass in; weights are never bundled and load from their upstream host through @hackbuild/weights; every package has a single file build that runs from file://.

Every package is ESM only with types included, installs from npm under @hackbuild, and is MIT. Each llms.md below lists the package's exports with signatures, minimal examples and the mistakes to avoid. Code: https://github.com/hackbuild/hackbuild-browser-ai

## Packages

- [@hackbuild/act](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/act/llms.md): Let a language model act while it speaks: mood, gesture and posture tags in its reply fire when the voice reaches them, limited to names your avatar can realize.
- [@hackbuild/agent](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/agent/llms.md): Run an agent turn sized for small models in a browser tab: perceive, recall, decide, act and reflect, over tools you give it.
- [@hackbuild/ai-elements](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/ai-elements/llms.md): Deprecated: use [@hackbuild/ai-views](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/ai-views/llms.md), which draws the same views with hackbuild-ui as custom elements and Vue components.
- [@hackbuild/ai-env](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/ai-env/llms.md): Find out what the tab can run, and load runtimes and workers in a way that also works from a file:// page.
- [@hackbuild/ai-views](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/ai-views/llms.md): Put a model picker, a chat, a transcriber, a mask studio or a camera frame on your page, drawn with the hackbuild-ui stylesheet, as custom elements or Vue components.
- [@hackbuild/audio-dsp](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/audio-dsp/llms.md): Filter, clean, measure and time speech and music in the tab on a Rust wasm core, and write the WAV, MIDI, subtitle and zip files the results go into.
- [@hackbuild/biosignal](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/biosignal/llms.md): Filter EEG, train a Riemannian classifier on it and cross validate it without leaks, in a Rust wasm core that runs in your tab.
- [@hackbuild/character](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/character/llms.md): Read, upgrade, check and write character cards in the tab, as JSON, PNG or CHARX, with a profile that names a character's body, voice and actions.
- [@hackbuild/chat](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/chat/llms.md): Stream chat replies from WebLLM, wllama, transformers.js, the Chrome Prompt API or a remote endpoint through one interface.
- [@hackbuild/converse](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/converse/llms.md): Run a conversation over a streaming chat engine with the history rules small models need, and save it as a versioned chat session.
- [@hackbuild/depth-mesh](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/depth-mesh/llms.md): Turn a depth map, a photo or turntable silhouettes into a closed solid you can print, with a Rust wasm core that runs in your tab.
- [@hackbuild/devices](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/devices/llms.md): Plug onnxruntime-web and transformers.js into the models hub, with device ladders, pinned runtime imports and failure lines your users can read.
- [@hackbuild/embed](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/embed/llms.md): Turn sentences into vectors in the tab, for memory recall and action matching, with an id that changes only when the vectors would.
- [@hackbuild/imagegen](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/imagegen/llms.md): Generate an image from a prompt in your tab with SD-Turbo or SD 1.5 on onnxruntime-web WebGPU, seeded so the same seed gives the same start.
- [@hackbuild/listen](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/listen/llms.md): You feed it microphone blocks and it hands back each thing the person said as text, and tells you when they talk over your character.
- [@hackbuild/media](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/media/llms.md): Decode a file's audio at the rate a model wants, pick keyframes from a video, and record a canvas, all in the tab.
- [@hackbuild/memory](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/memory/llms.md): Give an agent or character in a browser tab a memory you can add to, recall from and fit into a prompt, with a wasm core and IndexedDB storage.
- [@hackbuild/models](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/models/llms.md): Describe each model once, with its runtime, device ladder, size and weight licence, and let a hub load the one that fits this machine.
- [@hackbuild/notes](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/notes/llms.md): Turn a recording into notes, drum hits, a tempo and a MIDI file, in the tab.
- [@hackbuild/speak](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/speak/llms.md): You give it a reply as it streams and it speaks it through the first voice engine that works, telling you which character of your text the voice has reached.
- [@hackbuild/stems](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/stems/llms.md): Split a song into drums, bass, other and vocals with htdemucs, in the tab.
- [@hackbuild/structured](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/structured/llms.md): Get a tool decision or tagged text out of a small model in the tab, in the format that model and runtime can keep to.
- [@hackbuild/transcribe](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/transcribe/llms.md): Turn a recording into timed text in the tab, with Whisper or Moonshine behind a front end that finds quiet speech and drops the lines a model writes over silence.
- [@hackbuild/vision](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/vision/llms.md): Get depth, objects, masks, landmarks and captions from an image or a webcam in your tab, through one models hub that shares the GPU with your scene.
- [@hackbuild/weights](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/weights/llms.md): Download model weights once, resume them when the download breaks, check their SHA-256, and keep them on the machine for the next visit.

# @hackbuild/act

> Let a language model act while it speaks: mood, gesture and posture tags in its reply fire when the voice reaches them, limited to names your avatar can realize.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/act/

## Purpose

- Takes tags such as `[happy]`, `*waves*`, `[mood: sad]` and `[happy, wave]` out of a streamed reply and hands speech the visible text.
- Holds each cue until speech reports the character offset where the tag sat, then fires it.
- Keeps names to the avatar's own moods (expression presets), gestures (one shot clips) and postures (held clips), with a strict resolver and an alias table.
- Writes the prompt block and a GBNF grammar or JSON Schema that hold a model to that vocabulary.
- Binds an avatar's expression list and clip library to the vocabulary, and infers a mood or gesture for untagged sentences in hybrid mode.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/act
```

It depends on `@hackbuild/structured` for the streaming tag parser. `@hackbuild/memory` is an optional peer: install it when you pass an embedder for the embedding steps of the resolver, the inferrer or `pickClip`. No model ships here, and the package imports no speech engine.

## Exports

### @hackbuild/act

```ts
interface ActBinding {
  acts: Required<AvatarActs>;
  all: BoundClip[];
  clips: Record<string, BoundClip[]>;
  loops: { idle: BoundClip[]; talk: BoundClip[] };
  manual: BoundClip[];
}
```

What `bindActs` returns: the lists for `buildVocabulary`, the clips behind each name, the loops and the clips kept out of replies.

```ts
const ACTION_WORDS: WordTable
```

Whole body moves and stances, also explicit only.

```ts
type ActKind = "mood" | "gesture" | "posture"
```

The three kinds of act: a mood on the face, a one shot gesture, or a posture the body holds.

```ts
interface ActVocabulary {
  aliases: Record<string, string>;
  gestures: string[];
  moods: string[];
  postures: string[];
}
```

The moods, gestures and postures one avatar can realize, with an alias table from other words to those names.

```ts
function aliasesFrom(...tables: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>[]): Record<string, string>
```

Word to bucket name over several tables; the first table that holds a word wins.

```ts
interface AvatarActs {
  expressions?: readonly string[];
  gestures?: readonly string[];
  postures?: readonly string[];
}
```

What an avatar can realize: expression presets, gesture clips and posture clips.

```ts
function bindActs(input: { clips?: readonly ClipInfo[]; expressions?: readonly string[] }, o?: BindOptions): ActBinding
```

Bind an avatar's expressions and clips to `act`.

```ts
interface BindOptions {
  buckets?: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>;
  max?: number;
  rules?: readonly ClipRule[];
}
```

Options for `bindActs`: names per kind, clip rules and extra word buckets.

```ts
interface BoundClip extends ClipInfo {
  buckets: string[];
  cls: ClipClass;
  description?: string;
  folder?: string;
  id: string;
  label: string;
  name: string;
  pose?: boolean;
  tags?: readonly string[];
  userTags?: readonly string[];
}
```

A clip after binding: its class, the word buckets it sits in, and the label the model sees.

```ts
function bucketOf(table: WordTable, text: string): string | null
```

The bucket a word or phrase names, whole words only: "across" is not "cross", "understand" is not "stand".

```ts
function bucketsOf(table: WordTable, phrases: readonly string[]): string[]
```

Every bucket a list of phrases touches.

```ts
function buildVocabulary(avatar: AvatarActs, opts?: { aliases?: Record<string, string>; defaults?: boolean }): ActVocabulary
```

Build a vocabulary from what the avatar can do.

```ts
function classifyClip(c: Pick<ClipInfo, "name" | "folder" | "tags" | "userTags">, rules?: readonly ClipRule[]): ClipClass
```

The class of one clip.

```ts
const CLIP_CLASSES: readonly ClipClass[]
```

Every clip class, in order.

```ts
const CLIP_RULES: readonly ClipRule[]
```

The eight rules, first match wins, narrow rules first.

```ts
type ClipClass = "idle" | "talk" | "gesture" | "posture" | "dance" | "reaction" | "locomotion" | "action" | "odd"
```

The nine classes a clip sorts into, from idle and talk loops to clips kept for playing by hand.

```ts
interface ClipInfo {
  description?: string;
  folder?: string;
  id: string;
  name: string;
  pose?: boolean;
  tags?: readonly string[];
  userTags?: readonly string[];
}
```

One clip of an avatar's library as the app describes it: id, name, folder, description and tags.

```ts
interface ClipRule {
  cls: ClipClass;
  re: RegExp;
}
```

A rule that puts a clip in a class when its folder and name match the pattern.

```ts
function cosine(a: Float32Array, b: Float32Array): number
```

The cosine similarity of two vectors, 0 when either is all zeros.

```ts
function createDirector(o: DirectorOptions): Director
```

Make a director over a vocabulary that places cues as the reply streams and fires them as speech reports offsets.

```ts
function createInferrer(v: ActVocabulary, o?: InferrerOptions): Inferrer
```

Make an inferrer over a vocabulary's moods and gestures; postures are never inferred.

```ts
function createResolver(v: ActVocabulary, o?: ResolverOptions): Resolver
```

Make a resolver over a vocabulary: exact name, alias, whole word overlap, then the nearest embedding above the floor.

```ts
interface Cue {
  at: number;
  kind: ActKind;
  name: string;
  raw: string;
  source: "json" | "tag" | "infer" | "replay";
}
```

An act placed at an offset of the visible text, with the tag or sentence it came from.

```ts
const CUE_CLASSES: ReadonlySet<ClipClass>
```

Classes a reply may set off on its own.

```ts
const CUE_POSE_SECONDS: 6
```

A pose picked by a cue relaxes back after this many seconds (vendor).

```ts
function cuesFromJson(obj: unknown): { names: { kind: "mood" | "gesture" | "posture"; name: string }[]; say: string }
```

Cues from a JSON reply in the json style: all sit at offset 0 of the say text.

```ts
const DEFAULT_ALIASES: Readonly<Record<string, string>>
```

Common words for the usual names: the hand table below, then every word of the word tables (hand entries win).

```ts
const DEFAULT_KEYWORDS: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>
```

Keywords per common name: the hand table plus the mood and gesture word tables.

```ts
interface Director {
  begin(): void;
  feed(chunk: string): { cues: Cue[]; text: string };
  finish(): { cues: Cue[]; text: string };
  json(obj: unknown): { cues: Cue[]; say: string };
  mood(): { name: string; weight: number } | null;
  pending(): readonly Cue[];
  posture(): string | null;
  reached(offset: number): FiredCue[];
  record(): ReplayRecord;
  settle(): Promise<void>;
}
```

Reads a streamed reply, returns the visible text for speech and fires each cue when speech reaches its offset.

```ts
interface DirectorOptions {
  embedder?: Embedder;
  fire: (cue: FiredCue) => void;
  gestureCooldownMs?: number;
  inferrer?: Inferrer;
  mode?: "tags" | "hybrid" | "off";
  moodDecayMs?: number;
  moodFloor?: number;
  now?: () => number;
  onSuppressed?: (cue: Suppressed) => void;
  resolver?: Resolver;
  vocab: ActVocabulary;
}
```

Options for `createDirector`: the vocabulary, the mode, the fire callback, an optional embedder and the timing settings.

```ts
const EMOTION_WORDS: WordTable
```

Mood buckets: the words that name each of eleven moods, from happy to excited.

```ts
interface FiredCue extends Cue {
  at: number;
  kind: ActKind;
  name: string;
  raw: string;
  source: "json" | "tag" | "infer" | "replay";
  t: number;
}
```

A cue that fired, with the clock time in ms.

```ts
const GESTURE_WORDS: WordTable
```

Conversational gestures: small moves that fit a sentence, so inference may fire them.

```ts
function grammar(v: ActVocabulary, format: "gbnf" | "json-schema"): string
```

A GBNF grammar (llama.cpp and wllama) or a JSON Schema (WebLLM XGrammar, remote json_schema) for replies that use only this vocabulary.

```ts
function idleLoop(clips: readonly BoundClip[]): BoundClip | null
```

The idle loop: a standing idle clip, calm names first; null when the library has none.

```ts
interface Inferred {
  kind: "mood" | "gesture";
  name: string;
  score: number;
  via: "embed" | "keyword";
}
```

A mood or gesture inferred from an untagged sentence, with its score and the step that found it.

```ts
interface Inferrer {
  infer(sentence: string): Promise<Inferred | null>;
  keyword(sentence: string): Inferred | null;
}
```

Infers a mood or gesture from a sentence, by keywords and then by embedding.

```ts
interface InferrerOptions {
  embedder?: Embedder;
  floor?: number;
  keywords?: Record<string, readonly string[]>;
  margin?: number;
  weak?: readonly string[];
  weakWords?: readonly string[];
}
```

Options for `createInferrer`: keyword tables, weak phrases and words, and the embedding floor and margin.

```ts
function kindOf(v: ActVocabulary, name: string): ActKind | null
```

The kind of a vocabulary name, ignoring case, or null when the avatar has no such name.

```ts
const KINDS: readonly ActKind[]
```

The act kinds in order: mood, gesture, posture.

```ts
function meaningfulWords(s: string): string[]
```

Meaningful words of a name: no numbers, no format noise, no one letter fragments.

```ts
const MOOD_RELATIVES: Readonly<Record<string, string>>
```

Moods with no preset on many avatars, and the near relative to show instead.

```ts
const MOTION_WORDS: WordTable
```

Everything a motion can be named for: gestures, postures and actions.

```ts
const NAMED_BONUS: 0.15
```

A clip named for the thing ("Sitting 1" for sit) beats one that only carries it as a tag by this much (vendor).

```ts
function namesOf(v: ActVocabulary, kind: ActKind): string[]
```

The vocabulary's names of one kind.

```ts
function nameTokens(s: string): string[]
```

"HairRibbon_02" to ["hair", "ribbon", "02"]; "IdleHappyWave01" to ["idle", "happy", "wave", "01"].

```ts
const OPTIONAL_BUCKETS: WordTable
```

Buckets left out of the defaults; the owner of an app decides whether to turn them on.

```ts
function pickClip(binding: ActBinding, name: string, sentence: string, o: { buckets?: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>; embedder?: Embedder; rng: () => number }): Promise<BoundClip | null>
```

The clip for a resolved name that best fits what was said, or null when the avatar has no clip for it.

```ts
const POSTURE_WORDS: WordTable
```

Postures change how the body rests: only an explicit tag takes one, never a word in passing ("i won't lie").

```ts
function promptBlock(v: ActVocabulary, o?: PromptOptions): string
```

The system prompt lines that tell the model which tags it may use, in the tags or json style.

```ts
interface PromptOptions {
  max?: { gestures?: number; moods?: number; postures?: number };
  style?: "tags" | "json";
}
```

Options for `promptBlock`: the reply style and how many names of each kind to list.

```ts
function replay(rec: ReplayRecord, fire: (cue: FiredCue) => void, now?: () => number): { reached(offset: number): FiredCue[] }
```

Replay a recorded reply: the same cues fire at the same offsets when the reply is spoken again, with no model and no inference.

```ts
interface ReplayRecord {
  cues: { at: number; kind: ActKind; name: string }[];
}
```

The cues that fired in one reply, by offset, for `replay`.

```ts
interface Resolved {
  kind: ActKind;
  name: string;
  via: "exact" | "alias" | "words" | "embed";
}
```

A name resolved to the vocabulary: its kind, the avatar's name, and the step that found it.

```ts
interface Resolver {
  resolve(name: string, kind?: ActKind | null): Resolved | null;
  resolveAsync(name: string, kind?: ActKind | null): Promise<Resolved | null>;
}
```

Resolves a name a model wrote to a vocabulary name, lexically or with the embedding step.

```ts
interface ResolverOptions {
  embedder?: Embedder;
  floor?: number;
}
```

Options for `createResolver`: an optional embedder and its cosine floor.

```ts
function stem(w: string): string
```

Light stemmer: lowercase and strip ing, ed, es, s (and a doubled final consonant after ing or ed).

```ts
interface Suppressed extends Cue {
  at: number;
  kind: ActKind;
  name: string;
  raw: string;
  reason: "repeat" | "cooldown";
  source: "json" | "tag" | "infer" | "replay";
}
```

A cue that did not fire because it repeated the current mood or posture, or fell inside the gesture cooldown.

```ts
function surfaceForms(v: ActVocabulary): string[]
```

Every surface form (names and alias words), longest first.

```ts
function talkingLoop(clips: readonly BoundClip[]): BoundClip | null
```

The loop to stand in while talking: a talk clip named as a standing idle.

```ts
const WEAK_PHRASES: readonly string[]
```

Phrases removed before keyword matching: they read as feeling words but are filler.

```ts
const WEAK_WORDS: readonly string[]
```

Single words too common to carry a feeling or a gesture on their own ("right", "sure", "love", "show"): skipped by the keyword step.

```ts
function words(s: string): string[]
```

The lowercase words of a string, letters and digits, with apostrophes removed.

```ts
type WordTable = Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>
```

Bucket name to the words that name it.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { buildVocabulary, createDirector, grammar, promptBlock } from "@hackbuild/act";

// the names this avatar can realize
const vocab = buildVocabulary({ expressions: ["happy", "sad", "surprised"], gestures: ["wave", "nod"], postures: ["sit"] });

// add the tag list to the system prompt; pass the grammar where the runtime takes one
const system = `You are Ada.\n\n${promptBlock(vocab)}`;
const gbnf = grammar(vocab, "gbnf");
console.log(system, gbnf);

// strip tags from the streamed reply and fire each cue when the voice reaches it
const director = createDirector({ vocab, mode: "hybrid", fire: (cue) => console.log(cue.kind, cue.name, "at", cue.at) });
director.begin();
let spoken = "";
for (const chunk of ["[happy] Hello there, ", "*waves* nice to ", "see you."]) spoken += director.feed(chunk).text;
spoken += director.finish().text;

// speech reports character offsets in the visible text it was given
director.reached(spoken.length);
```

### from the concepts

```ts
import { bindActs, buildVocabulary, createResolver, pickClip, talkingLoop, idleLoop } from "@hackbuild/act";

const binding = bindActs({ expressions: avatar.expressions, clips: library.map((c) => ({ id: c.id, name: c.name, folder: c.folder, tags: c.analysisTags })) });
const vocab = buildVocabulary(binding.acts);
const r = createResolver(vocab).resolve(tag);
const clip = r && r.kind !== "mood" ? await pickClip(binding, r.name, sentence, { rng }) : null;   // null: no clip for it, do nothing
const idle = idleLoop(binding.all);
const talk = talkingLoop(binding.all);
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- You expect untagged sentences to fire cues. The director mode defaults to `"tags"`; pass `mode: "hybrid"` to `createDirector` to run the inferrer on sentences with no tag.
- You fire cues as the text streams in. `feed` and `finish` only place cues; call `director.reached(offset)` with the character offset your voice reports in the visible text, and cues fire then.
- You send the raw model text to speech. Send the `text` that `feed` and `finish` return, which has the tags stripped, and keep the raw tagged reply in the chat history so the model keeps tagging.
- You call `pickClip` without an `rng`. It requires `{ rng }`; pass a seeded function returning numbers in 0 to 1, since nothing here calls Math.random.
- You list clip names the avatar cannot play. Build the vocabulary with `buildVocabulary` from the avatar's own expressions and clips, or from `bindActs(...).acts`, so `promptBlock` and `grammar` offer only names it can realize.
- You read `director.record()` right after `finish` when you pass an `embedder`. Cues the embedder resolves or infers arrive later; await `director.settle()` first.

## Errors this package throws

- no cue fires (speech never calls `reached`, or reports offsets in other text): call `reached(offset)` with offsets into the text `feed` and `finish` returned
- `onSuppressed` with `repeat` (the same mood still shows, or the same posture is held): expected; lower `moodFloor` or `moodDecayMs` to allow repeats sooner
- `onSuppressed` with `cooldown` (a gesture inside `gestureCooldownMs` of the last): expected; lower `gestureCooldownMs`
- a tag vanishes from speech and fires nothing (it named nothing the avatar has, so it was read as a stage direction): add the word as an alias, or add a clip for it
- the model stops tagging after a few turns (tags were stripped from the chat history): keep the raw tagged reply in history
- a posture never comes from speech (postures fire only from explicit tags): expected; ask the model to tag it

---

# @hackbuild/agent

> Run an agent turn sized for small models in a browser tab: perceive, recall, decide, act and reflect, over tools you give it.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/agent/

## Purpose

- Runs a tool loop on a forced JSON turn contract, stepping down to a looser schema and then free text, with guards from `@hackbuild/structured`.
- Gives you a reflex brain of regex rules that works with no model and also writes hints for the smallest models.
- Keeps persistent goals with planners that need no model, skip lists, blocking and one report per ended goal.
- Builds a token budgeted context from ranked sections and memory, and caches plans that worked.
- Chains planners (model, scripted, reflex) and records why each one stepped down.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/agent
```

It depends on `@hackbuild/chat`, `@hackbuild/structured` and `@hackbuild/memory`, which install with it; there are no peers. No model ships here: the brain is a chat engine you create with `@hackbuild/chat`, or none.

## Exports

```ts
  heard: string | null;
```

```ts
class ToolError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string);

```

```ts

  calls: number;
  ended: Ended;
  goal: Goal | null;
```


```ts
type Why = "heard" | "goal" | "free" | "report"
```

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { createAgent, Reflex, ToolError, type Tool } from "@hackbuild/agent";

// tools the agent can call; a ToolError is read back to the model in first person
const tools: Tool[] = [
  { name: "go_to", description: "walk to a place", parameters: { type: "object", properties: { place: { type: "string", enum: ["table", "shelf"] } }, required: ["place"] }, run: ([place]) => `at the ${place}` },
  { name: "pick_up", description: "pick up a thing", parameters: { type: "object", properties: { thing: { type: "string" } }, required: ["thing"] }, run: ([thing]) => {
    if (thing !== "mug") throw new ToolError(`i do not see a ${thing} here.`);
  } },
];

// rules that map a clause to steps with no model
const reflex = new Reflex().add(/^go to (?:the )?(\w+)/, (m) => [{ tool: "go_to", args: [m[1]!] }]).add(/^pick up (?:the )?(.+)/, (m) => [{ tool: "pick_up", args: [m[1]!] }]);

// brain: pass a ChatEngine from @hackbuild/chat for model turns; null runs the reflex brain alone
const agent = createAgent({ tools, brain: null, mode: "reflex", soul: "You are a helpful robot.", reflex, onSay: (text) => console.log(text) });

// one heard turn: how it ended, each step's result, and the running cost
const turn = await agent.handle("go to the table, then pick up the mug", "heard");
console.log(turn.ended, turn.results.map((r) => `${r.step.tool}: ${r.text}`), agent.cost);
```

### from the concepts

```ts
import { createPlannerChain, dropLine, Reflex } from "@hackbuild/agent";
import { scripted } from "@hackbuild/chat";

const chain = createPlannerChain({
  tools: registry.names,
  getModel: () => brain,                 // null until a brain loads
  loading: () => brainLoading,
  scripted: scripted({ replies: cannedPlans }),
  reflex,
});
const r = await chain.plan({ text: heard, messages });
if (r) await run(r.plan.do);
for (const d of chain.lastDrops) inspector.push(dropLine(d), d.raw);
// "the brain returned no valid plan three times. reflexes took over."
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- You import a model runtime into the agent. The agent loads no runtime and no weights; pass a `ChatEngine` from `@hackbuild/chat` as `brain`, or `brain: null` to run the reflex brain and goal planners alone.
- You throw a plain `Error` from a tool for an expected failure. Throw `ToolError` with a first person sentence such as `i do not see a mug here.`; that text is what the model reads next.
- You leave `rng` unset and every free tick picks the first `idle` plan. Pass a seeded `rng` to `createAgent` when you give it `idle` plans.
- You set `mode: "reflex"` without a `reflex`. Give it a `Reflex` with `add(pattern, steps)` rules; with no brain, requests the rules cannot map end the turn as `no-brain`.
- You read only the spoken text after `handle`. Check `turn.ended` too: `failures`, `repeat`, `steps` and `guard` mean the turn stopped early, and `turn.results` holds each step's text.

## Errors this package throws

- `i do not know how to <tool>. i can: <tools>.` (the plan named a tool the registry lacks): expected for drifted replies; check the tool names in the prompt
- `<tool> needs <args>; i was given <args>.` (fewer arguments than the schema requires): expected; the model reads it and tries again
- `i cannot <tool> <arg>: <param> is one of <values>.` (an argument outside the enum): expected; check the enum matches what the host offers
- `<param> for <tool> is a number; i was given <arg>.` (a non numeric argument for a number): expected; the model reads it and tries again
- `<tool> failed: <message>` (a tool threw an error that is not a `ToolError`): throw `ToolError` with a first person sentence for expected failures
- `i was stopped.` (the turn was cancelled during a step): expected after `cancel()`
- `i do not know how to do that yet.` (turn ends `no-brain`) (`brain: null`, and no rule, cache entry or planner mapped the request): add a reflex rule, or pass a chat engine as the brain
- `the brain returned no valid plan three times. reflexes took over.` (the model tier of the chain gave no valid plan in `tries` calls): try a larger model, the looser schema, or hints mode
- `no brain loaded.` (the chain's model tier is absent): expected until `getModel` returns an engine

---

# @hackbuild/ai-elements

> Deprecated: use [@hackbuild/ai-views](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/ai-views/llms.md), which draws the same views with hackbuild-ui as custom elements and Vue components.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/ai-elements/

Deprecated: use @hackbuild/ai-views (https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/ai-views/llms.md).

## Purpose

- `define(prefix = "hb")` registers the ai-views custom elements under the prefix and writes one deprecation note to the console.
- `ELEMENT_NAMES`, `mountMemoryInspector`, `traceRows` and `inspectorHtml` are re-exported from ai-views.
- The model picker, download bar, status pills and chat panel of 0.1 are gone; use `<model-select>`, `<chat-pane>` and `<chat-composer>` from ai-views.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/ai-views
```

Existing code that imports the old name keeps working with `npm install @hackbuild/ai-elements`.

## Exports

### @hackbuild/ai-elements

```ts
function define(prefix?: string, registry?: DefineTarget, Base?: new () => HTMLElement): string[]
```

Registers the ai-views elements under the prefix (default hb) and notes the deprecation once.

```ts
interface DefineTarget {
  define(name: string, ctor: CustomElementConstructor): void;
  get(name: string): unknown;
}
```

The part of a custom element registry `define` uses; `customElements` satisfies it.

```ts
const DEPRECATION: "@hackbuild/ai-elements is deprecated. use @hackbuild/ai-views: <model-select>, <chat-pane>, <chat-composer>, <memory-inspector> and the other views."
```

Written once to the console by define().

```ts
const ELEMENT_NAMES: readonly ["model-select", "model-jobs", "chat-pane", "chat-composer", "chat-list", "chat-context", "transcribe-drop", "transcript-view", "transcribe-queue", "transcript-exports", "mask-studio", "mask-tools", "mask-verbs", "mask-rack", "frame-view", "camera-feed", "memory-inspector"]
```

The tag names define() registers, before any prefix.

```ts
function inspectorHtml(rec: RecallLike | null): string
```

The HTML of a recall trace table, or an empty note before any recall.

```ts
interface MemoryInspector extends Mounted {
  dispose(): void;
  set(rec: RecallLike | null): void;
}
```

A mounted memory inspector whose `set` shows a new recall.

```ts
function mountMemoryInspector(host: HTMLElement, rec?: RecallLike | null): MemoryInspector
```

Shows a recall trace as a table on a host.

```ts
type RecallLike = Pick<Recall, "trace" | "hits" | "query" | "mode">
```

The parts of a memory recall the inspector shows: trace, hits, query and mode.

```ts
interface TraceRow {
  bm25: string;
  cos: string;
  id: number;
  kind: string;
  rank: number;
  rrf: string;
  score: string;
  text: string;
  used: boolean;
}
```

One row of a recall trace as text: rank, id, kind, text, BM25, cosine, RRF, score, and whether it went to the model.

```ts
function traceRows(r: Pick<Recall, "trace" | "hits">, maxText?: number): TraceRow[]
```

The rows of a recall trace as text, marking the hits handed to the model.

## Mistakes to avoid

- You start new code on @hackbuild/ai-elements. It is deprecated; install @hackbuild/ai-views and import `define` from `@hackbuild/ai-views/elements`.
- You look for the 0.1 model picker, download bar, status pills or chat panel. They are gone; use `<model-select>`, `<chat-pane>` and `<chat-composer>` from @hackbuild/ai-views.
- You expect bare tag names from this package's `define()`. Its prefix defaults to `hb`, so you get `<hb-model-select>`; the ai-views `define()` registers bare names by default.
- You leave out the stylesheet. The elements draw with the page's hackbuild-ui stylesheet, so install @virgilvox/hackbuild-ui as the peer and load its CSS.

---

# @hackbuild/ai-env

> Find out what the tab can run, and load runtimes and workers in a way that also works from a file:// page.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/ai-env/

## Purpose

- Probes WebGPU, shader-f16, cross origin isolation, OPFS, Cache Storage, IndexedDB, safe wasm threads, device memory and the Prompt API by calling each API.
- Imports an ES module from a list of URLs, falling back from plain `import()` to a patched Blob URL to a base64 `data:` URL.
- Checks a SHA-256 of fetched module or worker text before it runs, when you give one.
- Starts a worker through a ladder of rungs, module Blob then classic Blob, with an opt in inline rung.
- Rewrites source text and reports each rewrite that matched nothing.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/ai-env
```

No dependencies and no peers. It fetches only the URLs you pass.

## Exports

### @hackbuild/ai-env

```ts
function absolutizeImports(src: string, base: string): string
```

Make relative import specifiers absolute against `base`, so a module imported from a Blob or data: URL can still reach its siblings.

```ts
function base64ToBytes(b64: string): Uint8Array
```

Decodes base64 text to bytes, skipping characters outside the base64 alphabet.

```ts
function bytesToBase64(bytes: Uint8Array): string
```

Base64 of bytes, built in 32 KB steps so no call takes a huge argument list.

```ts
interface Env {
  adapter: { architecture: string; vendor: string } | null;
  cacheStorage: boolean;
  deviceMemoryGB: number | null;
  f16: boolean;
  indexedDB: boolean;
  isolated: boolean;
  maxBufferBytes: number | null;
  notes: string[];
  opfs: boolean;
  promptApi: boolean;
  protocol: Protocol;
  threads: number;
  webgpu: boolean;
}
```

What the tab can do, as measured by `probe`, with one note per missing capability.

```ts
type Importer = (specifier: string) => Promise<unknown>
```

A function that imports a module specifier, such as a dynamic `import()`.

```ts
function importEsm<T = unknown>(urls: string | readonly string[], opts?: ImportEsmOptions): Promise<T>
```

Imports an ES module from the first URL that loads, through plain import, then a patched Blob URL, then a base64 data: URL, checking a SHA-256 when you give one.

```ts
interface ImportEsmOptions extends LoadDeps {
  classicWorkers?: boolean;
  createObjectURL?: (b: Blob) => string;
  fetch?: (input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>;
  importer?: Importer;
  integrity?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
  onAttempt?: (a: { error?: string; ok: boolean; url: string; via: "import" | "blob" | "data" }) => void;
  onMissed?: (missed: { index: number; pattern: string }[], url: string) => void;
  patch?: (src: string, url: string) => string;
  protocol?: string;
  revokeObjectURL?: (u: string) => void;
  rewrites?: readonly Rewrite[];
}
```

Options for `importEsm`: a SHA-256 per URL, source rewrites, the classic worker swap, a free form patch and attempt callbacks.

```ts
class InlineWorker {
  constructor(src: string);
  addEventListener(type: "message" | "error", fn: (ev: { data?: unknown; message?: string }) => void): void;
  postMessage(data: unknown): void;
  removeEventListener(type: "message" | "error", fn: (ev: { data?: unknown; message?: string }) => void): void;
  terminate(): void;
}
```

A worker shaped object that runs the source on the page.

```ts
interface LoadDeps {
  createObjectURL?: (b: Blob) => string;
  fetch?: (input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>;
  importer?: Importer;
  protocol?: string;
  revokeObjectURL?: (u: string) => void;
}
```

The browser functions the loaders call (fetch, import, object URLs, page protocol); tests pass fakes.

```ts
class LoadError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string, attempts: { error: string; url: string; via: string }[]);
  readonly attempts: { error: string; url: string; via: string }[];
}
```

The error importEsm and spawnWorker throw when every URL or rung failed, with one entry per attempt in `attempts`.

```ts
function probe(opts?: ProbeOptions): Promise<Env>
```

Measures what the tab can do: WebGPU and shader-f16, cross origin isolation, OPFS, Cache Storage, IndexedDB, safe wasm threads, device memory and the Prompt API.

```ts
interface ProbeGlobals {
  caches?: unknown;
  crossOriginIsolated?: boolean;
  indexedDB?: unknown;
  LanguageModel?: unknown;
  location?: { protocol?: string };
  navigator?: unknown;
}
```

What the probe reads.

```ts
interface ProbeOptions {
  globals?: ProbeGlobals;
  maxThreads?: number;
  timeoutMs?: number;
}
```

Options for `probe`: the globals to read, the timeout for adapter and OPFS calls, and the thread cap.

```ts
type Protocol = "file" | "http" | "https" | "other"
```

Capability probe.

```ts
function protocolOf(proto: string | undefined): Protocol
```

Maps a `location.protocol` string to "file", "http", "https" or "other".

```ts
type Rewrite = readonly [pattern: RegExp | string, replacement: string]
```

Source text rewriting for runtimes that must run from file://.

```ts
interface RewriteResult {
  missed: { index: number; pattern: string }[];
  text: string;
}
```

The rewritten text and the rewrites that matched nothing.

```ts
function rewriteSource(src: string, rewrites: readonly Rewrite[]): RewriteResult
```

Applies string or RegExp rewrites to source text and reports each one that matched nothing.

```ts
function sha256Text(text: string): Promise<string>
```

Lowercase hex SHA-256 of a string's UTF-8 bytes, through Web Crypto.

```ts
interface Spawned {
  failures: { error: string; rung: WorkerRung }[];
  rung: WorkerRung;
  worker: WorkerLike;
}
```

A started worker, the rung that started it, and the rungs that failed before it.

```ts
interface SpawnOptions {
  base?: string;
  createObjectURL?: (b: Blob) => string;
  fetch?: (input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>;
  name?: string;
  onMissed?: (missed: { index: number; pattern: string }[]) => void;
  prefer?: readonly WorkerRung[];
  prelude?: string;
  readyMs?: number;
  revokeObjectURL?: (u: string) => void;
  rewrites?: readonly Rewrite[];
  Worker?: new (url: string, opts?: { name?: string; type?: "module" | "classic" }) => WorkerLike;
}
```

Options for `spawnWorker`: rung order, rewrites, a prelude, a base URL, the handshake timeout and the Worker constructor.

```ts
function spawnWorker(source: string | { sha256?: string; url: string }, opts?: SpawnOptions): Promise<Spawned>
```

Spawn a worker from source text or a URL to source text, walking the rungs in `prefer` (default module-blob, classic-blob).

```ts
function textToDataUrl(text: string, mime?: string): string
```

Encodes text as a base64 data: URL, JavaScript by default.

```ts
function toClassicWorker(src: string): { count: number; text: string }
```

Turn module workers into classic workers: Chrome refuses module workers from a file:// page.

```ts
interface WorkerLike {
  addEventListener(type: "message" | "error", fn: (ev: { data?: unknown; message?: string }) => void): void;
  postMessage(msg: unknown, transfer?: Transferable[]): void;
  removeEventListener(type: "message" | "error", fn: (ev: { data?: unknown; message?: string }) => void): void;
  terminate(): void;
}
```

The parts of Worker the ladder uses.

```ts
type WorkerRung = "module-blob" | "classic-blob" | "inline"
```

A way to start a worker: a module worker from a Blob, a classic worker from a Blob, or the source run on the page.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { importEsm, probe, spawnWorker } from "@hackbuild/ai-env";

// what this tab can do, measured by calling each API
const env = await probe();
console.log(env.webgpu ? "webgpu" : "wasm", env.threads, "threads", env.protocol);
for (const note of env.notes) console.log(note);

// a runtime from a CDN, patched and imported from a Blob URL when the page is a file
const wllama = await importEsm(["https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@wllama/wllama@3.8.1/esm/index.js"], {
  onAttempt: (a) => console.log(a.via, a.ok ? "ok" : a.error),
});
console.log(Object.keys(wllama as object).length, "exports");

// a worker from source text: a module Blob first, then a classic Blob
const { worker, rung } = await spawnWorker("self.onmessage = (e) => self.postMessage(e.data * 2);");
worker.addEventListener("message", (e) => console.log(rung, "worker says", e.data));
worker.postMessage(21);
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- You import a runtime with a static `import` or a bare `import()` of a CDN URL. Load it with `importEsm(urls)` and pass the module on, so it also works from a file:// page; give a list of URLs to get a CDN fallback in one call.
- You point `importEsm` at a build whose imports use bare specifiers. It rewrites relative imports only, so use a bundled CDN build such as jsDelivr `+esm`.
- You read `navigator.hardwareConcurrency` for wasm threads. Use `env.threads` from `probe()`: it is 1 unless the page is cross origin isolated, then at most `maxThreads` (default 4).
- You assume OPFS and Cache Storage on a file:// page. `probe()` reports both false there without calling them, and `importEsm` swaps module workers for classic ones by default, since Chrome refuses module workers from a file:// page.
- You pass `integrity` or a worker `sha256` on a plain http page that is not localhost. The check needs Web Crypto, which exists only in a secure context, and it throws `no web crypto in this context, so a sha256 cannot be checked`.
- You add `"inline"` to the `spawnWorker` rungs for code you do not trust. The inline rung runs the source on the page with the DOM and storage in reach, and a `{ url }` source runs inline only with a matching `sha256`.

## Errors this package throws

- `could not import <urls>` (every URL failed on every way in; `LoadError.attempts` lists each): read the attempts; check the URL, CORS and that the build has no bare specifiers
- `sha256 <got>, expected <want>` (an attempt) (the fetched text differs from the pinned hash): pin the exact version the hash was taken from, or update the hash
- `no web crypto in this context, so a sha256 cannot be checked` (no `crypto.subtle`): serve the page over https or localhost
- `worker source http <status>` (the worker source URL failed): check the URL
- `worker source sha256 <got>, expected <want>` (the worker source differs from its hash): update the hash or the source
- `no worker rung started: <rung> (<error>); ...` (every rung failed): read each rung's error; add `"inline"` to `prefer` only for code you trust
- `no ready handshake in <ms> ms` (the worker's top level code did not finish in time): raise `readyMs`, or fix the error the worker throws
- `inline runs on the page, so a url source needs a sha256 for it` (`inline` listed for a URL source with no hash): pass `{ url, sha256 }`
- `importScripts is not available in an inline worker` (the source calls `importScripts` on the inline rung): use a Blob rung, or import modules instead

---

# @hackbuild/ai-views

> Put a model picker, a chat, a transcriber, a mask studio or a camera frame on your page, drawn with the hackbuild-ui stylesheet, as custom elements or Vue components.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/ai-views/

## Purpose

- Gives each job (chat, speech to text, vision, detector, masks, image, voice, depth, embed, face swap, landmarks) a model picker whose rows say whether a model fits this machine and why not.
- Keeps the state behind every view in node safe objects: a pick, a jobs rack, a chat thread and list, a transcribe queue.
- Draws the views in light DOM with the page's hackbuild-ui stylesheet and never styles locally.
- Ships every view as a mount function, a custom element and a Vue 3 component, all on one code path.
- Replaces @hackbuild/ai-elements.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/ai-views @virgilvox/hackbuild-ui
```

@virgilvox/hackbuild-ui is a required peer; the page also loads its stylesheet. Vue is an optional peer, needed only for the `/vue` entry.

| subpath | runtime | pin |
|---|---|---|
| `.` | none; node safe state | none |
| `./elements` | @virgilvox/hackbuild-ui (peer) | `>=0.10.0 <0.11.0` |
| `./vue` | vue (optional peer) and @virgilvox/hackbuild-ui | vue `^3.4.0` |

Model runtimes are never imported here. A picker loads only through the loader you pass, such as `weightsLoader(store)` or your own that starts a runtime.

```ts
}
```

One file in a transcribe queue: name, size, status, progress, segments, dropped lines and the error if it failed.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { importEsm } from "@hackbuild/ai-env";
import { ALL_RECORDS, chatThread, useModelPick, weightsLoader } from "@hackbuild/ai-views";
import { mountChatPane, mountComposer, mountModelSelect } from "@hackbuild/ai-views/elements";
import { loadWllama, wllamaUrls, type WllamaModule } from "@hackbuild/chat/wllama";
import { openWeightStore } from "@hackbuild/weights";

// a chat picker over the GGUF rows, files through the weight store; Qwen2.5 0.5B Instruct weights are Apache-2.0
const fetchFiles = weightsLoader(await openWeightStore());
const wllama = await importEsm<WllamaModule>(wllamaUrls().esm); // the runtime is passed in, never bundled
const thread = chatThread({ system: "answer in one line." });
const pick = useModelPick("chat", {
  records: ALL_RECORDS.filter((r) => r.provider === "wllama"), chosen: "qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-gguf",
  loader: async (rec, ctx) => thread.setEngine(await loadWllama({ module: wllama, blobs: [...((await fetchFiles(rec, ctx)) as Map<string, Blob>).values()] })),
});

// the picker, the turns and the composer, drawn with the page's hackbuild-ui stylesheet
mountModelSelect(document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#model")!, pick);
mountChatPane(document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#chat")!, thread);
mountComposer(document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#composer")!, thread);
```

### from the concepts

```ts
import { ModelSelect, ChatPane, Composer } from "@hackbuild/ai-views/vue";
import { chatThread } from "@hackbuild/ai-views";
const thread = chatThread({ engine });
// <ModelSelect job="chat" variant="chip" /> <ChatPane :thread="thread" /> <Composer :thread="thread" />
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- You import a model runtime into a view or expect a picker to start one. A pick loads only through the `loader` you pass to `useModelPick`; with none it throws `no loader for <id>: pass one to useModelPick, such as weightsLoader(store)`. Bring the runtime in with `importEsm` from @hackbuild/ai-env and start it inside your loader.
- You pass `weightsLoader(store)` for a record that loads through its runtime, such as a WebLLM row. It fetches only records with a `source.url` or a repo and files, under `rec.licence`, and throws `<label> loads through its runtime. the page passes a loader for it.` for the rest; write your own loader for those.
- You expect the elements to exist after import. Nothing registers on import; call `define()` once, or `define("hb")` for `<hb-model-select>`, from `@hackbuild/ai-views/elements`.
- You style the views locally or leave the stylesheet out. They draw in light DOM with the page's hackbuild-ui stylesheet, so load that stylesheet and install @virgilvox/hackbuild-ui as the required peer.
- You import `@hackbuild/ai-views/vue` on a page without Vue. Only that entry imports Vue, an optional peer; the main entry is node safe state and `/elements` needs no framework.

## Errors this package throws

- `no loader for <id>: pass one to useModelPick, such as weightsLoader(store)` (a pick has no loader): pass `loader` to `useModelPick`, or set `loader` on `<model-select>`
- `<model> loads through its runtime. the page passes a loader for it.` (`weightsLoader` got a record with no files to fetch (WebLLM, MediaPipe and the like)): pass a loader that starts that runtime
- `this needs a model. pick one in the bar and load it.` (a reply, `NO_ENGINE`) (the thread has no engine): load a model and call `thread.setEngine`, or set `engine` on `<chat-pane>`
- `no speech model loaded. pick one and load it.` (a failed file) (`<transcribe-drop>` has no transcriber): set its transcriber from @hackbuild/transcribe
- `no custom elements in this environment` (`define()` ran without `customElements` or `HTMLElement`): call it on a page, or pass a registry and a base class
- `the image did not load: ...`, `the cut failed: ...`, `segment everything failed: ...` (studio state) (the image or a segment model failed): read the message; check the model loaded

---

# @hackbuild/audio-dsp

> Filter, clean, measure and time speech and music in the tab on a Rust wasm core, and write the WAV, MIDI, subtitle and zip files the results go into.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/audio-dsp/

## Purpose

- Runs DSP kernels in a Rust core built for wasm32 with simd128: dc block, biquads, frame levels, noise floor, spectral subtraction, limiter, resampling, STFT, onsets, tempo, grid fit and LPC formants.
- Gives the same bits in the wasm and native builds, since its math functions are written out in the crate.
- Gates speech from frame levels and plans overlap add segments for models that take fixed length input.
- Writes txt, srt, vtt, json and lrc transcripts, WAV, standard MIDI files and store only zips, and reads WAV, lrc and those zips back.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/audio-dsp
```

No dependencies and no peers. The wasm core ships as `@hackbuild/audio-dsp/audio-dsp.wasm` and, as base64, in the `@hackbuild/audio-dsp/inline` subpath. It runs no model and fetches nothing unless you pass `{ url }`.

## Exports

### @hackbuild/audio-dsp

```ts
type CoreSource = { url: string | URL } | { bytes: ArrayBuffer | Uint8Array } | { base64: string }
```

Where `loadDsp` gets the wasm core: a URL to fetch, the bytes, or the inlined base64.

```ts
function coverage(regions: readonly Region[], a: number, b: number, sampleRate?: number): number
```

Fraction of [a, b) seconds covered by regions given in samples.

```ts
function crc32(b: Uint8Array): number
```

The CRC-32 of the bytes, as zip uses it.

```ts
function decodeWav(bytes: Uint8Array): { channels: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike>[]; sampleRate: number }
```

Parse PCM 8, 16, 24, 32 bit or float 32 WAV into channels.

```ts
class Dsp {
  constructor(x: Exports);
  readonly simd: boolean;
  biquad(x: Float32Array, kind: FilterKind, fc: number, sr: number, q?: number): Float32Array;
  biquadCoef(kind: FilterKind, fc: number, sr: number, q?: number): number[];
  dcBlock(x: Float32Array): Float32Array;
  decimate(x: Float32Array, factor: number, taps?: number, cutoff?: number, sr?: number): Float32Array;
  denoise(x: Float32Array, noise: Float32Array, alpha: number, gFloor: number, w?: number, hop?: number): Float32Array;
  envelopePeak(x: Float32Array, n: number): Float32Array;
  envelopeRms(x: Float32Array, hop: number): Float32Array;
  estimateTempo(env: Float32Array, fps: number): { bpm: number; offset: number };
  fitGrid(times: ArrayLike<number>, weights: ArrayLike<number>): { bpm: number; offset: number; r: number } | null;
  formants(x: Float32Array, sr: number, center: number, winSec?: number, decim?: number, order?: number): Formant[];
  frameCount(n: number, frame: number, hop: number): number;
  frameDb(x: Float32Array, hop?: number, frame?: number): Float32Array;
  limit(x: Float32Array, ceil?: number, sr?: number): Float32Array;
  math(): { atan2(y: number, x: number): number; cos(x: number): number; exp(x: number): number; ln(x: number): number; sin(x: number): number };
  noiseFloor(db: Float32Array, win?: number): number;
  noiseSpectrum(sig: Float32Array, db: Float32Array, floorDb: number, w?: number, frameHop?: number): Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike> | null;
  percentile(x: Float32Array, q: number): number;
  pickOnsets(env: Float32Array, fps: number, minGap?: number, sens?: number, gate?: number): Onset[];
  resample(x: Float32Array, src: number, dst: number, mode?: "sinc" | "linear", zeros?: number): Float32Array;
  resampleLength(n: number, src: number, dst: number): number;
  stftMag(x: Float32Array, w?: number, hop?: number): { bins: number; frames: number; mag: Float32Array };
  synth(seed: number, n: number, sr: number): Float32Array;
  vowel(n: number, sr: number, f0: number, f1: number, f2: number, f3: number): Float32Array;
}
```

The DSP kernels.

```ts
function encodeWav(channels: readonly Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike>[], sampleRate: number, format?: "pcm16" | "float32"): Uint8Array
```

WAV bytes, interleaved.

```ts
function fadeWeight(i: number, len: number, fade: number): number
```

Crossfade weight of sample i in a segment of len samples.

```ts
type FilterKind = "highpass" | "lowpass" | "bandpass"
```

The biquad shapes `Dsp.biquad` builds.

```ts
interface Formant {
  bw: number;
  f: number;
}
```

One resonance: centre frequency and bandwidth, Hz.

```ts
function gate(db: ArrayLike<number>, threshold: number, nSamples: number, o?: GateOptions): Region[]
```

Speech regions from frame levels in dB: open after `on` frames above `threshold`, close after `off` below, then pad, merge and drop short ones.

```ts
interface GateOptions {
  frame?: number;
  hop?: number;
  mergeGap?: number;
  minDur?: number;
  off?: number;
  on?: number;
  pad?: number;
  sampleRate?: number;
}
```

The hysteresis gate over frame levels in dB: speech turns on after 3 frames above the threshold and off after 25 below, regions are padded, merged across short gaps and dropped when short.

```ts
function gateThreshold(noiseDb: number, loudDb: number, marginDb?: number): number
```

Threshold from the floor: floor + margin, at least floor + 2, at most the 95th percentile minus 8.

```ts
function loadDsp(src: CoreSource): Promise<Dsp>
```

Instantiate the core from a URL, bytes, or the inlined base64 (`@hackbuild/audio-dsp/inline`).

```ts
function lrcStamp(sec: number): string
```

mm:ss.xx

```ts
interface MidiNote {
  dur: number;
  m: number;
  t: number;
  v: number;
}
```

One note for `writeMidi`: start and duration in seconds, note number and velocity.

```ts
interface MidiTrack {
  drums?: boolean;
  name: string;
  notes: readonly MidiNote[];
  program?: number;
}
```

One track for `writeMidi`: a name, its notes, a General MIDI program, or drums on channel 10.

```ts
interface OlaSegment {
  len: number;
  start: number;
}
```

Overlap add for models that take fixed length segments (htdemucs): segments of S samples on a stride of S (1 - overlap), a linear crossfade over min(S - stride, S / 4) at each end, weights floored at 1e-4, and a division by the summed weights.

```ts
interface Onset {
  frame: number;
  peak: number;
  strength: number;
}
```

One onset from `Dsp.pickOnsets`: the attack foot frame, the novelty peak frame and its strength.

```ts
class OverlapAdd {
  constructor(total: number, tracks: number, channels: number, fade: number);
  readonly channels: number;
  readonly fade: number;
  readonly out: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike>[][];
  readonly total: number;
  readonly tracks: number;
  add(seg: Segment, data: ArrayLike<number>, stride: number): void;
  finish(): Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike>[][];
}
```

Accumulates weighted segment outputs into `tracks` by `channels` buffers of `total` samples.

```ts
function parseLrc(text: string): Segment[]
```

Lines of an lrc file; a line's end is the next start, or start plus 0.07 s per character (at least 1.5 s).

```ts
function planSegments(total: number, size: number, overlap: number): { fade: number; segments: Segment[]; stride: number }
```

Segment starts and lengths over `total` samples for a model that takes `size` samples, with the stride and fade that `overlap` (0 to 0.6) gives.

```ts
type Region = [start: number, end: number]
```

A speech region in samples, end exclusive.

```ts
interface Segment {
  end: number;
  start: number;
  text: string;
}
```

File writers: txt, srt, vtt and json transcripts in fixed layouts (byte for byte), lrc, 16 bit and float WAV, standard MIDI files (format 1, 480 ticks per quarter, drums on channel 10), and a store only zip.

```ts
function spreadWords(text: string, start: number, end: number): Segment[]
```

Word timing spread across a line by character count.

```ts
function timestamp(t: number, comma: boolean): string
```

hh:mm:ss,mmm (srt) or hh:mm:ss.mmm (vtt); milliseconds rounded, capped at 999.

```ts
function toJson(t: TranscriptJson): string
```

The json export: times to 3 decimals, two space indent.

```ts
function toLrc(lines: readonly Segment[], title?: string): string
```

Lrc lyrics: an optional `[ti:]` title line, then one `[mm:ss.xx]` line per segment start.

```ts
function toSrt(segs: readonly Segment[]): string
```

SubRip text: numbered cues with comma millisecond stamps.

```ts
function toTxt(segs: readonly Segment[]): string
```

Plain text; a gap over 2 s starts a paragraph.

```ts
function toVtt(segs: readonly Segment[]): string
```

WebVTT text: a WEBVTT header, dot millisecond stamps, and `&` and `<` escaped in cue text.

```ts
interface TranscriptJson {
  dropped?: readonly { start: number; text: string; why: string }[];
  duration: number;
  language: string;
  model: string;
  segments: readonly Segment[];
  source: string;
  stats?: Record<string, unknown> | null;
}
```

The fields `toJson` writes: source, duration, model, language, stats, segments and dropped lines.

```ts
function unzipStore(zip: Uint8Array): { data: Uint8Array; name: string }[]
```

Reads a store only zip, as `zipStore` writes it, back into entries.

```ts
function writeMidi(tracks: readonly MidiTrack[], bpm: number): Uint8Array
```

A format 1 file: a tempo track (tempo, 4/4) then one track per input.

```ts
function zipStore(entries: readonly { data: string | Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>; name: string }[], date?: Date): Uint8Array
```

A store only zip (no compression), UTF-8 names.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { encodeWav, gate, gateThreshold, loadDsp, toSrt } from "@hackbuild/audio-dsp";
import { AUDIO_DSP_WASM_BASE64 } from "@hackbuild/audio-dsp/inline";

// the wasm core, inlined; { url } or { bytes } load it from elsewhere
const dsp = await loadDsp({ base64: AUDIO_DSP_WASM_BASE64 });
const pcm = new Float32Array(16000 * 10); // 10 s of 16 kHz mono

// clean the wire: dc block, 80 Hz high pass, denoise from a noise print, limit
const clean = dsp.biquad(dsp.dcBlock(pcm), "highpass", 80, 16000);
const db = dsp.frameDb(clean); // 25 ms frames on a 10 ms hop
const floor = dsp.noiseFloor(db);
const noise = dsp.noiseSpectrum(clean, db, floor);
const safe = dsp.limit(noise ? dsp.denoise(clean, noise, 1.8, 0.08) : clean, 0.891, 16000);

// speech regions 6 dB over the floor, then a WAV and an srt of them
const regions = gate(db, gateThreshold(floor, dsp.percentile(db, 0.95)), safe.length);
const wav = encodeWav([safe], 16000);
console.log(wav.length, "bytes", toSrt(regions.map(([a, b]) => ({ start: a / 16000, end: b / 16000, text: "speech" }))));
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- You fetch the wasm by a relative URL and the page breaks on file://. Pass `{ base64: AUDIO_DSP_WASM_BASE64 }` from `@hackbuild/audio-dsp/inline` to `loadDsp`; use `{ url }` or `{ bytes }` only when you host the file yourself, and a failed fetch throws `audio-dsp wasm: http <status> for <url>`.
- You call the kernels before `loadDsp` resolves, or expect them on the module. Await `loadDsp(src)` once and call every kernel on the `Dsp` it returns; each call copies its input into wasm memory and hands back a new `Float32Array`.
- You expect a scalar fallback on an old browser. The core needs WebAssembly with simd128 and there is no build without it, so feature check and tell the person the browser is too old.
- You read `gate` regions as seconds. They come back in samples, end exclusive; divide by the sample rate before you pass them to `toSrt` or `toVtt`, which take seconds.
- You pass `stftMag` a window that is not a power of two, or `frameDb` a fractional hop. Both throw a RangeError naming the bad value; use whole numbers, and a power of two for the window.

## Errors this package throws

- `audio-dsp wasm: http <status> for <url>` (`loadDsp({ url })` got a failed response): check the URL, or load `{ base64 }` from the inline subpath
- `frameDb: hop <h> and frame <f> must be integers of at least 1` (RangeError) (bad frame settings): pass whole numbers of 1 or more
- `stftMag: window <w> must be a power of two` (RangeError) (window not a power of two): use 512, 1024 or 2048
- `stftMag: hop <h> must be an integer of at least 1` (RangeError) (bad hop): pass a whole number of 1 or more
- `not a wav file: no RIFF WAVE header` (`decodeWav` got another format): decode it with @hackbuild/media instead
- `wav data before fmt chunk` / `wav: no data chunk` (a damaged WAV): write it again
- `wav: <bits> bit format <fmt> is not supported` (a WAV layout `decodeWav` does not read): convert to 16 bit PCM or 32 bit float
- `not a zip file: no end of central directory` (`unzipStore` got another file): pass a zip from `zipStore`
- `zip directory entry <i> is damaged` / `zip entry <name> fails its crc32 check` (a damaged zip): write it again
- `zip entry <name> is compressed; only store only zips are read` (a deflated zip): read it with a zip library

---

# @hackbuild/biosignal

> Filter EEG, train a Riemannian classifier on it and cross validate it without leaks, in a Rust wasm core that runs in your tab.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/biosignal/

## Purpose

- Band passes each channel with zero phase biquads, with an optional mains notch and its harmonic.
- Turns each window into one shrunk covariance per frequency band.
- Trains a tangent space classifier on those covariances and gives class probabilities per window.
- Cross validates with folds that hold whole trials, so windows from one trial never sit on both sides.
- Exports the trained model as plain JSON and loads it back.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/biosignal
```

No dependencies and no peers. The wasm core ships in the package as `wasm/biosignal.wasm` and as base64 in the `@hackbuild/biosignal/inline` subpath.

## Exports

### @hackbuild/biosignal

```ts
interface Band {
  hi: number;
  lo: number;
}
```

A frequency band in Hz; each band gets its own band pass and covariance.

```ts
class Biosignal {
  constructor(x: Exports);
  readonly simd: boolean;
  bandpass(x: Float32Array, fs: number, lo: number, hi: number, notch?: number): Float32Array;
  covariance(data: Float32Array, channels: number, samples: number, shrink?: number): Float64Array;
  crossValidate(epochs: readonly Epoch[], bands: readonly Band[], fs: number, o: TrainOptions & { byTrial?: boolean; folds?: number; seed?: number }, shrink?: number, notch?: number): number[];
  distance(a: Float64Array, b: Float64Array, n: number): number;
  features(epochs: readonly Epoch[], bands: readonly Band[], fs: number, shrink?: number, notch?: number): Float64Array;
  load(m: ModelJson): Classifier;
  synth(seed: number, c: number, t: number, fs: number, hz: number, trials: number, per: number): Epoch[];
  tangent(c: Float64Array, invSqrtRef: Float64Array, n: number): Float64Array;
  train(epochs: readonly Epoch[], bands: readonly Band[], fs: number, o: TrainOptions, shrink?: number, notch?: number): Classifier;
}
```

The loaded wasm core: filtering, covariances, Riemannian distance, training, cross validation and model reload.

```ts
class Classifier {
  constructor(bs: Biosignal, x: Exports, h: number, bands: readonly Band[], fs: number, shrink: number, notch: number, channels: number);
  readonly bands: readonly Band[];
  readonly channels: number;
  readonly fs: number;
  readonly notch: number;
  readonly shrink: number;
  dispose(): void;
  predict(e: Epoch): number;
  proba(e: Epoch): number[];
  toJSON(): ModelJson;
}
```

A trained tangent space classifier: class probabilities and the predicted class for one epoch, JSON export, and `dispose` to free it in the core.

```ts
type CoreSource = { url: string | URL } | { bytes: ArrayBuffer | Uint8Array } | { base64: string }
```

Where loadBiosignal gets the wasm core: a URL, the bytes, or base64 text such as `BIOSIGNAL_WASM_BASE64`.

```ts
interface EegNetRunner {
  export?(): Promise<Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>>;
  fit(epochs: readonly Epoch[], classes: number): Promise<void>;
  proba(epoch: Epoch): Promise<number[]>;
}
```

Where a neural model (such as EEGNet on tfjs) plugs in.

```ts
interface Epoch {
  channels: number;
  data: Float32Array;
  label: number;
  samples: number;
  trial: number;
}
```

A window: c channels by t samples, row major.

```ts
function epochsFromEvents(data: readonly Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike>[], events: readonly { at: number; label: number }[], samples: number, per?: number, step?: number): Epoch[]
```

Cut windows of `samples` from continuous [c][n] data at event sample indices; one trial per event, `per` windows stepping by `step`.

```ts
function loadBiosignal(src: CoreSource): Promise<Biosignal>
```

Instantiate the biosignal wasm core from a URL, bytes or base64 and return a Biosignal.

```ts
interface ModelJson {
  bands: Band[];
  fs: number;
  kind: "hackbuild-biosignal-riemann";
  notch: number;
  shrink: number;
  values: number[];
  version: 1;
}
```

The exported model: plain JSON, loadable with `Biosignal.load`.

```ts
interface TrainOptions {
  classes: number;
  epochs?: number;
  l2?: number;
  lr?: number;
}
```

Classifier settings: the class count, and L2 weight (0.05), training epochs (150) and learning rate (0.14) by default.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { epochsFromEvents, loadBiosignal } from "@hackbuild/biosignal";
import { BIOSIGNAL_WASM_BASE64 } from "@hackbuild/biosignal/inline";

// the wasm core, inlined so nothing is fetched
const bs = await loadBiosignal({ base64: BIOSIGNAL_WASM_BASE64 });
const input = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("input[type=file]")!;
input.onchange = async () => {
  // a CSV at 256 Hz: one row per sample, one column per channel, then a label where a trial starts
  const rows = (await input.files![0]!.text()).trim().split("\n").map((l) => l.trim().split(","));
  const n = rows[0]!.length - 1;
  const channels = Array.from({ length: n }, (_, c) => Float32Array.from(rows, (r) => Number(r[c])));
  const events = rows.flatMap((r, at) => (r[n] ? [{ at, label: Number(r[n]) }] : []));
  const epochs = epochsFromEvents(channels, events, 256, 4, 64); // 4 windows of 1 s per trial
  // alpha and beta bands; folds hold whole trials, so no window leaks across
  const bands = [{ lo: 8, hi: 12 }, { lo: 13, hi: 30 }];
  console.log("accuracy per fold", bs.crossValidate(epochs, bands, 256, { classes: 2 }));
  // train on everything, then save the model as JSON (reload with bs.load)
  const model = bs.train(epochs, bands, 256, { classes: 2 });
  console.log(model.predict(epochs[0]!), JSON.stringify(model.toJSON()).length, "bytes of json");
};
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- You fetch `biosignal.wasm` by URL from a page opened on file://, and the fetch fails. Pass `{ base64: BIOSIGNAL_WASM_BASE64 }` from `@hackbuild/biosignal/inline` to `loadBiosignal`, which fetches nothing.
- You cut windows yourself and give every window its own trial. Build epochs with `epochsFromEvents`, which marks each event's windows with one `trial`, so `crossValidate` keeps whole trials on one side of a fold; `byTrial: false` gives the leaky number.
- You call `train` or `crossValidate` without `classes`, or with labels outside it. `classes` is required and every label must be 0 to `classes - 1`, or it throws a `RangeError` such as "label 2 is outside 0 to 1".
- You reload a saved model with `JSON.parse` alone. Pass the parsed object to `bs.load`, which checks its kind, version and header and throws "not a hackbuild biosignal model, or a newer version" otherwise.
- You call `predict` after `dispose`. The classifier lives in the wasm core and throws "model was dropped" once freed; dispose it only when you are done with it.

## Errors this package throws

- `train: no epochs` (or `crossValidate: ...`) (the epoch list is empty): check that your events fall inside the data; windows past the end are skipped
- `train: no bands` (the band list is empty): pass at least one `{ lo, hi }`
- `train: every epoch needs N channels and channels times samples values` (epochs differ in channel count, or `data` has the wrong length): cut every epoch from the same channels, `data.length` equal to channels times samples
- `train: label L is outside 0 to K` (a label is not below `classes`): number classes from 0 and set `classes` to their count
- `not a hackbuild biosignal model, or a newer version` (`load` got other JSON): pass the object from `toJSON()`
- `model values do not match their header` (the model JSON was cut or edited): export it again
- `model was dropped` (`proba` after `dispose()`): load the model again
- `biosignal wasm: http 404 for ...` (the wasm URL did not load): serve `wasm/biosignal.wasm`, or pass `{ base64: BIOSIGNAL_WASM_BASE64 }`

---

# @hackbuild/character

> Read, upgrade, check and write character cards in the tab, as JSON, PNG or CHARX, with a profile that names a character's body, voice and actions.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/character/

## Purpose

- Reads Character Card V1, V2 and V3 from JSON, from PNG text chunks and from CHARX archives, detecting the format from the bytes.
- Upgrades any card to V3, downgrades to V2, and lists every problem with a card by path.
- Writes cards into PNG text chunks and CHARX archives, with the same bytes for the same input.
- Keeps a versioned profile extension for avatar, voice, action vocabulary, behaviour, memory and an optional lock, and migrates old ones.
- Fills `{{char}}` and `{{user}}` macros and picks the lorebook entries a passage of chat activates.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/character
```

No dependencies and no peers. The card work runs in a Rust core compiled to wasm32; the `@hackbuild/character/inline` subpath carries it as base64, and `@hackbuild/character/character.wasm` is the file for a URL load. No character content, avatar or voice reference ships here.

## Exports

### @hackbuild/character

```ts
function activeLore(book: CharacterBook | undefined, text: string, o?: LoreOptions): LoreEntry[]
```

Entries a passage of recent chat activates: enabled entries that are constant or whose keys appear (substring, or regex when use_regex), and for selective entries also a secondary key.

```ts
type AvatarKind = "vrm" | "glb" | "fbx" | "mmd" | "live2d"
```

The avatar file kinds a profile can name: vrm, glb, fbx, mmd or live2d.

```ts
type Card = CardV2 | CardV3
```

A V2 or V3 card.

```ts
interface CardAsset {
  ext: string;
  name: string;
  type: string;
  uri: string;
}
```

One entry of a V3 card's `assets` list: its type, where it lives, a name and a file extension.

```ts
interface CardDataV2 {
  alternate_greetings: string[];
  character_book?: CharacterBook;
  character_version: string;

  tags: string[];
}
```

The `data` object of a V2 card: name, persona text, greetings, lorebook, tags and extensions.

```ts
interface CardDataV3 extends CardDataV2 {
  alternate_greetings: string[];
  assets?: CardAsset[];
  character_book?: CharacterBook;
  character_version: string;
  creation_date?: number;
  creator: string;
  creator_notes: string;
  creator_notes_multilingual?: Record<string, string>;
  description: string;
  extensions: Record<string, unknown> & { hackbuild?: Profile };
  first_mes: string;
  group_only_greetings: string[];

  modification_date?: number;

  nickname?: string;

  system_prompt: string;
  tags: string[];
}
```

The `data` object of a V3 card: the V2 fields plus group greetings, assets, nickname, sources and dates.

```ts
type CardInput = Card | Record<string, unknown> | Uint8Array
```

A card as an object, or card bytes (PNG, CHARX or JSON).

```ts
interface CardV2 {
  data: CardDataV2;
  spec: "chara_card_v2";
  spec_version: "2.0";
}
```

A Character Card V2, `spec` set to `chara_card_v2`.

```ts
interface CardV3 {
  data: CardDataV3;
  spec: "chara_card_v3";
  spec_version: "3.0";
}
```

A Character Card V3, `spec` set to `chara_card_v3` and `spec_version` 3.0.

```ts
interface CharacterBook {
  description?: string;
  entries: LoreEntry[];
  extensions: Record<string, unknown>;
  name?: string;
  recursive_scanning?: boolean;
  scan_depth?: number;
  token_budget?: number;
}
```

A lorebook: its entries plus optional scan depth, token budget and recursion settings.

```ts
class CharacterCore {
  constructor(x: Exports);
  readonly profileVersion: number;
  blankPng(w: number, h: number, rgb?: number): Uint8Array;
  downgrade(card: CardInput): Card & { spec: "chara_card_v2" };
  entry(charx: Uint8Array, path: string): Uint8Array;
  migrate(card: CardInput, o?: { create?: boolean }): { card: Card; notes: string[] };
  migrateProfile(profile: unknown): { notes: string[]; profile: Profile };
  raw(op: RawOp, a: Uint8Array, b?: Uint8Array, n?: number): { code: number; out: Uint8Array };
  read(bytes: Uint8Array): ReadResult;
  upgrade(card: CardInput): Card & { spec: "chara_card_v3" };
  validate(card: CardInput): string[];
  writeCharx(card: CardInput, assets?: readonly CharxAsset[], o?: { refs?: boolean }): Uint8Array;
  writePng(card: CardInput, o?: { image?: Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>; mode?: "both" | "v3" | "v2" }): Uint8Array;
}
```

The card operations.

```ts
class CharacterError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string);
}
```

The error every failed core call and a failed wasm fetch throw, carrying the core's message.

```ts
interface CharxAsset {
  bytes: Uint8Array;
  path: string;
}
```

A file to put in a CHARX archive: its path inside the archive and its bytes.

```ts
type CoreSource = { url: string | URL } | { bytes: ArrayBuffer | Uint8Array } | { base64: string }
```

Where `loadCharacterCore` gets the wasm: a URL to fetch, bytes, or a base64 string such as `CHARACTER_WASM_BASE64`.

```ts
function fillMacros(text: string, names: { char: string; user: string }): string
```

Replace {{char}} and {{user}} (any case) and the older <BOT> and <USER>.

```ts
function loadCharacterCore(src: CoreSource): Promise<CharacterCore>
```

```ts
  iterations: number;
  salt: string;
}
```

```ts
interface LoreEntry {
  case_sensitive?: boolean;
```

```ts
interface Profile {
  actions: { aliases: Record<string, string>; gestures: string[]; moods: string[]; postures: string[] };
  avatar: { asset: string; expressions: Record<string, string>; kind: AvatarKind; uri: string; wardrobe: Record<string, boolean> };
  behavior: { ambientGestures: boolean; blink: boolean; breath: boolean; gaze: boolean; idle: boolean };
  lock?: Lock;
  memory: { enabled: boolean };
  version: number;
  voice: { cloneRef: string; engine: string; pitch: number; rate: number; voiceId: string };
}
```

```ts

```
