```ts
type RawOp = "read" | "entry" | "upgrade" | "downgrade" | "validate" | "migrate" | "migrate_profile" | "write_png" | "write_charx"
```

Names of the raw operations, as the parity fixture spells them.

```ts
interface ReadResult {
  assets: { name: string; size: number }[];
  card: Record<string, unknown>;
  format: "png" | "charx" | "json";
  source: string;
  spec: "chara_card_v2" | "chara_card_v3" | "v1" | "unknown";
}
```

What `CharacterCore.read` returns: the detected format, where the card came from, its spec, the card as stored and the CHARX files beside it.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { activeLore, fillMacros, loadCharacterCore, profileOf } from "@hackbuild/character";
import { CHARACTER_WASM_BASE64 } from "@hackbuild/character/inline";

// load the wasm core from the inlined base64 (or pass { url } or { bytes })
const core = await loadCharacterCore({ base64: CHARACTER_WASM_BASE64 });

// read a card the user picks: PNG, CHARX or JSON, detected from the bytes
const input = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("input[type=file]")!;
input.onchange = async () => {
  const read = core.read(new Uint8Array(await input.files![0]!.arrayBuffer()));
  // any version to V3, then add or update the profile extension
  const { card, notes } = core.migrate(core.upgrade(read.card), { create: true });
  console.log(read.format, read.spec, notes, core.validate(card), profileOf(card)?.voice.engine);
  // fill the greeting and pick the lorebook entries the last turns activate
  console.log(fillMacros(card.data.first_mes, { char: card.data.name, user: "Sam" }));
  console.log(activeLore(card.data.character_book, "the last few turns of chat", { budgetChars: 1200 }));
  // write it back as a PNG with both card chunks
  console.log(core.writePng(card).length, "bytes");
};
```

### from the concepts

```ts
{ version: 1,
  avatar:   { uri, asset, kind: "vrm" | "glb" | "fbx" | "mmd" | "live2d", expressions: { mood: name }, wardrobe: { part: shown } },
  voice:    { engine, voiceId, rate (0.25 to 4), pitch (0 to 2), cloneRef },
  actions:  { moods: [], gestures: [], postures: [], aliases: { word: name } },
  behavior: { gaze, blink, breath, idle, ambientGestures },
  memory:   { enabled },
  lock?:    { algo: "pbkdf2-sha256", iterations, salt, hash } }
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- You call card methods on the module itself. Await `loadCharacterCore` once and call `read`, `upgrade`, `migrate`, `validate` and `writePng` on the `CharacterCore` it returns; every method is synchronous after that.
- You fetch `character.wasm` by a relative URL from a file:// page and the fetch fails. Import `CHARACTER_WASM_BASE64` from `@hackbuild/character/inline` and pass `{ base64: CHARACTER_WASM_BASE64 }`, or pass `{ bytes }` you already hold.
- You pass a `File` or `Blob` to `core.read`. Pass a `Uint8Array` of the file's bytes, for example `new Uint8Array(await file.arrayBuffer())`; the format is detected from the bytes.
- You read `profileOf(card)` on a card straight from `read` and get null. Run `core.migrate(core.upgrade(read.card), { create: true })` to get a V3 card with the profile extension added.
- You treat a bad card as a quiet failure. Every failed core call throws a `CharacterError` with the core's message, so wrap `read` and the writers in try and catch, and use `validate` to list problems by path without throwing.

## Errors this package throws

- `character wasm: http <status> for <url>` (the wasm URL did not load): check the URL, or load `{ base64: CHARACTER_WASM_BASE64 }`
- `png: no png signature` (the bytes are not a PNG): pass the card file itself
- `png: no chara or ccv3 text chunk` (a PNG with no card in it): the image carries no card; ask for a card PNG
- `png: crc mismatch in <chunk>` (a damaged PNG): get the file again
- `charx: no card.json` (a ZIP that is not a CHARX): pass a CHARX archive
- `zip: zip64 archives are not read` (a Zip64 archive): write the archive without Zip64
- `zip: encrypted entries are not read` (an encrypted entry): decrypt the archive first
- `zip: compression method <m> is not read` (an entry that is neither stored nor deflate): repack with stored or deflate
- `inflate: output over the size cap` (an entry over 512 MB): split the asset or keep it outside the archive
- `charx: unsafe or reserved path <p>` (an asset path with `..`, a leading slash or a backslash): use a relative path such as `assets/avatar/body.vrm`
- `charx: no entry <name>` (`entry` asked for a file the archive lacks): list `read(...).assets` first
- `card: unknown spec <spec>` (the JSON is no V1, V2 or V3 card): check the file is a character card
- `card: migrate needs a v2 or v3 card; upgrade it first` (`migrate` on a V1 card): call `upgrade` first
- `json: <problem> at byte <n>` (the card JSON does not parse): fix the JSON at that byte

---

# @hackbuild/chat

> Stream chat replies from WebLLM, wllama, transformers.js, the Chrome Prompt API or a remote endpoint through one interface.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/chat/

## Purpose

- Gives every runtime the same `stream`, `complete`, `prewarm` and `dispose` calls, with the runtime module passed in.
- Normalizes roles for templates with no system role, and splits think blocks and leaked control markers out of visible text as the stream arrives.
- Cuts stop strings on the client for every runtime, also across chunk edges.
- Asks for JSON by schema in each runtime's own form, and falls back to the schema as prompt text when the runtime refuses it.
- Reports time to first token and tokens per second for every reply.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/chat @hackbuild/ai-env @hackbuild/models @hackbuild/weights
```

It depends on `@hackbuild/converse`. The quick start also uses `@hackbuild/ai-env`, `@hackbuild/models` and `@hackbuild/weights`. Each runtime is an optional peer behind its own subpath, and no file imports a runtime: you pass the module in, so a page that uses only the remote engine never loads WebLLM. Install only the peer for the subpath you use.

| subpath | runtime | pin |
|---|---|---|
| `@hackbuild/chat/webllm` | `@mlc-ai/web-llm` (optional peer) | 0.2.84 |
| `@hackbuild/chat/wllama` | `@wllama/wllama` (optional peer) | 4.0.0, fallback 3.8.1 |
| `@hackbuild/chat/transformers` | `@huggingface/transformers` (optional peer) | 4.3.2 |
| `@hackbuild/chat/prompt-api` | Chrome `LanguageModel` | Chrome 148 |
| `@hackbuild/chat/remote` | fetch only | none |

```ts
interface ChatEngine {
```

A chat engine over one runtime, with the same stream, complete, prewarm and dispose calls for every runtime.

Options for `transformersDriver`: the module's streamer and stopping classes, a built pipeline, an id and the system role quirk.

```ts
interface TransformersModule {
  InterruptableStoppingCriteria: new () => { interrupt(): void; reset?(): void };
  TextStreamer: new (tokenizer: unknown, opts: { callback_function?: (t: string) => void; skip_prompt?: boolean; skip_special_tokens?: boolean }) => unknown;
  pipeline(task: "text-generation", model: string, opts?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<TextGenerationLike>;
}
```

### @hackbuild/chat/wllama

Options for `wllamaDriver`: a loaded Wllama, an id and whether to keep the KV prefix between calls.

```ts

```

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { importEsm } from "@hackbuild/ai-env";
import type { ChatMessage } from "@hackbuild/chat";
import { loadWllama, wllamaUrls, type WllamaModule } from "@hackbuild/chat/wllama";
import { CATALOG, pinnedBase } from "@hackbuild/models";
import { openWeightStore } from "@hackbuild/weights";

// Qwen2.5 0.5B Instruct q4_k_m GGUF; the record names the weight licence, the store caches the file
const rec = CATALOG.find((r) => r.id === "qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-gguf")!;
const url = pinnedBase(rec.source.repo!) + rec.source.file!;
const gguf = await (await openWeightStore()).get({ url, licence: rec.licence });

// the runtime is passed in, never bundled
const chat = await loadWllama({ module: await importEsm<WllamaModule>(wllamaUrls().esm), blobs: [gguf] });

// stream a reply; visible text never holds think blocks or control markers
const messages: ChatMessage[] = [{ role: "system", content: "answer in one line." }, { role: "user", content: "what should I pack for rain?" }];
for await (const ev of chat.stream(messages, { maxTokens: 120 })) {
  if (ev.type === "text") console.log(ev.text);
  if (ev.type === "done") console.log(ev.result.stats.tokensPerSecond, "tokens per second");
}
```

### from the concepts

```ts
hub.provide("wllama", async ({ record }) => loadWllama({ module, blobs: [await store.get(refFor(record))] }));
const chat = await hub.use("chat", { size: "small" });
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- You never import `@mlc-ai/web-llm`, `@wllama/wllama` or `@huggingface/transformers` statically. Pass the imported module as `module` to `loadWebLLM`, `loadWllama` or `loadTransformers`; for wllama use `await importEsm(wllamaUrls().esm)` from `@hackbuild/ai-env`, which also works from file://.
- `loadWllama` takes GGUF files as `blobs`, never a URL. Get each Blob with `store.get({ url, licence })` from `@hackbuild/weights`, take the licence from the model record (`rec.licence`), and pass split GGUF files in order.
- Text events never hold think blocks or control markers. Read reasoning from `think` events, or pass `think: "drop"`; do not strip tags from `text` yourself.
- A schema refusal does not throw. The engine tries `fallbackSchemas`, then turns schemas off for that engine and puts the schema in the prompt; check `result.schemaFallback` and parse the text yourself when it is true.
- `anthropicMessages` needs `model` and sends no temperature, top_p or top_k. `openaiCompatible` takes the base URL up to `/v1`, and sends `repeat_penalty` only with `llamaParams: true`.
- "webllm runtime and model library do not match" means the WebLLM module and the model library disagree. Pin `@mlc-ai/web-llm` to 0.2.84 and call `dispose()` on an engine before you load the next one.

## Errors this package throws

- `webllm runtime and model library do not match (...). pin @mlc-ai/web-llm to the version the model was built for.` (a LinkError, TVMFFI or instantiate failure): pin `@mlc-ai/web-llm` to 0.2.84 or the version the model library was built for
- `webllm could not load <model>: ...` (every rung of the context ladder failed): read the per context errors in the message; try a smaller `contextWindow` or another model
- `the model did not load: ...` (wllama loaded no model; the last native error is named): check the GGUF blobs are whole and in order, and lower `nCtx`
- `no LanguageModel in this browser. the built in model needs chrome 148 or later.` (no Prompt API): use Chrome 148 or later, or another engine
- `the built in model is unavailable on this device.` (`availability()` said unavailable): use another engine
- `could not reach <host>: ...` (fetch failed: network, CORS or a stopped server): start the server, allow the page's origin, check the base URL
- `http <status> from <host>: ...` (the endpoint answered with an error; `ChatError.status` holds the code): read the body text in the message; a schema 400 falls back on its own
- `response has no body to stream` (the endpoint sent no stream body): check the endpoint streams chat completions
- `request aborted` (the signal aborted the request): none; the reply ends with finish `abort`
- `stream error` (the stream carried an error event with no message): retry; check the server log
- `schema fallback did not settle` (the runtime kept refusing after the free text fallback): report it; send without `schema`

---

# @hackbuild/converse

> Run a conversation over a streaming chat engine with the history rules small models need, and save it as a versioned chat session.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/converse/

## Purpose

- Runs one turn loop over any streaming engine: send, stop, redo, edit, remove, speak again, restore and clear, with state changes as events.
- Keeps the history rules small models need: wordless and failed replies out, the greeting never sent, the raw tagged reply sent back, a message cap.
- Keeps memory and camera lines on the user turn they were recalled for, with a system text that stays byte equal across turns.
- Drives an optional director and speaker, and replays recorded cues when a reply is spoken again.
- Reads and writes the versioned `.hbchat.json` session schema and saves it through a debounced store.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/converse @hackbuild/chat
```

It depends on `@hackbuild/memory`, which installs with it. No peers. The engine, director and speaker are taken by shape, so it imports none of `@hackbuild/chat`, `@hackbuild/act` or `@hackbuild/speak`; install the ones you use. The quick start uses the scripted engine of `@hackbuild/chat`.

## Exports

### @hackbuild/converse

```ts
function buildMessages(s: Pick<ChatSession, "system" | "messages">, o?: HistoryOptions): ChatMessage[]
```

The messages to send: failed, empty and wordless replies out, a leading assistant greeting out, the raw tagged reply in place of the visible one, the cap applied at a user turn, then the notes and lines.

```ts
interface ChatMessage {
  content: string;

```


A saved chat in the `.hbchat.json` shape: id, title, times, model, system text, settings and messages.

A debounced saver of one session; it drops saves until `markRestored()` is called.

```ts
interface ConverseEngine {
```

The engine a conversation streams from: a `stream` of events per request, and an optional `prewarm` that fills the prefix cache.

```ts
type ConverseEvent = { session: ChatSession; type: "change" } | { id: string; text: string; type: "text" } | { id: string; text: string; type: "think" } | { message: SessionMessage; type: "done" } | { error: unknown; message: SessionMessage; type: "error" } | { busy: boolean; type: "busy" }
```

What a conversation emits: the session changed, reply text or think text arrived, a reply finished or failed, or busy flipped.

```ts

  debounceMs?: number;

}
```

What a conversation needs: the engine and a clock, and optionally the system text, greeting, history cap, director, speaker, memory, camera line and sink.

```ts
interface RecordedCue {
```

```ts
const SEEN_NOTE: "Lines that start with [seen] under a user message say what the camera showed when the person wrote it. Use them when they fit."
```

```ts
const SEEN_TAG: "[seen]"
```

```ts
class SessionError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string);
}
```

The error a session read throws, with a lowercase reason such as `not a chat session: no messages list`.

```ts
interface SessionMessage {
  at?: number;
  content: string;
  cues?: unknown;
  edited?: boolean;
  error?: string;
  id: string;
  raw?: string;
  recalled?: { id: string; text: string }[];

  seen?: string;

  think?: string;
  toolCalls?: ToolCall[];
}
```

One stored message: visible text, the raw reply, think text, error, stats, seen and recalled lines, cues and tool calls.

```ts
function sessionMessages(s: ChatSession): ChatMessage[]
```

The messages to send an engine: the system text first, raw replies in place of their stripped text, and failed or empty replies left out.

```ts
function sessionToMarkdown(s: ChatSession): string
```

The session as markdown: a title line, then one section per message.

```ts
interface SpeakerLike {
  feed(textSoFar: string, final?: boolean): unknown;

}
```

The part of an `@hackbuild/speak` Speaker the turn loop drives.

```ts
interface Timers {
  clearTimeout(h: unknown): void;
  setTimeout(fn: () => void, ms: number): unknown;
}
```

The timer pair the store debounces with; pass your own in tests.

```ts
interface ToolCall {
  arguments: string;
  id?: string;
  name: string;
}
```

One tool call a model asked for: the tool name and its arguments as a JSON string.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { scripted } from "@hackbuild/chat";
import { createConversation, exportSession } from "@hackbuild/converse";

// any ChatEngine from @hackbuild/chat fits; the scripted one runs no model
const engine = scripted({ replies: ["[wave] hi, ready for a walk"] });

// one conversation with a system text and a greeting that is never sent
const conv = createConversation({ engine, now: () => Date.now(), system: "you are a dog", greeting: "woof. what are we doing" });

// stream the reply text as it arrives
conv.on((e) => {
  if (e.type === "text") console.log("so far:", e.text);
});

// send a turn, then look at the next request and the saved session
const reply = await conv.send("walk time");
console.log("reply:", reply?.content, "next request:", conv.request().length, "messages");
console.log(exportSession(conv.session));
```

### from the concepts

```ts
// new Speaker({ ..., onProgress: (p) => conv.reached(p.offset) })
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- This package imports no runtime and no engine. Pass any `ChatEngine` from `@hackbuild/chat` as `engine`, or `scripted()` from there when you want no model; never import a runtime here.
- `now` is required. Pass a clock such as `() => Date.now()`, or a fake clock in tests.
- With a `sink`, call `await conv.restore()` before the first `send`. Nothing is saved until `restore()` resolves, so a page that skips it never writes its session.
- `send` stops the reply that is still streaming before it adds the new turn, and resolves with `null` when the reply was empty or aborted before a word. Check for `null` instead of reading `reply.content`.
- The `greeting` is shown first and never sent to the engine. Put instructions in `system`, and read what the next reply would send with `conv.request()`.
- `importSession` throws `SessionError` for a file that is not JSON, has no messages list, or carries a newer version. Catch it and show its message instead of loading a broken session.

## Errors this package throws

- `not a chat session: the file is not json (...)` (`importSession` got text that does not parse): check the file is a `.hbchat.json` export
- `not a chat session: the file holds no object` (the JSON is an array or a value): pass the session object
- `not a chat session: no messages list` (the object has no `messages` array): export the chat again, or wrap the messages as `{ messages: [...] }`
- `not a chat session: kind ...` (`kind` is set to something other than `hackbuild.chat`): open the file with the tool that wrote it
- `not a chat session this build reads: version ..., newest known 1` (the file is from a newer build): update `@hackbuild/converse`
- `message N is not an object`, `message N has no known role`, `message N has no text` (one message is malformed): fix or drop that message; roles are system, user, assistant and tool
- `the engine stopped` (on a reply's `error`) (the engine threw with no message): look at the `error` event; the reply stays flagged and out of the next request

---

# @hackbuild/depth-mesh

> Turn a depth map, a photo or turntable silhouettes into a closed solid you can print, with a Rust wasm core that runs in your tab.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/depth-mesh/

## Purpose

- Turns a photo into a closed relief solid in one call, with height from depth, brightness or an inflated silhouette.
- Turns a depth map into a point cloud and tracks frames against a voxel model with point to plane ICP.
- Carves a hull from turntable silhouettes and meshes it with surface nets.
- Exports binary STL, OBJ and binary PLY, and checks bounds, open edges and volume.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/depth-mesh
```

No dependencies and no peers. The wasm core ships in the package as `wasm/depth-mesh.wasm` and as base64 in the `@hackbuild/depth-mesh/inline` subpath. Depth maps come from [@hackbuild/vision](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/vision/llms.md) (Depth Anything V2 small, Apache-2.0) or any other source; install it only if you want the depth source.

## Exports

### @hackbuild/depth-mesh

```ts
function bounds(pos: Float32Array): Bounds
```

The axis aligned bounds of xyz positions.

```ts
interface Bounds {
  max: [number, number, number];
  min: [number, number, number];
}
```

The smallest and largest x, y and z of a set of positions.

```ts
function brightnessHeight(img: RgbaImage, cols: number, rows: number): { cover: Uint8Array; values: Float32Array }
```

Brightness per cell, 0 to 1, and coverage (alpha over 127).

```ts
interface Cloud {
  count: number;
  normals: Float32Array;
  positions: Float32Array;
}
```

A point cloud: `count` xyz positions with a normal each.

```ts
interface CloudOptions {
  dmax?: number;
  dmin?: number;
  far: number;
  focal: number;
  near: number;
  stride?: number;
}
```

How DepthMesh.cloud maps depth to distance: near and far, focal length, and the pixel stride and depth range kept.

```ts
function cloudToPly(c: Cloud, colors?: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike>): Uint8Array
```

A binary PLY of a point cloud with its normals and, when given, 0 to 1 colours.

```ts
type CoreSource = { url: string | URL } | { bytes: ArrayBuffer | Uint8Array } | { base64: string }
```

Where loadDepthMesh gets the wasm core: a URL, the bytes, or base64 text such as `DEPTH_MESH_WASM_BASE64`.

```ts
interface DepthGrid {
  data: ArrayLike<number>;
  height: number;
  width: number;
}
```

0 to 1 per pixel, larger is nearer.

```ts
function depthHeight(d: DepthGrid, cols: number, rows: number): Float32Array
```

Depth per cell, resampled bilinear from the map's own size.

```ts
class DepthMesh {
  constructor(x: Exports);
  readonly simd: boolean;
  carve(masks: readonly Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>[], angles: readonly number[], t: Turntable, resolution?: number, smooth?: number): Mesh;
  cloud(depth: Float32Array, w: number, h: number, o: CloudOptions): Cloud;
  healPinches(h: Float32Array, w: number, ht: number): number;
  heightfieldMesh(h: Float32Array, w: number, ht: number, px: number, x0?: number, y0?: number, z0?: number): Mesh;
  model(voxel: number, cap?: number): VoxelModel;
  morphOpen(mask: Uint8Array, w: number, h: number): Uint8Array;
  relief(values: Float32Array, o: ReliefOptions): Float32Array;
  rodrigues(w: [number, number, number]): number[];
  surfaceNets(field: Float32Array, dx: number, dy: number, dz: number, smooth?: number): Mesh;
  synthBox(theta: number, extents: [number, number, number], t: Omit<Turntable, "half">): Uint8Array;
  synthDepth(w: number, h: number): Float32Array;
}
```

The loaded wasm core: depth to cloud, relief heights and solids, surface nets, silhouette carving and voxel models for ICP.

```ts
function fitToPrint(m: Mesh, sizeMM: number): Mesh
```

Centre the mesh and scale it so its longest side is `sizeMM`.

```ts
const HEIGHT_SOURCES: readonly HeightSource[]
```

The height sources, in the order and words a height source select shows.

```ts
interface HeightSource {
  label: string;
  name: HeightSourceName;
  needsModel: boolean;
  params: readonly keyof ReliefParams[];
}
```

One entry of HEIGHT_SOURCES: the name, the label to show, whether it needs a depth model, and the options it reads.

```ts
type HeightSourceName = "depth" | "brightness" | "inflate"
```

The three height sources: Depth Anything depth, brightness, or an inflated silhouette.

```ts
const IDENTITY: Pose
```

The pose with no rotation and no translation.

```ts
function inflateHeight(img: RgbaImage, cols: number, rows: number, o?: { blur?: number; invert?: boolean; threshold?: number }): { cover: Uint8Array; values: Float32Array }
```

Inflated silhouette per cell, 0 to 1: a dome sqrt(1 - (1 - t)^2) over t, the distance to the outline over the largest distance.

```ts
function loadDepthMesh(src: CoreSource): Promise<DepthMesh>
```

Instantiate the depth-mesh wasm core from a URL, bytes or base64 and return a DepthMesh.

```ts
interface MaskGrid {
  data: ArrayLike<number>;
  height: number;
  width: number;
}
```

Any size; resampled to the relief grid, nonzero (128 and up for 8 bit masks) is set.

```ts
interface Mesh {
  indices: Uint32Array;
  positions: Float32Array;
}
```

A triangle mesh: xyz positions and three indices per triangle.

```ts
function openEdges(indices: Uint32Array): number
```

Edges used by other than exactly two triangles; 0 for a closed manifold surface.

```ts
function photoRelief(dm: DepthMesh, image: RgbaImage, o: PhotoReliefOptions): Promise<PhotoRelief>
```

Photo to relief in one call: a height source, the relief parameters, the relief mask and the erase and restore brushes, then the closed solid.

```ts
interface PhotoRelief {
  cols: number;
  depth?: DepthGrid;
  heights: Float32Array;
  mesh: Mesh;
  notes: [level: "ok" | "warn", text: string][];
  px: number;
  rows: number;
  source: HeightSourceName;
}
```

What photoRelief returns: the closed solid, the heights per cell, the cell size, the source used and status notes.

```ts
interface PhotoReliefOptions extends Partial<ReliefParams> {
  base?: number;
  bgcut?: number;
  cells?: number;
  depth?: DepthGrid | (image: RgbaImage) => Promise<DepthGrid>;
  erase?: MaskGrid;
  gamma?: number;
  heal?: boolean;
  height?: number;
  invert?: boolean;
  keepLargest?: boolean;
  mask?: MaskGrid;
  restore?: MaskGrid;
  smooth?: number;
  source: HeightSourceName;
  threshold?: number;
  width?: number;
}
```

Options for photoRelief: the height source, a depth map or a call that makes one, the masks and brushes, and any relief settings to change.

```ts
interface Pose {
  r: number[];
  t: number[];
}
```

Row major rotation (9) and translation (3).

```ts
const RELIEF_DEFAULTS: Readonly<ReliefParams>
```

The default relief settings: 30 mm wide, 0.24 to 2.4 mm high, gamma 1, background cut 0.25, smoothing 0.3 mm, threshold 0.5.

```ts
interface ReliefOptions {
  base: number;
  bgcut?: number;
  gamma?: number;
  height: number;
  invert?: boolean;
  mask?: Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>;
}
```

How DepthMesh.relief turns 0 to 1 values into heights in mm: range, gamma, background cut, invert and mask.

```ts
interface ReliefParams {
  base: number;
  bgcut: number;
  gamma: number;
  height: number;
  invert: boolean;
  smooth: number;
  threshold: number;
  width: number;
}
```

The relief settings in mm and 0 to 1 units; RELIEF_DEFAULTS holds the defaults.

```ts
interface RgbaImage {
  data: ArrayLike<number>;
  height: number;
  width: number;
}
```

RGBA pixels, as ImageData has them.

```ts
function toObj(m: Mesh, name?: string): string
```

A Wavefront OBJ text of the mesh: one object named `name`, vertices and faces.

```ts
function toPly(p: { colors?: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike>; indices?: Uint32Array<ArrayBufferLike>; normals?: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike>; positions: Float32Array }): Uint8Array
```

Binary little endian PLY: vertices with optional normals and 0 to 1 colours, and faces when given.

```ts
function toStl(m: Mesh): Uint8Array
```

A binary STL of the mesh, with a face normal per triangle, in the mesh's own units.

```ts
function trackGood(r: { error: number; inliers: number; pose: Pose }, prev: Pose, sampled: number, maxDist?: number): boolean
```

The accept test for a tracked frame: enough inliers, low error, and no jump.

```ts
interface Turntable {
  dist: number;
  focal: number;
  half: number;
  height: number;
  width: number;
}
```

The turntable camera for DepthMesh.carve: image size, focal length, distance to the axis and the carved cube's half size.

```ts
function volume(m: Mesh): number
```

Signed volume of a closed mesh (positive when faces wind outward).

```ts
class VoxelModel {
  constructor(x: Exports, h: number, dm: DepthMesh);
  readonly size: number;
  dispose(): void;
  icp(c: Cloud, start?: Pose, o?: { iters?: number; maxDist?: number; normalDot?: number; step?: number }): { error: number; inliers: number; pose: Pose };
  integrate(c: Cloud, pose?: Pose): void;
  points(): Cloud;
}
```

A voxel model a scan builds up: refine a frame's pose with `icp`, fold the frame in with `integrate`, read the points back, and `dispose` when done.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { loadDepthMesh, openEdges, photoRelief, toStl } from "@hackbuild/depth-mesh";
import { DEPTH_MESH_WASM_BASE64 } from "@hackbuild/depth-mesh/inline";

// the wasm core, inlined so nothing is fetched
const dm = await loadDepthMesh({ base64: DEPTH_MESH_WASM_BASE64 });
const input = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("input[type=file]")!;

input.onchange = async () => {
  // the chosen photo's pixels; brightness needs no model
  const bitmap = await createImageBitmap(input.files![0]!);
  const ctx = new OffscreenCanvas(bitmap.width, bitmap.height).getContext("2d")!;
  ctx.drawImage(bitmap, 0, 0);
  // a 30 mm wide relief, 0.24 to 2.4 mm high, as a closed solid
  const r = await photoRelief(dm, ctx.getImageData(0, 0, bitmap.width, bitmap.height), { source: "brightness", width: 30, base: 0.24, height: 2.4 });
  console.log("open edges", openEdges(r.mesh.indices), r.notes); // 0 for a closed solid
  // a binary STL in mm, ready for a slicer
  const stl = toStl(r.mesh);
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([stl as BlobPart], { type: "model/stl" }));
  console.log("relief.stl", stl.length, "bytes at", url);
};
```

### from the concepts

```ts
import { depth } from "@hackbuild/vision";
import { photoRelief, toStl } from "@hackbuild/depth-mesh";

const r = await photoRelief(dm, ctx.getImageData(0, 0, w, h), {
  source: "depth",
  depth: saved ?? (() => depth(hub, canvas)),       // a stored map skips the model
  width: 30, base: 0.24, height: 2.4, bgcut: 0.25, smooth: 0.3,
  erase, restore,
});
store(r.depth);                                      // keep the map with the design
download("relief.stl", toStl(r.mesh));               // mm, centred, image up is +y
```

### from the concepts

```ts
const h = dm.relief(map.data, { base: 0.4, height: 2.4, gamma: 1.2, bgcut: 0.1 });
dm.healPinches(h, map.width, map.height);
const relief = dm.heightfieldMesh(h, map.width, map.height, 0.25);
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- You fetch `depth-mesh.wasm` by URL from a page opened on file://, and the fetch fails. Pass `{ base64: DEPTH_MESH_WASM_BASE64 }` from `@hackbuild/depth-mesh/inline` to `loadDepthMesh`, which fetches nothing; use `{ url }` or `{ bytes }` only where you serve the file.
- You expect this package to run Depth Anything. It loads no model; for `source: "depth"` pass `depth` to `photoRelief` as a stored map or a call that makes one, for example through `depth` from @hackbuild/vision, whose weights are Apache-2.0.
- You treat a `photoRelief` result as depth based without reading `notes`. When the depth map is missing or its call throws, it falls back to brightness and says so in a "warn" note; check `r.notes` before you tell the user what they got.
- You keep the voxel model from `model(voxel)` forever. Call `dispose` on it when the scan ends, since its memory lives in the wasm heap.
- You pass grids whose length does not match the size you give. Every call checks and throws a `RangeError` such as "values for a ... grid, which needs ..."; pass `cols * rows` values, and masks the same length as the heights.

## Errors this package throws

- `cloud: grid size W x H must be positive integers` (and other calls) (a width, height or grid size is 0, negative or fractional): pass whole positive sizes
- `cloud: N values for a W x H grid, which needs M` (the array is shorter than the grid): pass width times height values (dx times dy times dz for fields)
- `relief: mask has N cells, values have M` (the relief mask is another size): make the mask the same size as the values, or pass it to `photoRelief`, which resamples
- `carve: N masks but M angles` (masks and angles differ in count): pass one angle per mask
- `photoRelief: N bytes for a W x H RGBA image` (the image is empty or its data is short): pass ImageData or RGBA with width times height times 4 bytes
- `depth failed: ... using brightness; inflate also works with no model` (a note, not a throw) (no depth map, or the depth call threw): pass a stored map or a working depth call; the relief falls back to brightness
- `no relief: every cell was cut. lower the background cut or clear the erase brush` (a note) (background cut, mask or erase removed every cell): lower `bgcut` or clear the brushes
- `depth-mesh wasm: http 404 for ...` (the wasm URL did not load): serve `wasm/depth-mesh.wasm`, or pass `{ base64: DEPTH_MESH_WASM_BASE64 }`

---

# @hackbuild/devices

> Plug onnxruntime-web and transformers.js into the models hub, with device ladders, pinned runtime imports and failure lines your users can read.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/devices/

## Purpose

- Gives the two providers every model package plugs into the `@hackbuild/models` hub, one per runtime.
- Imports transformers.js and onnxruntime-web at run time from pinned CDN URLs with fallbacks, once per page.
- Builds the ladders of device and dtype a load walks, in a fixed order per model family.
- Merges per file download progress into one fraction and one status line.
- Turns a load, run, storage, mic or camera failure into one lowercase line that names it and the working alternative.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/devices
```

It depends on [@hackbuild/ai-env](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/ai-env/llms.md), [@hackbuild/models](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/models/llms.md) and [@hackbuild/weights](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/weights/llms.md). No runtime ships in the package; both load at run time from pinned CDN URLs:

| subpath | runtime | pin |
|---|---|---|
| `.` (`loadTransformers`, `tjsProvider`) | @huggingface/transformers, Apache-2.0 | 4.3.2 |
| `.` (`loadOrt`, `ortProvider`) | onnxruntime-web, Apache-2.0 | 1.27.0 |

Each runtime is optional: load only the one your models use.

## Exports

### @hackbuild/devices


Ladders by name, one per model family.

```ts
function loadOrt(opts?: ImportEsmOptions & { version?: string }): () => Promise<OrtModule>
```

A memoized loader of the pinned transformers.js; call the returned function to import it.

```ts
  total: number | null;
}
```

Progress summed across files: bytes loaded, the total when known, the fraction, the file count and a status line.

```ts

  readonly sessions: Record<string, OrtSession>;
  dispose(): Promise<void>;

```

What ortProvider loads: the runtime module, sessions by graph name, the first session, the rung that worked, and `dispose`.

The parts of the onnxruntime-web module the provider touches.

```ts
function ortProvider(opts: OrtProviderOptions): OrtProvider
```

The onnxruntime-web provider for the models hub: fetches each graph once through the weight store and builds a session per rung from the same bytes.

```ts
interface OrtProvider {
  factory: Factory<OrtModel>;

}
```

The onnxruntime-web provider: the hub factory, and `forget` to release a record's bytes.

```ts
interface OrtProviderOptions {

```

Options for ortProvider: the runtime loader, the weight store, the wasm file directory and a per file progress callback.

```ts
interface OrtSession {
```

Pipeline options for a rung.

```ts
function runtimeLoader<T>(urls: readonly string[], opts?: ImportEsmOptions): () => Promise<T>
```

Memoized loaders, so every package shares one runtime instance per page.


Session options for a rung: the rung's ort block plus any runtime options.

```ts
const TJS_TASKS: Record<string, string>
```

```ts
interface TjsEnv {
  allowLocalModels?: boolean;
  allowRemoteModels?: boolean;
  backends?: { onnx?: { wasm?: { numThreads?: number; proxy?: boolean } } };
  customCache?: unknown;
  useBrowserCache?: boolean;
  useCustomCache?: boolean;
  useWasmCache?: boolean;
}
```

The parts of transformers.js `env` the provider sets: local and remote models, caches and the onnx wasm backend.

```ts
function tjsLadder(spec: TjsLadderSpec): Rung[]
```

transformers.js rungs from a spec.

```ts
interface TjsLadderSpec {
  freshHeapRetry?: boolean;
  options?: Record<string, unknown>;
  wasm?: readonly Dtype[];
  wasmFirst?: boolean;
  webgpu?: readonly Dtype[];
}
```

The dtypes to try on WebGPU and on wasm, their order, a fresh heap retry, and options copied onto every rung.

```ts
interface TjsLoadContext extends FactoryContext {
  env: Env | undefined;
  hub: Hub;
  last: boolean;
  options: Record<string, unknown>;
  record: ModelRecord;
  rung: Rung;
  signal: AbortSignal | undefined;
  tjs: TjsModule;
  report(phase: "fetch" | "compile" | "warm", fraction: number | null, file?: string): void;
}
```

What a custom TjsLoader receives: the hub's factory context, the transformers.js module and the pipeline options for the rung.

```ts
type TjsLoader<T = unknown> = (ctx: TjsLoadContext) => Promise<T>
```

A custom loader for one capability on the transformers.js provider; it returns the loaded model.

```ts
interface TjsModule {
  [name: string]: unknown;
  env?: TjsEnv;
  pipeline?: (task: string, model: string, opts: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<unknown>;
}
```

The parts of the transformers.js module the provider touches.

```ts
function tjsProvider(opts: TjsProviderOptions): TjsProvider
```

The transformers.js provider for the models hub: configures the runtime once and loads each record through a registered loader or `pipeline`.

```ts
interface TjsProvider {
  factory: Factory;
  configure(tjs: TjsModule, env: Env | undefined): void;
  loader<T>(capability: string, fn: TjsLoader<T>): void;
}
```

The transformers.js provider: the hub factory, `loader` to register a capability's loader, and `configure`.

```ts
interface TjsProviderOptions {
  cache?: unknown;
  onProgress?: (recordId: string, p: MergedProgress) => void;
  runtime: () => Promise<TjsModule>;
}
```

Options for tjsProvider: the runtime loader, a custom cache from @hackbuild/weights, and a progress callback.

```ts
function transformersUrls(version?: string): string[]
```

The URLs transformers.js is imported from, jsDelivr first, then esm.sh.

```ts
function walkLadder<T>(id: string, rungs: readonly Rung[], attempt: (rung: Rung, index: number) => Promise<T>, opts?: { onFailure?: (f: LadderFailure) => void }): Promise<{ failures: LadderFailure[]; rung: Rung; value: T }>
```

Try each rung until `attempt` resolves.

```ts
function wasmThreads(env: Env | undefined): number
```

wasm thread count to set on a runtime: the probe's safe count, 1 without a probe.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { probe } from "@hackbuild/ai-env";
import { humanError, LADDERS, loadOrt, loadTransformers, ortProvider, ortWasmPaths, tjsProvider } from "@hackbuild/devices";
import { CATALOG, createHub } from "@hackbuild/models";
import { openWeightStore } from "@hackbuild/weights";

// one hub per page; one provider per runtime, each runtime imported at run time from a pinned url
const hub = createHub({ env: await probe() });
hub.provide("tjs", tjsProvider({ runtime: loadTransformers() }).factory);
hub.provide("ort", ortProvider({ runtime: loadOrt(), store: await openWeightStore(), wasmPaths: ortWasmPaths() }).factory);

// a catalog record on the depth ladder: webgpu fp16, webgpu fp32, wasm q8, wasm fp32
const rec = { ...CATALOG.find((r) => r.id === "depth-anything-v2-small")!, ladder: LADDERS.depth() };
hub.registry.add(rec);
console.log("weight licence", rec.licence); // from the record

// load it; a failure becomes one lowercase line naming it and what still works
const line = await hub.use("depth").then((l) => `loaded on ${l.rung.device}`, (e) => humanError(e));
console.log(line);
```

### from the concepts

```ts
const tjs = tjsProvider({ runtime: loadTransformers() });
const ort = ortProvider({ runtime: loadOrt(), store: await openWeightStore(), wasmPaths: ortWasmPaths() });
hub.provide("tjs", tjs.factory);
hub.provide("ort", ort.factory);
```

### from the concepts

```ts
LADDERS.depth()          // webgpu fp16, webgpu fp32, wasm q8, wasm fp32
LADDERS.perceptionCpu()  // wasm q8, wasm fp32, then webgpu
LADDERS.whisperTurbo()   // fp16 encoder plus q4 decoder, fp32 encoder, q8 on wasm
LADDERS.smolvlm()        // per sub graph dtypes, q4 retry in a fresh heap
LADDERS.ort()            // webgpu at basic, all, disabled, then wasm
tjsLadder({ webgpu: ["q4f16"], wasm: ["q8"] })
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- You import `@huggingface/transformers` or `onnxruntime-web` at the top of your file. Pass `loadTransformers()` to `tjsProvider` and `loadOrt()` to `ortProvider`; both import once per page from pinned URLs through the file:// safe `importEsm`, and a failed import retries on the next call.
- You call `hub.provide` for a runtime in each package or component. Provide `tjs` and `ort` once per page; every model package registers its loader on the same provider with `tjs.loader(capability, fn)`.
- You expect transformers.js weights to persist on file://. The browser cache is off there; pass `cache: transformersCache(store)` from @hackbuild/weights to `tjsProvider`. Wasm threads come from the probe, so do not set them yourself.
- You build an ort record without files or fetch the graph per rung. `ortProvider` needs `store` and reads each file once through `store.once`, then builds every rung's session from the same bytes; a record without `source.url`, `source.file` or `source.files` throws "an ort record needs source.url, source.file or source.files". The weight licence is the record's `licence`.
- You pass `{ integrity: RUNTIME_SHA256 }` and leave ort's wasm paths alone. The checked text imports from a Blob URL, which moves `import.meta.url`; pass `wasmPaths: ortWasmPaths()` to `ortProvider` when you turn integrity on.
- You show the raw error from a failed load. Pass it to `humanError(e)`, or `humanError("mic", e)` and `humanError("camera", e)` for a device, and show the one lowercase line it returns.

## Errors this package throws

- `ID: an ort record needs source.url, source.file or source.files` (the record names no graph): give the record a `source.url`, `file` or `files`
- `ID: no .onnx graph among the files` (every file was external data): list the `.onnx` graph in `source.files`
- `ID: a transformers.js record needs source.modelId` (no model id or repo): set `source.modelId`
- `ID: no transformers.js task for CAPABILITY; register a loader` (the capability is not in `TJS_TASKS`): set `rung.options.task`, or call `tjs.loader(capability, fn)`
- `the transformers.js module has no pipeline export` (the runtime import gave another module): load it with `loadTransformers()`, or pass a module with `pipeline`

---

# @hackbuild/embed

> Turn sentences into vectors in the tab, for memory recall and action matching, with an id that changes only when the vectors would.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/embed/

## Purpose

- Builds a model2vec style static embedder in plain TypeScript from tokenizer.json, model.safetensors and config.json, with no ML runtime.
- Wraps a transformers.js feature extraction pipeline, MiniLM by default or bge-small, as the same `Embedder` shape.
- Gives each embedder an id that fingerprints the model and settings, so @hackbuild/memory re-embeds only when the vectors would change.
- Adds its model records and loaders to a @hackbuild/models hub.
- Keeps vectors in a brute force cosine `VectorIndex` with top k and a score floor.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/embed @hackbuild/weights
```

It depends on @hackbuild/memory, @hackbuild/models and @hackbuild/devices, which install with it. It has no peers. The quick start also uses `@hackbuild/weights`. transformers.js is passed in at run time for `miniLM` and `tjsEmbedder`, never imported by this package; `loadTransformers` in @hackbuild/devices loads the pinned 4.3.2.

## Exports

### @hackbuild/embed


Add the embed records to a hub, register the transformers.js loader for "embed" (an Embedder, with the rung's dtype and device in its id) and the static factory.

```ts
function cosine(a: Float32Array, b: Float32Array): number
```

```ts
interface TjsLike {
  pipeline?: (task: string, model: string, opts: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<unknown>;
}
```

The pieces of transformers.js this adapter calls.

```ts
interface Tokenizer {
  readonly unkId: number | null;
  readonly vocabSize: number;
  encode(text: string): number[];
  tokens(text: string): string[];
}
```

A loaded tokenizer that turns text into token ids with no special tokens.

```ts
interface TokenizerJson {
  added_tokens?: { content: string; id: number; special?: boolean }[];
  model?: { continuing_subword_prefix?: string; max_input_chars_per_word?: number; type?: string; unk_token?: string; vocab?: Record<string, number> | [string, number][] };
  normalizer?: NormalizerJson | null;
}
```

BERT style tokenization from a Hugging Face tokenizer.json: the BertNormalizer (clean text, pad CJK ideographs, strip accents, lowercase), the BertPreTokenizer (split on whitespace and punctuation) and WordPiece (greedy longest match with a continuation prefix).

```ts
class VectorIndex<T> {
  constructor();
  readonly size: number;
  add(item: T, vec: Float32Array): void;
  remove(pred: (item: T) => boolean): number;
  search(q: Float32Array, k?: number, minScore?: number): { item: T; score: number }[];
}
```

An in memory list of items and their vectors, searched by cosine for the top k.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { EMBED_RECORDS, staticEmbedder, VectorIndex } from "@hackbuild/embed";
import { openWeightStore } from "@hackbuild/weights";

// potion-base-8M; its record gives the pinned base URL and the weight licence, the weight store caches each file
const rec = EMBED_RECORDS.find((r) => r.id === "potion-base-8m")!;
const store = await openWeightStore();
const get = (file: string) => store.once({ url: rec.source.url + file, licence: rec.licence });
const dec = new TextDecoder();
const e = staticEmbedder({ name: "potion-base-8M", tokenizer: dec.decode(await get("tokenizer.json")), weights: await get("model.safetensors"), config: dec.decode(await get("config.json")) });

// embed a few notes and keep them in an index
const notes = ["the mug goes on the shelf", "water the plants on friday", "the router password is on the fridge"];
const index = new VectorIndex<string>();
(await e.embed(notes)).forEach((v, i) => index.add(notes[i]!, v));

// the two closest notes at cosine 0.1 or above, best first
console.log(e.id, index.search(e.embedOne("where is the cup"), 2, 0.1));
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- Never import `@huggingface/transformers` here. Pass the module to `miniLM` or a pipeline to `tjsEmbedder`, for example `await loadTransformers()()` from `@hackbuild/devices`; the static embedder needs no runtime at all.
- `loadStaticEmbedder(base)` fetches straight from the URL and does not cache. To keep the files, read them with `store.once({ url, licence: rec.licence })` from `@hackbuild/weights`, taking the URL from the record's `source.url` in `EMBED_RECORDS`, and pass the bytes to `staticEmbedder`.
- Take the weight licence from the record (`rec.licence` in `EMBED_RECORDS`): potion-base-8M and bge-small-en-v1.5 are MIT, all-MiniLM-L6-v2 is Apache-2.0. Never write it as a constant.
- The static embedder reads WordPiece and WordLevel tokenizers only. A Unigram or BPE tokenizer.json throws `tokenizer model ... is not supported`, so point it at a model2vec repo such as potion-base-8M.
- Keep the embedder `id` with your stored vectors. It changes whenever the weights, tokenizer, dtype, device, pooling or normalization change, and `@hackbuild/memory` re-embeds on a new id; never compare vectors from two ids.
- `miniLM` runs on wasm q8 by default. Pass `device: "webgpu"` with `dtype: "fp32"` to move it; never pair webgpu with q8.

## Errors this package throws

- `safetensors: file shorter than its header length` (the weights file is truncated or not safetensors): fetch the file again
- `safetensors: header runs past the end of the file` (the download stopped early): fetch the file again
- `safetensors: dtype ... of ... is not supported` (a tensor type other than F32, F16, BF16, I32 or I64): use a model with float weights
- `model2vec: no 2d float embeddings tensor in the safetensors file` (the file is not a model2vec model): point at a model2vec repo such as potion-base-8M
- `model2vec: http ... for ...` (the base URL returned an error): check the base URL ends at the repo's resolve path
- `model2vec: sha256 of ... is ..., expected ...` (the file does not match its pin): fetch it again; the pin names the expected bytes
- `tokenizer.json has no model.vocab` (the tokenizer file has no vocabulary): use the repo's tokenizer.json or a vocab.txt
- `tokenizer model ... is not supported; WordPiece and WordLevel are` (a Unigram or BPE tokenizer): use a model with a WordPiece or WordLevel tokenizer
- `the transformers.js module has no pipeline export` (the module passed in is not transformers.js): pass the module from `loadTransformers` in @hackbuild/devices
- `...: a static record needs source.url` (a static hub record with no URL): give the record a `source.url`

---

# @hackbuild/imagegen

> Generate an image from a prompt in your tab with SD-Turbo or SD 1.5 on onnxruntime-web WebGPU, seeded so the same seed gives the same start.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/imagegen/

## Purpose

- Runs the CLIP text encoder, a seeded Euler loop over the UNet and the VAE decoder, and returns RGBA ready for ImageData.
- Loads SD-Turbo or SD 1.5 through the models hub, with the three graphs cached in the weight store.
- Gives each model a form (steps, guidance, negative prompt, sizes) and clamps requests to it.
- Runs every graph call under the hub's gpu lock and frame budget, so it shares the GPU with chat or vision models.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/imagegen @hackbuild/ai-env @hackbuild/devices @hackbuild/weights
```

It depends on [@hackbuild/models](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/models/llms.md). The hub path in the quick start also needs [@hackbuild/ai-env](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/ai-env/llms.md) for `probe`, [@hackbuild/devices](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/devices/llms.md) for the ort provider and [@hackbuild/weights](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/weights/llms.md) for the store; the line above installs them. No package is bundled from these runtimes; they load at run time:

| subpath | runtime | pin |
|---|---|---|
| `.` (graphs) | onnxruntime-web, through `loadOrt` from @hackbuild/devices | 1.27.0 |
| `.` (tokenizer) | @huggingface/transformers, through `loadTransformers` from @hackbuild/devices | 4.3.2 |

Load an image model through the hub: a record id (`{ id: "sd-1.5" }`) or the capability ("imagegen", which the hub routes, or sends to the stub in stub mode).

The load button label: names the model and its download size with the size's source.

```ts
function mulberry32(seed: number): Rng
```

mulberry32: a 32 bit seeded generator in [0, 1).

```ts
interface OrtLike {
  Tensor: new (type: string, data: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike> | Int32Array<ArrayBufferLike> | BigInt64Array<ArrayBufferLike>, dims: number[]) => unknown;
}
```

```ts
function padIds(ids: ArrayLike<number>, n?: number, pad?: number): Int32Array
```

CLIP token ids padded or cut to `n` (77), padded with `pad` or the last id.

```ts
type Rng = () => number
```

The sampler SD-Turbo is distilled for, written from the published diffusers description: 1000 step scaled linear betas (0.00085 to 0.012), sigma = sqrt((1 - alphaBar) / alphaBar), trailing timestep spacing, and an Euler step on epsilon.

```ts
interface SessionLike {
  run(feeds: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<Record<string, { data: ArrayLike<number>; dims?: readonly number[] }>>;
}
```

The part of an onnxruntime-web InferenceSession generate calls: `run` with named feeds.

```ts
interface Sessions {
  textEncoder: SessionLike;
  unet: SessionLike;
  vaeDecoder: SessionLike;
}
```

The three graphs of a Stable Diffusion export: text encoder, UNet and VAE decoder.

```ts
function sessionsOf(m: ImagegenModel, form: ImageForm): Sessions
```

The three sessions of a loaded model, by the form's graph names.

```ts
function sigmas(n?: number, betaStart?: number, betaEnd?: number): Float64Array
```

Sigma for each of the 1000 training timesteps.

```ts
type Spacing = "trailing" | "leading"
```

Timestep spacing: `trailing` for SD-Turbo, `leading` for SD 1.5.

```ts
function stubImagegenModel(): ImagegenModel
```

A weightless model for stub pages and tests: the text encoder returns zeros, the UNet predicts zero noise, and the VAE returns a flat grey, so the whole flow (stages, timing cells, history) runs with no download.

```ts
function toRgba(nchw: ArrayLike<number>, w: number, h: number): Uint8ClampedArray
```

NCHW floats in [-1, 1] to RGBA bytes.

```ts
function trailingTimesteps(steps: number, train?: number): number[]
```

Trailing spacing: 1 step is [999], 4 steps are [999, 749, 499, 249].

```ts
const VAE_SCALE: 0.18215
```

The latent scale of the Stable Diffusion VAE; the final latent is divided by it before decoding.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { probe } from "@hackbuild/ai-env";
import { loadOrt, loadTransformers, ortProvider } from "@hackbuild/devices";
import { attachImagegen, loadImagegen, type ClipTokenize } from "@hackbuild/imagegen";
import { createHub } from "@hackbuild/models";
import { openWeightStore } from "@hackbuild/weights";

// a hub with the ort provider: onnxruntime-web loads from a pinned url, the weight store caches the graphs
const hub = createHub({ env: await probe() });
hub.provide("ort", ortProvider({ runtime: loadOrt(), store: await openWeightStore() }).factory);
attachImagegen(hub);

// sd-turbo; gen.record.licence names its weight licence (Stability AI, no commercial use)
const gen = await loadImagegen(hub, { id: "sd-turbo" });

// the CLIP tokenizer (weights MIT) through transformers.js, 77 ids
type Tok = { from_pretrained(id: string): Promise<(p: string, o: object) => Promise<{ input_ids: { data: ArrayLike<number> } }>> };
const clip = await ((await loadTransformers()()).AutoTokenizer as Tok).from_pretrained(gen.form.tokenizer);
const tokenize: ClipTokenize = async (p) => (await clip(p, { padding: "max_length", max_length: 77, truncation: true })).input_ids.data;
const img = await gen.generate(tokenize, { prompt: "a ceramic mug on a wooden shelf", seed: 42 }); // seeded, on webgpu
document.querySelector("canvas")!.getContext("2d")!.putImageData(new ImageData(img.rgba as Uint8ClampedArray<ArrayBuffer>, img.width, img.height), 0, 0);
```

### from the concepts

```ts
import { generate } from "@hackbuild/imagegen";

// sessions from your own bytes (the weights store), webgpu execution provider
const sessions = {
  textEncoder: await ort.InferenceSession.create(te, { executionProviders: ["webgpu"] }),
  unet: await ort.InferenceSession.create(unet, { executionProviders: ["webgpu"] }),
  vaeDecoder: await ort.InferenceSession.create(vae, { executionProviders: ["webgpu"] }),
};
const img = await generate(ort, sessions, tokenize, {
  prompt: "a ceramic mug on a wooden shelf",
  steps: 1,
  seed: 42,
  run: (fn) => hub.exclusive("gpu", fn), // share the gpu with a chat or vision model
});
ctx2d.putImageData(new ImageData(img.rgba, img.width, img.height), 0, 0);
```

### from the concepts

```ts
const rec = IMAGEGEN_RECORDS[1];        // sd-1.5
button.textContent = loadLabel(rec);    // "load stable diffusion 1.5, about 2.0 gb (vendor)"
const gen = await loadImagegen(hub, { id: rec.id });
const img = await gen.generate(tokenize, { prompt, negative, seed, signal });
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- You import `onnxruntime-web` statically. Provide it through the hub with `hub.provide("ort", ortProvider({ runtime: loadOrt(), store }).factory)` from @hackbuild/devices, and onnxruntime-web loads at run time from its pinned URL.
- You fetch the three graphs yourself. Pass `store: await openWeightStore()` to `ortProvider`, call `attachImagegen(hub)`, then `loadImagegen(hub, { id: "sd-turbo" })`; the graphs load from the Hugging Face hub and the weight store caches them. Read the weight licence from `gen.record.licence`, since SD-Turbo here bars commercial use.
- You call `generate` without a tokenizer. It takes a `ClipTokenize` you build, for example the CLIP tokenizer from `loadTransformers()` padded to 77 ids, then the request with `prompt` and `seed`.
- You offer image generation where there is no WebGPU adapter. The records have only a WebGPU rung and no wasm fallback, so check the adapter first and disable the load button without one.
- You pass a size the model does not make. `applyForm` refuses it with a `FormError` ("this model makes 512 pixel images, not ...") whose message you can show as is; read the sizes from `gen.form.sizes`.
- You keep the model loaded after the user leaves the generator. Call `gen.release()` so the hub can drop the graphs under its memory budget.

## Errors this package throws

- `size must be a multiple of 8` (`size` is not divisible by 8): pass 512, or another multiple of 8 the graphs accept
- `this model makes 512 pixel images, not N.` (`FormError`) (the size is not in the model's form): use a size from `gen.form.sizes`; show the message as is
- `the loaded model has no unet graph; it has ...` (the record's files did not load as three graphs): check the record's `source.files` paths
- `image generation stopped` (`AbortError`) (the signal was aborted): expected on cancel; catch it by name

---

# @hackbuild/listen

> You feed it microphone blocks and it hands back each thing the person said as text, and tells you when they talk over your character.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/listen/

## Purpose

- Finds utterances in microphone audio with a VAD state machine fed by Silero VAD v5 or an energy gate with no weights.
- Sends each utterance to a transcriber and through the phantom text filter of @hackbuild/transcribe.
- Swaps to stricter thresholds while your character talks, so its own voice does not count and speech that clears the bar is a barge in.
- Shows interim words while the person speaks, from a growing Whisper window or the browser's system recognizer, and writes them into a text field with `dictate`.
- Opens the microphone with echo cancellation and streams blocks from a capture AudioWorklet that runs from file://.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/listen @hackbuild/devices @hackbuild/weights
```

It depends on @hackbuild/models and @hackbuild/transcribe and has no peers; the quick start also uses @hackbuild/devices for the runtimes and @hackbuild/weights for the Silero bytes. onnxruntime-web for Silero and the transcriber's runtime are passed in by you, for example through the loaders in @hackbuild/devices.

| subpath | runtime | pin |
|---|---|---|
| `.` (`sileroVad`) | onnxruntime-web, passed in | your choice; `loadOrt` in @hackbuild/devices pins 1.27.0 |
| `.` (`hubTranscriber`) | the models hub with @hackbuild/transcribe's records | what you register on the hub |
| `.` (`speechEngine`) | the browser's SpeechRecognition | none |

## Exports

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { loadOrt, loadTransformers, tjsProvider } from "@hackbuild/devices";
import { createListener, hubTranscriber, micBlocks, openMic, sileroVad, VAD_RECORDS, type OrtLike } from "@hackbuild/listen";
import { createHub } from "@hackbuild/models";
import { attachTranscribe } from "@hackbuild/transcribe";
import { openWeightStore } from "@hackbuild/weights";

// ask for the microphone first, so the prompt shows before any download
const stream = await openMic();
const ctx = new AudioContext();
// Silero VAD v5 (weights MIT) on onnxruntime-web, its bytes cached by the weight store
const silero = VAD_RECORDS[0]!;
const bytes = await (await openWeightStore()).once({ url: silero.source.url!, sha256: silero.source.sha256!, licence: silero.licence });
const vad = await sileroVad((await loadOrt()()) as unknown as OrtLike, bytes);
// Whisper (weights MIT) through the models hub turns each utterance into text; mic blocks feed the listener
const hub = createHub();
attachTranscribe(hub);
hub.provide("tjs", tjsProvider({ runtime: loadTransformers() }).factory);
const listener = createListener({ vad, inputRate: ctx.sampleRate, transcribe: hubTranscriber(hub, { model: "whisper-base.en" }), onUtterance: (u) => console.log(u.bargeIn ? "barge in:" : "heard:", u.text) });
listener.start();
await micBlocks(ctx, stream, (b) => listener.push(b));
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- You import onnxruntime-web at the top of the file for Silero. Pass the runtime in: `sileroVad(await loadOrt()(), bytes)` with `loadOrt` from @hackbuild/devices; this package bundles no runtime.
- You pass `sileroVad` a URL. It takes the model bytes: fetch them with `store.once({ url, sha256, licence })` from @hackbuild/weights, taking `url`, `sha256` and `licence` from `VAD_RECORDS[0]`, so the hash is checked and the licence comes from the record.
- You push blocks and nothing happens. The listener drops every block until you call `start()`, and `stop()` resets the machine and the VAD state.
- You leave out `inputRate`. It defaults to 48000, so pass `ctx.sampleRate` from the AudioContext that feeds `micBlocks`, or the 16 kHz frames are cut from the wrong rate.
- You download the models before asking for the microphone. Call `openMic()` first so the prompt shows at once, and keep its echo cancellation on, since barge in counts on the character's voice being cancelled out of the input.
- You expect barge in to work on its own. Wire `setTalking` to @hackbuild/speak's `onSpeaking` and `onBargeIn` to the speaker's `stop()`; transcription failures arrive in `onError`, never as a throw.

## Errors this package throws

- `onError` with the transcriber's error (the transcriber threw): read the error from @hackbuild/models or @hackbuild/transcribe; the listener keeps listening
- `speechEngine` state `unsupported` (no SpeechRecognition in this browser): use the window path with `onInterim`
- `speechEngine` state `denied`, `onError` with `not-allowed`, `service-not-allowed` or `audio-capture` (the microphone or the recognizer service was refused): ask again from a click, or use the window path
- `Utterance.dropped` set and `text` empty (the phantom filter dropped the text; `dropped` names the reason): nothing, or pass `filter: false`
- barge in fires on the character's own voice (echo cancellation is off or the speakers are loud): use `openMic`, headphones, or raise the `talking` thresholds

---

# @hackbuild/media

> Decode a file's audio at the rate a model wants, pick keyframes from a video, and record a canvas, all in the tab.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/media/

## Purpose

- Decodes the audio track of a file or Blob with the browser's own decoder and resamples it to the rate you ask for.
- Picks keyframes from frames you sampled, by how far each frame's brightness histogram moved.
- Records a canvas or any MediaStream with the first webm or mp4 type the browser supports.
- Takes every browser object as an optional argument, so tests and workers pass their own.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/media
```

No dependencies and no peers. It runs no model and fetches nothing.

## Exports

### @hackbuild/media

```ts
function decodeAudio(data: ArrayBuffer | Blob, sampleRate?: number, Ctx?: OfflineCtor): Promise<DecodedAudio>
```

Decode and resample with the browser's decoder.

```ts
interface DecodedAudio {
  channels: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike>[];
  duration: number;
  sampleRate: number;
}
```

Audio decoded and resampled by decodeAudio: one Float32Array per channel at sampleRate.

```ts
function histDistance(a: Float32Array, b: Float32Array): number
```

Half the L1 distance of two normalized histograms: 0 same, 1 disjoint.

```ts
function lumaHistogram(rgba: ArrayLike<number>, bins?: number): Float32Array
```

A 32 bin luminance histogram of RGBA pixels, normalized to sum 1.

```ts
type OfflineCtor = new (channels: number, length: number, sampleRate: number) => OfflineCtxLike
```

A constructor of an OfflineCtxLike, with the OfflineAudioContext arguments.

```ts
interface OfflineCtxLike {
  destination: unknown;
  createBufferSource(): { buffer: AudioBufferLike | null; connect(d: unknown): void; start(): void };
  decodeAudioData(b: ArrayBuffer): Promise<AudioBufferLike>;
  startRendering(): Promise<AudioBufferLike>;
}
```

The part of OfflineAudioContext that decodeAudio calls; tests and workers pass their own.

```ts
function pickKeyframes(frames: readonly { hist: Float32Array; t: number }[], o?: { max?: number; maxGap?: number; threshold?: number }): number[]
```

Keyframes from sampled frames: the first frame, every frame whose histogram moved more than `threshold` from the last keyframe, and at least one every `maxGap` seconds; at most `max` frames, the biggest changes kept.

```ts
function pickMime(isSupported?: (t: string) => boolean, types?: string[]): string
```

The first type the recorder supports, or "" for the browser default.

```ts
function record(stream: unknown, o?: { bitsPerSecond?: number; mimeType?: string; Recorder?: new (s: unknown, opts: Record<string, unknown>) => RecorderLike; timeslice?: number }): { mimeType: string; stop(): Promise<Blob> }
```

Record a MediaStream (canvas.captureStream() plus audio tracks) until `stop()`; resolves the Blob.

```ts
const RECORDER_TYPES: string[]
```

MIME types pickMime tries in order: vp9, vp8, plain webm, then mp4.

```ts
function sampleTimes(duration: number, step?: number): number[]
```

Sample times for a video of `duration` seconds every `step` seconds, inside the clip.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { decodeAudio, lumaHistogram, pickKeyframes, sampleTimes } from "@hackbuild/media";

const input = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("input[type=file]")!;
input.onchange = async () => {
  const file = input.files![0]!;
  const { channels, duration } = await decodeAudio(file, 16000); // the audio at 16 kHz for speech to text
  console.log(`${channels.length} channels, ${duration.toFixed(1)} s`);
  // one small frame a second off a video element, then keyframes by scene change
  const video = Object.assign(document.createElement("video"), { src: URL.createObjectURL(file), muted: true });
  await new Promise((r) => (video.onloadeddata = r));
  const g = new OffscreenCanvas(64, 36).getContext("2d")!;
  const frames: { t: number; hist: Float32Array }[] = [];
  for (const t of sampleTimes(video.duration, 1)) {
    video.currentTime = t;
    await new Promise((r) => (video.onseeked = r));
    g.drawImage(video, 0, 0, 64, 36);
    frames.push({ t, hist: lumaHistogram(g.getImageData(0, 0, 64, 36).data) });
  }
  console.log("keyframes at", pickKeyframes(frames, { threshold: 0.3, maxGap: 10, max: 12 }).map((i) => frames[i]!.t));
};
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- You call `decodeAudio` in a worker and get `no OfflineAudioContext here. decode on the page, not in a worker.` Decode on the page and post the channels to the worker, or pass an OfflineAudioContext constructor as the third argument in tests.
- You decode at the file's own rate and resample later. Pass the rate the model wants as the second argument: `decodeAudio(file, 16000)` for speech models, 44100 for @hackbuild/stems, 22050 for @hackbuild/notes.
- You mix the channels yourself and lose one. `decodeAudio` keeps every channel in `channels`; pick or mix them where you use them, for example with `toMono` from @hackbuild/transcribe.
- You expect mkv or avi to decode everywhere. This package adds no demuxer, so a file decodes only when the browser plays it in a video tag; catch `this browser will not decode the audio track (...)` and ask for mp4, webm, mp3 or wav.
- You pass `pickKeyframes` raw pixels. Give it `{ t, hist }` per frame, where `hist` is `lumaHistogram(rgba)`; it returns indices into your frames, and `sampleTimes(duration, step)` gives the times to seek to.
- You start `record` without a MediaRecorder check. It throws `no MediaRecorder in this browser. recording is off.`; hide the record control and say why, and read `mimeType` for the type it chose.

## Errors this package throws

- `no OfflineAudioContext here. decode on the page, not in a worker.` (called in a worker or in Node): decode on the page, or pass a constructor as the third argument
- `this browser will not decode the audio track (...)` (the browser refused the container or codec): convert to mp4, webm, mp3 or wav; mkv and avi usually fail
- `no MediaRecorder in this browser. recording is off.` (no MediaRecorder): pass `Recorder`, or hide the record control and say why

---

# @hackbuild/memory

> Give an agent or character in a browser tab a memory you can add to, recall from and fit into a prompt, with a wasm core and IndexedDB storage.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/memory/

## Purpose

- Recalls by BM25 plus cosine search fused by reciprocal rank in a Rust core compiled to wasm32 with SIMD128, with two scorers, kind decay, strengthening on recall and near duplicate merge.
- Keeps items in IndexedDB, one database per memory, and caches vectors per embedder.
- Assembles a context into a token budget and injects recall without changing earlier messages, so a cached prompt prefix stays reusable.
- Explains every recall: per candidate ranks, score parts and per term BM25 weights.
- Seals text, metadata, vectors and values at rest under a password through the `./seal` subpath.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/memory
```

No dependencies and no peers. The wasm core ships in the package; load it from `@hackbuild/memory/memory.wasm` by URL, as bytes, or inlined base64 from `@hackbuild/memory/inline`.

| subpath | what it adds |
|---|---|
| `.` | the core loader, `open`, `Memory`, assembly and trace |
| `./inline` | `MEMORY_WASM_BASE64`, the wasm as base64 |
| `./seal` | password sealing and `sealedSink` |
| `./memory.wasm` | the wasm file |

## Exports

### @hackbuild/memory

```ts
interface AddOptions {
  arousal?: number;
  dedup?: boolean;
  dupCosine?: number;
  dupWindowMs?: number;
  entities?: string[];
  importance?: number;
  kind?: "episode" | "gist" | "lesson" | "fact" | "rule" | "lore" | "doc" | "note";
  meta?: Record<string, unknown>;
  novelty?: number;
  place?: [number, number, number];
  scope?: string;
  section?: string;
  valence?: number;
}
```

Options for `Memory.add`: kind, scope, importance, emotion, novelty and the other fields stored on the item.

```ts
interface Assembled {
  budgetTokens: number;
  dropped: string[];
  kept: string[];
  text: string;
  usedTokens: number;
}
```

A context fitted to a token budget: the text, the section names kept and dropped, and the tokens used.

```ts
function assembleSections(o: { budgetTokens: number; coreText?: string; estimate?: (s: string) => number; fixed?: string[]; recalled?: string[]; recent?: string[]; sections?: Section[]; summary?: string }): Assembled
```

The memory sections in the order of the embodied agent prompt: core facts (priority 10), caller sections, a summary (6), recalled lines (5), recent turns (3), then budget().

```ts
function budget(opts: { budgetTokens: number; estimate?: (s: string) => number; fixed?: string[]; joiner?: string; sections: Section[] }): Assembled
```

Fixed lines always go in; ranked sections join highest priority first while they fit the budget (equal priorities keep their given order).

```ts
const CHARS_PER_TOKEN: 3.6
```

Characters per token for the default estimate (inferred, not measured on a tokenizer).

```ts
interface CompactOptions {
  consolidate?: false | { keep?: number; min?: number; scope?: string; summarize?: (texts: string[]) => Promise<string> };
  decay?: number | false;
  merge?: number | false;
}
```

Options for `Memory.compact`: the decay floor, the merge cosine and the episode folding, each of which can be turned off.

```ts
interface CompactReport {
  after: number;
  before: number;
  decayed: number[];
  gist: { folded: number; id: number } | null;
  merged: [number, number][];
}
```

What `Memory.compact` did: item counts before and after, the ids decayed, the pairs merged and the gist made.

```ts
class Core {
  constructor(x: Exports);
  readonly simd: boolean;
  readonly exports: Exports;
  call<R>(bufs: (Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike> | null)[], fn: (flat: number[]) => R): R;
  exp(x: number): number;
  index(dim: number): CoreIndex;

  out(n: number): Float64Array;
  retention(kind: number, ageH: number, uses: number): number;
}
```

```ts

  vecRank: number;

```

```ts
class CoreIndex {
  constructor(core: Core, handle: number, dim: number);
  readonly dim: number;
  readonly handle: number;
  readonly size: number;
  decay(nowH: number, floor: number): number[];
  dispose(): void;
  findDup(text: string, vec: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike> | null, kind: number, scope: number, nowH: number, windowH: number, threshold: number): number | null;
  merge(keep: number, drop: number): boolean;
  mergeNear(threshold: number): [number, number][];

  recall(query: string, vec: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike> | null, p: CoreParams): CoreHit[];
  recallRaw(query: string, vec: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike> | null, block: Float64Array, scopes: Uint32Array): Float64Array;

```

One index inside the core: a flat list of items with BM25 tokens and vectors.

```ts
interface CoreItem {

  created: number;

  importance: number;
  kind: number;
  lastUsed: number;

```

Numbers of one item as the core keeps them.

```ts
class CoreMemory {
  constructor(lines?: string[], maxChars?: number);
  lines: string[];
  readonly maxChars: number;
  append(fact: string): boolean;
  remove(match: string): boolean;
  text(): string;
  static key(s: string): string;
}
```

Pinned facts that go into every prompt, capped in characters.

```ts
interface CoreParams {
  b?: number;
  cand?: number;
  k?: number;
  k1?: number;
  kinds?: number[];

  wImp?: number;

  wRel?: number;
}
```

Recall parameters; each one left out takes its default.

```ts
type CoreSource = { url: string | URL } | { bytes: ArrayBuffer | Uint8Array } | { base64: string }
```

Where `loadCore` gets the wasm: a URL, the bytes, or inlined base64.

```ts
interface EditPatch {
  entities?: string[];

  meta?: Record<string, unknown>;
  scope?: string;
  section?: string;
  text?: string;
}
```

The fields `Memory.edit` changes on one item; new text is embedded again.

```ts
interface Embedder {
  readonly dim: number;
  readonly id: string;
  embed(texts: string[]): Promise<Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike>[]>;
}
```

Anything that turns texts into vectors of one size: a transformers.js MiniLM (Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, weights Apache-2.0), bge-small (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5, weights MIT), a static model2vec table, or the hashed embedder below.

```ts
function estimateTokens(s: string): number
```

Estimates the tokens in a string as its length over `CHARS_PER_TOKEN`, rounded up.

```ts

```

An exchange worth keeping, as a note: null under 3 meaningful words; the reply cut at 160 characters on a word boundary.

```ts
function expandQuery(query: string, previous?: string, minChars?: number): string
```

The previous user turn goes in front of a short query (under 45 characters), so follow ups retrieve.

```ts

  version: 1;
```

FNV-1a 32 bit over the UTF-16 code units of s.


A gist without a model: the most frequent words and three samples.

```ts

```

Hashed unigram plus bigram embedder: FNV-1a picks a bucket and a sign, the vector is L2 normalized.

```ts

}
```

One recalled item with its final score and the core's per stage numbers.

```ts
const HIT_STRIDE: 11
```

```ts
class Memory {
  constructor(id: string, opts: OpenOptions, sink: MemorySink, notes: string[]);
  readonly core: CoreMemory;
  readonly id: string;
  readonly sink: MemorySink;
  readonly size: number;
  readonly status: Status;
  add(text: string, o?: AddOptions): Promise<{ id: number; merged: boolean }>;
  addExchange(said: string, reply: string, o?: AddOptions & { minWords?: number; replyChars?: number }): Promise<{ id: number; merged: boolean } | null>;
  all(): StoredItem[];
  assemble(o: { budgetTokens: number; core?: boolean; estimate?: (s: string) => number; fixed?: string[]; previous?: string; query?: string; recall?: RecallOptions; recent?: string[]; sections?: Section[]; select?: { dedup?: number; k?: number; maxChars?: number; perSection?: number }; summary?: string }): Promise<Assembled & { recalled: string[] }>;
  close(): void;
  compact(o?: CompactOptions): Promise<CompactReport>;
  consolidate(o?: { keep?: number; min?: number; scope?: string; summarize?: (texts: string[]) => Promise<string> }): Promise<{ folded: number; id: number } | null>;
  decay(floor?: number): Promise<number[]>;
  edit(id: number, patch: EditPatch): Promise<StoredItem | null>;

  export(): ExportData;
  get(id: number): StoredItem | undefined;
  import(data: ExportData, o?: { replace?: boolean }): Promise<number>;
  mergeNear(threshold?: number): Promise<[number, number][]>;
  persist(o?: { storage?: StorageLike | null }): Promise<boolean>;
  recall(q: string, o?: RecallOptions): Promise<Recall>;
  remember(fact: string): Promise<boolean>;
  remove(ids: number[]): Promise<void>;
  trace(r: Recall): RecallTrace;
  usage(o?: { storage?: StorageLike | null }): Promise<Usage>;
}
```

### @hackbuild/memory/seal

```ts

```

The cached session key for a lock, or undefined until deriveKey or makeLock ran.

```ts

```

The session key for a lock: derives once, checks the password and caches the key for the page's life.

```ts
function forgetKey(lock?: SealLock): void
```

Drop one lock's cached key, or every cached key.

```ts
function fromBase64(s: string): Bytes
```

Decodes base64 into bytes; the inverse of `toBase64`.

```ts

```

True when bytes start with the envelope magic.

