
A new lock for a password and its session key, cached.

```ts
function open<T = unknown>(key: SealKey, sealed: Uint8Array, context?: string): Promise<T>
```

Open a sealed JSON value.

```ts
function openBytes(key: SealKey, sealed: Uint8Array, context?: string): Promise<Bytes>
```

Open sealed bytes.

```ts
function seal(key: SealKey, value: unknown, context?: string): Promise<Bytes>
```

Seal a JSON value.

```ts
const SEAL_ITERATIONS: 210000
```

The default PBKDF2 SHA-256 iteration count.

```ts
const SEAL_OVERHEAD: 48
```

Envelope bytes added to every sealed payload: magic 4, salt 16, iv 12, tag 16.

```ts
function sealBytes(key: SealKey, plain: Uint8Array, context?: string): Promise<Bytes>
```

Seal bytes.

```ts
function sealedSink(inner: MemorySink, key: SealKey): MemorySink
```

Wrap a sink so every item, vector and kv value is sealed with `key` (from deriveKey or makeLock in "@hackbuild/memory/seal").

```ts
class SealError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string, code: "wrong-password" | "bad-lock" | "bad-envelope" | "rejected");
  readonly code: "wrong-password" | "bad-lock" | "bad-envelope" | "rejected";
}
```

The error sealing throws, with a `code`: wrong-password, bad-lock, bad-envelope or rejected.

```ts
class SealKey {
  readonly id: string;
}
```

A session key.

```ts
interface SealLock {
  algo: "pbkdf2-sha256";
  hash: string;
  iterations: number;
  salt: string;
}
```

The lock record: stored beside the sealed data, safe to show.

```ts
function toBase64(b: Uint8Array): string
```

Base64 without spreading the whole array onto the stack.

```ts
function verifyLock(password: string, lock: SealLock): Promise<boolean>
```

True when the password opens the lock.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { loadCore, open, hashedEmbedder, RecallConversation } from "@hackbuild/memory";
import { MEMORY_WASM_BASE64 } from "@hackbuild/memory/inline";

// load the wasm core from inlined base64, or pass { url } or { bytes }
const core = await loadCore({ base64: MEMORY_WASM_BASE64 });

// one memory per agent, kept in IndexedDB; the hashed embedder downloads nothing
const mem = await open("dog-1", { core, embed: hashedEmbedder(), scopes: ["self", "shared"] });
await mem.add("the mug goes on the shelf", { kind: "rule" });
await mem.add("they asked for the red ball", { kind: "episode", arousal: 0.4 });

// recall with the trace of every fused candidate
const r = await mem.recall("where does the mug go", { k: 6, score: "linear" });
console.log(r.hits.map((h) => h.item.text), r.trace.length);

// fit recall and recent turns into a token budget, then build the next prompt
const ctx = await mem.assemble({ budgetTokens: 1000, query: "mug", recent: ["user: tidy up"] });
const talk = new RecallConversation("you are a dog.");
console.log(talk.user("where is my mug?", ctx.recalled));
```

### from the concepts

```ts
const t = await mem.explain("where does the mug go");   // no strengthening
// t.how, t.terms [{ term, df, idf }], t.rows [{ rank, used, score, weight, parts, terms, ... }]
const last = mem.trace(recallFromTheLastReply);          // the same object for a past recall
await mem.edit(id, { text: "the mug goes on the top shelf" });
const report = await mem.compact();                      // decay, merge near duplicates, fold episodes
const u = await mem.usage();                             // counts, bytes (computed estimate), browser estimate
await mem.persist();                                     // asks the browser to keep the origin's storage
await mem.addExchange(userTurn, reply);                  // null under 3 meaningful words
await mem.recall(q, { skipSaid: userTurnsInView });
```

### from the concepts

```ts
import { makeLock, deriveKey, seal, sealedSink } from "@hackbuild/memory/seal";
const { lock } = await makeLock(password);         // keep lock beside the data
const key = await deriveKey(password, lock);       // once per session; wrong password throws
const mem = await open(id, { core, sink: sealedSink(await indexedDbSink(id), key) });
const file = await seal(key, workspaceJson, "file:workspace.json");
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- `open` needs a loaded core. Call `loadCore` first with `{ url }`, `{ bytes }` or `{ base64: MEMORY_WASM_BASE64 }` from `@hackbuild/memory/inline`, and pass it as `core`; on file:// use the base64 form, since the core has no threads and loads from bytes.
- Without `embed`, recall is keyword only and `status.mode` says `keyword`. `hashedEmbedder()` downloads nothing and matches shared words only; for real recall pass an embedder from `@hackbuild/embed`, whose weights carry their own licence.
- `recall` strengthens every hit and counts a use. Call `explain` when you want the trace of a query without changing the memory.
- When IndexedDB fails, `open` still resolves and the memory lives in a Map until the page closes. Read `status.notes` and tell the person instead of assuming it was saved.
- A lost password means sealed data is gone. `deriveKey` throws `SealError` with code `wrong-password` for a wrong one, and a plain row in a sealed store throws, so export a plain memory and import it into a sealed one.
- Inject recall with `injectRecall` or `RecallConversation`, which keep a fixed note in the system message and put recalled lines under the latest user message only. Do not put recall into the system prompt per turn, or the runtime loses its cached prefix.

## Errors this package throws

- `memory core: fetch <url> returned <status>` (the wasm URL did not load): check the URL, or load from bytes or `MEMORY_WASM_BASE64`
- `memory: no indexeddb in this context` (`indexedDbSink` called where there is no IndexedDB): pass `indexedDB`, or use `memorySink`
- `indexeddb failed (...). memory lasts until the page closes.` (a status note) (opening the database failed): expect a Map that empties on close; say so to the user
- `no embedder. recall is keyword only.` (a status note) (no embedder passed): pass an embedder for semantic recall
- `embedder failed (...). recall is keyword only.` (a status note) (the embedder threw): check the model load; recall keeps working on keywords
- `memory: unknown kind ...` (`edit` or `import` got a kind outside the eight): use episode, gist, lesson, fact, rule, lore, doc or note
- `memory: an edit cannot empty the text. forget the memory instead.` (`edit` with empty text): forget the item instead
- `memory: not a hackbuild-memory version 1 export` (`import` got other JSON): pass what `export()` gave
- `seal: no web crypto in this context. sealing needs a secure origin.` (http page or no Web Crypto): serve over https or localhost
- `seal: the lock record is not one this version reads.` (a changed or foreign lock record): use the lock `makeLock` gave
- `seal: empty password.` (empty password): ask for a password
- `seal: wrong password. there is no recovery.` (wrong password): ask again; a lost password cannot be recovered
- `seal: not a sealed envelope.` (the bytes are not sealed): pass what `seal` or `sealBytes` gave
- `seal: the envelope does not open. wrong key, or it was changed.` (wrong key, a changed byte, or another context): use the same key and context it was sealed with
- `memory: item <id> is not sealed. ...` (a plain row in a sealed store): export the plain memory and import it into the sealed one

---

# @hackbuild/models

> Describe each model once, with its runtime, device ladder, size and weight licence, and let a hub load the one that fits this machine.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/models/

## Purpose

- Holds model records: what a model provides, which runtime runs it, the device and dtype ladder to walk, quirks app code needs, its size with a source word, and its weight licence.
- Ships a catalogue of chat and starter records with pinned commits and file hashes for the Hugging Face repos they load.
- Says whether a record fits this machine (memory budget, WebGPU, shader-f16, storage) and why not, before any download.
- Runs a hub that routes a capability to a record, walks its ladder through a provider factory, keeps loaded models under a memory budget, and runs GPU work one job at a time.
- Suggests first visit defaults with one reason per field.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/models @hackbuild/devices @hackbuild/weights
```

Depends on @hackbuild/ai-env for the `Env` type. No peers. The quick start also installs @hackbuild/devices for the transformers.js provider and @hackbuild/weights for the file cache; the records and the hub need neither. No weights ship here; runtimes come in through the factories you register.

## Exports

### @hackbuild/models

```ts
interface Budget {
  mb: number;
  source: "proposed";
  why: string;
}
```

The largest model in MB this machine can give one model, with a lowercase reason.

```ts
function budgetFor(env: Env | undefined): Budget
```

The memory budget for one model on this machine, from `deviceMemoryGB` and the backend.

```ts
type Capability = KnownCapability | string & {}
```

Known names plus any string a later package adds.

```ts

```

The starter model records, each with its size source and weight licence.

```ts
type Censorship = "stock" | "uncensored" | "abliterated" | "unknown"
```

How the weights treat refusals, from the record's label or repo name; never guessed from substrings at run time.

```ts
function classifyError(e: unknown): ErrorKind
```

Name the failure so a ladder and a status line can act on it.

```ts
const CPU_CAP_MB: number
```

Cap on cpu: reply speed falls with size long before memory runs out.

```ts
function createHub(opts?: HubOptions): Hub
```

Creates a model hub over a registry, with the memory budget and licence notice from `opts`.

```ts
function createRegistry(initial?: readonly ModelRecord[]): Registry
```

Creates a registry holding `initial`, validating each record and setting the pinned revision of pinned repos.

```ts

  budget: Budget;

  patch: { device: "webgpu" | "wasm"; model: string | null; threads: number };
  reasons: Reason[];
}
```

A first visit's suggestion: the model, device and threads to set, a reason per field, a download worth offering, and the budget used.

```ts

  budget?: Budget;
  catalogue: readonly ModelRecord[];
  estimate?: StorageEstimate | null;
  provides?: Capability;
  stored?: readonly string[];
}
```

What `suggestDefaults` and `pickModel` choose from: the catalogue, stored ids, the storage estimate, the capability and an optional budget.

```ts
type Device = "webgpu" | "wasm" | "webgl" | "cpu" | "browser" | "remote"
```

Where a rung runs: webgpu, wasm, webgl, cpu, the browser's built in model, or a remote endpoint.

```ts
type ErrorKind = "runtime-mismatch" | "out-of-memory" | "f16" | "device-lost" | "unsupported-op" | "network" | "abort" | "unknown"
```

The kind of a load failure as `classifyError` names it.

```ts
interface ExclusiveOptions {

}
```

Priority and abort signal for a job in an exclusive queue.


Builds a runtime object for one rung.


How a record fits this machine, best first: "fits", then the reasons it does not, down to "cannot run here".

Whether a record fits this machine, from three checks: the ladder against the probe (webgpu and shader-f16), the memory budget against VRAM or download size, and the storage estimate against the download.

```ts
interface Hub {
  readonly env: Env | undefined;
  readonly registry: Registry;
  busy(id?: string): number;
  chain(name: string): <R>(fn: () => Promise<R>) => Promise<R>;
  exclusive<R>(resource: string, fn: () => Promise<R>, opts?: ExclusiveOptions): Promise<R>;
  frameMs(): number;
  onBusy(fn: (count: number) => void): () => void;
  onLoad(fn: (e: LoadEvent) => void): () => void;
  provide<T>(provider: Provider, factory: Factory<T>): void;
  release(l: Loaded): void;
  reportFrame(ms: number): void;
  residentMB(): number;
  run<T, R>(l: Loaded<T>, fn: (value: T) => Promise<R>, opts?: RunOptions): Promise<R>;
  status(): HubStatus[];
  unload(id: string): Promise<void>;
  use<T = unknown>(what: Capability | { id: string }, opts?: UseOptions): Promise<Loaded<T>>;
}
```

A model hub: routes a capability to a record, loads it through a provider factory, keeps loaded models under a memory budget and queues GPU work.

```ts

  readonly code: "abort" | "no-route" | "no-provider" | "budget" | "skipped";
}
```

The error the hub throws, with a `code` of "no-route", "no-provider", "budget", "abort" or "skipped".

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { probe } from "@hackbuild/ai-env";
import { loadTransformers, tjsProvider } from "@hackbuild/devices";
import { CATALOG, createHub, createRegistry, fitOf, pinnedSha } from "@hackbuild/models";
import { openWeightStore, transformersCache } from "@hackbuild/weights";

// what fits this machine, before any download
const env = await probe();
for (const r of CATALOG) console.log(r.id, fitOf(r, env).reason);
// transformers.js is imported at run time; its files go through the weight store under each record's licence
const licenceFor = (url: string) => CATALOG.find((r) => r.source?.repo && url.includes(`/${r.source.repo}/`))?.licence ?? null;
const cache = transformersCache(await openWeightStore(), { licenceFor, sha256For: pinnedSha });
const hub = createHub({ registry: createRegistry(CATALOG), env, budgetMB: 4000 });
hub.provide("tjs", tjsProvider({ runtime: loadTransformers(), cache }).factory);
// depth-anything-v2-small, weights Apache-2.0, on a picked photo: routed by capability, ladder walked, loaded once
const input = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("input[type=file]")!;
input.onchange = async () => {
  const depth = await hub.use<(image: string) => Promise<unknown>>("depth");
  console.log("runs on", depth.rung.device, await hub.run(depth, (pipe) => pipe(URL.createObjectURL(input.files![0]!))));
  hub.release(depth);
};
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- You import transformers.js, onnxruntime-web or WebLLM yourself and call it directly. Register a factory per provider with `hub.provide("tjs", tjsProvider({ runtime: loadTransformers(), cache }).factory)` from @hackbuild/devices, so the runtime comes in at run time, then ask the hub with `hub.use(capability)`.
- You write a record without `licence`, or hard code a licence string where the record has one. `createRegistry` refuses a record with no licence, and the hub states `record.licence` once before the first load; read the licence from the record.
- You call `hub.use` and never `hub.release`. A model stays resident until its refs reach zero, and with `budgetMB` set a new load throws `HubError` code `budget` when busy models fill it; release what you are done with.
- You run webgpu inference beside a render loop without a schedule. Call `hub.reportFrame(ms)` from the loop and pass `{ frameBudgetMs, minIntervalMs }` to `hub.run`, and catch code `skipped` when you pass `when: "skip"`.
- You walk `ortLadder()` with a fresh download per rung. Pair it with `store.once(ref)` from @hackbuild/weights so every rung reads one download, and pass `pinnedSha` as `sha256For` so pinned files are checked.
- You read `LadderError` as a single failure. `failures` lists one kind per rung: `runtime-mismatch` means pin the runtime, `out-of-memory` means a smaller model, `f16` means an f32 rung.

## Errors this package throws

- `no model for <capability> fits this device and budget` (HubError `no-route`) (no record provides it, or every one is over budget or has no rung for this env): add a record, raise `budgetMB`, or pass a smaller `size`
- `no factory for provider <p>; call hub.provide("<p>", ...)` (HubError `no-provider`) (no factory registered for the record's provider): register one, e.g. `tjsProvider(...).factory` from @hackbuild/devices
- `needs <mb> MB, <n> MB resident in use, budget <b> MB. release a model first.` (HubError `budget`) (busy models fill the budget): `hub.release` a model you are done with
- `<id>: run aborted while waiting for the frame budget`, `<id>: run aborted before it started` (HubError `abort`) (the signal aborted): none
- HubError `skipped` (`next start in <ms> ms`, `frames at <ms> ms over the <budget> ms budget`, `a run of this model is in flight`) (`when: "skip"` and the run was not due): drop the frame, or use `when: "wait"`
- `<id>: every rung failed: <device> <dtype> (<kind>), ...` (LadderError) (each rung threw; `failures` has the kinds): read the kinds: `runtime-mismatch` pins the runtime, `out-of-memory` picks a smaller model, `f16` needs an f32 rung
- `<id>: no rung fits this device` (LadderError) (`ladderFor` dropped every rung): use a record with a wasm rung, or a machine with WebGPU
- `<id>: every model reference names its weight licence` (RegistryError) (a record with no `licence`): add the licence
- `<id>: provides is empty`, `<id>: ladder is empty`, `<id>: vramMB needs its source word in vramSource`, `<id>: speed is one of ...`, `<id>: a verdict is one to four words, got "..."`, `<id>: censorship is one of ...` (RegistryError) (a malformed record): fix the field named
- `no stub for <capability>` (stub mode with no builder for that capability): add a builder to `stubFactory`

---

# @hackbuild/notes

> Turn a recording into notes, drum hits, a tempo and a MIDI file, in the tab.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/notes/

## Purpose

- Runs Spotify's Basic Pitch graph on tfjs through the models hub, framing the windows by hand.
- Decodes frame and onset posteriors into notes, then merges splits and drops harmonic ghosts.
- Finds kick, snare, hat and optional tom hits on the `@hackbuild/audio-dsp` wasm core.
- Estimates tempo and fits a beat grid to notes.
- Writes a General MIDI file with pitched and drum tracks.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/notes @hackbuild/ai-env @hackbuild/media
```

It depends on `@hackbuild/models` and `@hackbuild/audio-dsp`. The quick start also uses @hackbuild/ai-env to import tfjs and @hackbuild/media to decode the file. It has no peer dependencies: you pass tfjs 3.21.0 in at runtime through `tfjsPitchProvider`, so nothing of tfjs is bundled.

## Exports

```ts

```

Notes from posteriors: a note starts at an onset peak over onsetThresh (or a frame rise over the frame threshold when no onset fired), lasts while the frame posterior stays over frameThresh (gaps up to 2 frames bridged), and needs minFrames frames.

```ts
const DETAILS: { readonly loose: { readonly frameThresh: 0.22; readonly mergeGap: 0.08; readonly minDur: 0.03; readonly minFrames: 3; readonly onsetThresh: 0.35 }; readonly normal: { readonly frameThresh: 0.3; readonly mergeGap: 0.05; readonly minDur: 0.05; readonly minFrames: 5; readonly onsetThresh: 0.5 }; readonly tight: { readonly frameThresh: 0.35; readonly mergeGap: 0.03; readonly minDur: 0.06; readonly minFrames: 8; readonly onsetThresh: 0.6 } }
```

```ts
}
```

Runs B windows (B * BP_WINDOW samples) and returns frames and onsets, B * BP_ROWS * BP_BINS each.

```ts
function refineNotes(notes: readonly Note[], o?: { harmonics?: boolean; mergeGap?: number; minDur?: number; minVel?: number }): Note[]
```

Merge same pitch splits, drop octave, twelfth and double octave ghosts, drop dust.

```ts
function runPitch(m: PitchModel, mono: Float32Array, o?: { onProgress?: (f: number) => void; signal?: AbortSignal; yieldEvery?: () => Promise<void> }): Promise<{ frames: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike>[]; onsets: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike>[] }>
```

Frames and onsets (rows of 88) for a 22050 Hz mono signal.

```ts
function stubPitch(): PitchModel
```

A stub pitch model: A4 (bin 48) held through every window, onset on each window's first kept frame.

```ts
interface Tfjs {
  env(): { set(flag: string, v: unknown): void };
  loadGraphModel(url: string): Promise<{ dispose?(): void; execute(x: unknown, outs: string[]): { data(): Promise<Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike>>; dispose(): void }[] }>;
  ready(): Promise<void>;
  setBackend(name: string): Promise<boolean>;
  tensor(data: Float32Array, shape: number[], dtype?: string): { dispose(): void };
}
```

The parts of tfjs the provider touches.

```ts
function tfjsPitchProvider(opts: { runtime: () => Promise<Tfjs> }): Factory<PitchModel>
```

A models hub factory for the tfjs provider that loads the Basic Pitch graph and returns a PitchModel.

```ts
function writeMidi(tracks: readonly MidiTrack[], bpm: number): Uint8Array
```

`writeMidi` and `MidiTrack` from @hackbuild/audio-dsp, re-exported for MIDI out.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { importEsm } from "@hackbuild/ai-env";
import { decodeAudio } from "@hackbuild/media";
import { createHub } from "@hackbuild/models";
import { attachNotes, decodeNotes, DETAILS, refineNotes, runPitch, tfjsPitchProvider, writeMidi, type PitchModel, type Tfjs } from "@hackbuild/notes";

// a hub with the Basic Pitch record (weights Apache-2.0, stated by the hub from the record), tfjs 3.21.0 passed in at runtime
const hub = createHub();
attachNotes(hub);
hub.provide("tfjs", tfjsPitchProvider({ runtime: () => importEsm<Tfjs>("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@tensorflow/tfjs@3.21.0/+esm") }));
// a picked file at 22050 Hz, frame and onset posteriors from Basic Pitch, then notes and a MIDI file
const input = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("input[type=file]")!;
input.onchange = async () => {
  const { channels } = await decodeAudio(input.files![0]!, 22050);
  const m = await hub.use<PitchModel>("notes");
  const post = await hub.run(m, (pitch) => runPitch(pitch, channels[0]!, { onProgress: (f) => console.log(`${Math.round(f * 100)} percent`) }));
  hub.release(m);
  const notes = refineNotes(decodeNotes(post.frames, post.onsets, DETAILS.normal), DETAILS.normal);
  const mid = writeMidi([{ name: "bass", notes, program: 33 }], 120); // one bass track at 120 bpm
  console.log(`${notes.length} notes, ${mid.length} bytes`);
};
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- You import @tensorflow/tfjs at the top of the file. Pass a loader instead: `tfjsPitchProvider({ runtime: () => importEsm(url) })` with tfjs 3.21.0, and share that one tfjs instance across the page.
- You call `hub.use("notes")` before registering the runtime and get `no factory for provider tfjs`. Call `attachNotes(hub)` and `hub.provide("tfjs", tfjsPitchProvider(...))` first.
- You expect the Basic Pitch graph to go through @hackbuild/weights. tfjs `loadGraphModel` fetches it from the record's `source.url`, so it sits in the browser's HTTP cache, and the hub states the licence from the record on first load.
- You hand `runPitch` 44.1 kHz stereo. It takes 22050 Hz mono: decode with `decodeAudio(file, 22050)` from @hackbuild/media and pass one channel, and run it inside `hub.run(m, ...)` with `hub.release(m)` after.
- You decode with the basic-pitch library's settings and wonder why notes differ. `decodeNotes` is its own decoder; pass the same `DETAILS` preset to `decodeNotes` and `refineNotes`, and treat the AbortError `notes stopped` from your `signal` as a cancel.

## Errors this package throws

- `tfjs webgl backend did not start` (tfjs refused the webgl backend): the hub falls to the cpu rung; check that the tfjs you pass in has webgl
- `tfjs cpu backend did not start` (the tfjs you passed in has no cpu backend): pass the full tfjs 3.21.0 build
- `notes stopped` (AbortError) (the `signal` you passed aborted): expected; start again when you want notes
- `no factory for provider tfjs; call hub.provide("tfjs", ...)` (the hub has no tfjs factory): call `hub.provide("tfjs", tfjsPitchProvider(...))` before `hub.use("notes")`

---

# @hackbuild/speak

> You give it a reply as it streams and it speaks it through the first voice engine that works, telling you which character of your text the voice has reached.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/speak/

## Purpose

- Cuts a streaming reply into segments, with a short first clause so speech starts early, and synthesizes the next segment while the current one plays.
- Runs each segment through a chain of engines (the bellows voice, Pocket TTS, Kokoro, the system voice) and moves to the next one on a load error, a synth error or a watchdog trip.
- Plays PCM back to back on one AudioContext through one analyser, the single output for a level or lip sync driver.
- Reports progress, words and phonemes as offsets in your text, the same offsets the action tag parser in @hackbuild/structured uses.
- Renders a whole text offline to one buffer, a wav Blob and word timing json.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/speak
```

It depends on @hackbuild/ai-env, @hackbuild/models and @hackbuild/audio-dsp. No runtime is bundled: each engine loads its runtime from a loader you pass. bellows-voice and bellowsjs are optional peers; install them only for the bellows voice. kokoro-js and the Pocket build are fetched from a URL at run time and are not peers.

| subpath | runtime | pin |
|---|---|---|
| `.` (`bellowsEngine`) | bellows-voice, which imports bellowsjs (optional peers) | bellows-voice 0.8.0, bellowsjs 0.5.0 |
| `.` (`kokoroEngine`) | kokoro-js, from your URL | 1.2.1 |
| `.` (`pocketEngine`) | the Pocket TTS community browser build, from its Space | commit `d0c0c79` |
| `.` (`webSpeechEngine`) | the browser's speechSynthesis | none |

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { importEsm } from "@hackbuild/ai-env";
import { bellowsEngine, createSpeaker, renderedWav, webSpeechEngine, type BellowsVoiceModule } from "@hackbuild/speak";

// the browser lets audio play only after a click
document.querySelector("button")!.onclick = async () => {
  const ctx = new AudioContext();
  // the bellows voice first (a vocal tract model, no weights, code MIT), the system voice as fallback
  const bellows = bellowsEngine({ runtime: () => importEsm<BellowsVoiceModule>("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bellows-voice@0.8.0/dist/engine.js/+esm"), rng: Math.random });
  const speaker = createSpeaker({ ctx, engines: [bellows, webSpeechEngine()], onProgress: (p) => console.log("reached", p.offset, p.kind) });

  // feed a reply as it streams; the last call says it is complete
  speaker.feed("Hello there, this is the first clause.");
  speaker.feed("Hello there, this is the first clause. And here is the rest.", true);
  await speaker.done();

  // render a line offline and keep it as a wav
  const wav = renderedWav(await speaker.render("Saved to a file."));
  console.log("wav", wav.size, "bytes");
};
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- You import kokoro-js or bellows-voice at the top of the file. Pass a loader instead: `runtime: () => importEsm(url)` from @hackbuild/ai-env or `runtimeLoader` from @hackbuild/devices; this package never bundles a runtime.
- You add `kokoroEngine` and it refuses to load. Its phonemizer is GPL-3.0-or-later, so it loads only with `allowGplPhonemizer: true`; show `KOKORO_GPL_NOTICE` first, or use `bellowsEngine` and `webSpeechEngine`, which carry no GPL code.
- You call `bellowsEngine({ runtime })` without `rng`. The seed is one draw from the `rng` you inject, so pass one (`Math.random`, or a seeded Rng when you want the same audio twice).
- You make the AudioContext at page load and hear nothing. Make it inside a click handler and pass it to `createSpeaker({ ctx, engines })`, with `webSpeechEngine()` last in the chain as the fallback.
- You feed each new token on its own. `feed(text)` takes the whole visible reply so far, `feed(text, true)` marks it complete, and offsets in `onProgress` are in that text; call `stop()` for barge in and `dispose()` when the speaker goes away.
- You expect Kokoro or Pocket weights to go through @hackbuild/weights. Kokoro's come through kokoro-js and Pocket's from its pinned Space commit, each with its own fetch, and each engine states its weight licence through `onStatus` on first load.

## Errors this package throws

- `kokoro-js phonemizes with the phonemizer package, ... pass allowGplPhonemizer: true to load it.` (Kokoro without the GPL opt in): show `KOKORO_GPL_NOTICE` and pass `allowGplPhonemizer: true`, or use the bellows voice or the system voice
- `no speechSynthesis in this browser` (no Web Speech synthesis): put another engine in the chain
- `speech synthesis: <error>` (the platform voice failed): the chain moves on; check the system voice settings
- `pocket worker changed upstream; patches did not match` (a rewrite matched nothing in the worker): keep the pinned base, or pass `strictPatches: false` at your own risk
- `sentencepiece.js sha256 <got>, expected <want>` (the fetched script differs from the pinned hash): use the default base, or pass the hashes for your base
- `sentencepiece.js http <status>` (the script did not download): check the network or the base URL
- `pocket did not load in <n> s` (the worker sent no `loaded` in time): raise `loadTimeoutMs`, or let the chain move on
- `pocket is not loaded`, `kokoro is not loaded`, `bellows is not loaded` (synth or clone before load): let the speaker load the engine, or call `load` first
- `bellows-voice has no renderSpeech; pass bellows-voice 0.8.0 /engine, or renderSpeechFrom(parts) for 0.7.3` (the loader returned the wrong module): load `bellows-voice/engine` from 0.8.0, or wrap 0.7.3 with `renderSpeechFrom`
- `bellows-voice: no starter voice "<id>"` (the voice id is not in `BELLOWS_VOICES`): pick one of `BELLOWS_VOICES`
- `the system voice plays live and gives no audio to save. pick bellows or pocket to save a wav.` (`OfflineRenderError` code `native`: only native engines were left): show the message as is (`humanError` in @hackbuild/devices returns it unchanged) and offer a PCM engine
- `no voice could render this text. <reasons>.` (`OfflineRenderError` code `failed`: every PCM engine failed): read the reasons; `onSkip` reports each engine skipped
- `the engine returned no audio` (a render produced no samples): try another engine
- `render stopped` (AbortError) (your signal aborted the render): none needed

---

# @hackbuild/stems

> Split a song into drums, bass, other and vocals with htdemucs, in the tab.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/stems/

## Purpose

- Registers two htdemucs tiers with the models hub; onnxruntime-web runs them through `@hackbuild/devices`.
- Cuts a 44.1 kHz stereo mix into segments and joins the model output by its own overlap add with linear crossfades.
- Reports progress per segment and the realtime factor.
- Ships a stub separator for tests and pages without weights.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/stems @hackbuild/media @hackbuild/weights
```

It depends on `@hackbuild/models`, `@hackbuild/devices` and `@hackbuild/audio-dsp`. It has no peer dependencies: onnxruntime-web 1.27.0 loads at runtime through `loadOrt` in `@hackbuild/devices`, and you open the weight store with `@hackbuild/weights`.

## Exports

### @hackbuild/stems

```ts
function attachStems(hub: Hub): void
```

Add the htdemucs records to a models hub's registry.

```ts
function ortSeparator(m: OrtModel): Separator
```

Wrap an ort model as a Separator; refuses two input exports.

```ts
function overlapOf(r: ModelRecord): number
```

The overlap a record was tuned for (notes "overlap x"), else 0.25.

```ts
const SAMPLE_RATE: 44100
```

Sample rate the separator takes and returns, 44100 Hz.

```ts
const SEGMENT: 343980
```

Samples per model segment, 343980 (7.8 s at 44.1 kHz).

```ts
function separate(hub: Hub, left: Float32Array, right: Float32Array, o?: SeparateOptions): Promise<Stems>
```

Separate a 44.1 kHz stereo mix.

```ts
interface SeparateOptions {
  model?: string;
  now?: () => number;
  onProgress?: (p: { done: number; rtf: number; total: number }) => void;
  overlap?: number;
  schedule?: RunOptions;
  segment?: number;
  signal?: AbortSignal;
}
```

Options for `separate`: record id, overlap, segment length, abort signal, run schedule, progress callback and clock.

```ts
interface Separator {
  separate(left: Float32Array, right: Float32Array): Promise<{ data: ArrayLike<number>; samples: number; tracks: number }>;
}
```

A separator takes one stereo segment of SEGMENT samples, returns [tracks][2][SEGMENT] flat.

```ts
interface Stems {
  model: string;
  rtf: number;
  stems: Record<Track, { left: Float32Array; right: Float32Array }>;
}
```

What `separate` returns: left and right channels per stem, the realtime factor and the record id used.

```ts
const STEMS_RECORDS: ModelRecord[]
```

The models hub records for htdemucs (weights MIT): fp16 weights at 10 percent overlap, fp32 at 40 percent.

```ts
function stemsStubs(): Record<string, (r: ModelRecord) => unknown>
```

Stub builders for the models hub: the `stems` capability returns `stubSeparator()`.

```ts
function stubSeparator(): Separator
```

Stub separator: every stem is a quarter of the mix.

```ts
type Track = typeof TRACKS[number]
```

One stem name from TRACKS.

```ts
const TRACKS: readonly ["drums", "bass", "other", "vocals"]
```

The four stems in model output order: drums, bass, other, vocals.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { loadOrt, ortProvider } from "@hackbuild/devices";
import { decodeAudio } from "@hackbuild/media";
import { createHub } from "@hackbuild/models";
import { attachStems, separate } from "@hackbuild/stems";
import { openWeightStore } from "@hackbuild/weights";

// a hub with the htdemucs records (weights MIT, stated from the record); onnxruntime-web loads at runtime, weights go through the store
const hub = createHub();
attachStems(hub);
hub.provide("ort", ortProvider({ runtime: loadOrt(), store: await openWeightStore() }).factory);

// a picked song at 44.1 kHz stereo, separated on the fast tier with progress per segment
const input = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("input[type=file]")!;
input.onchange = async () => {
  const { channels } = await decodeAudio(input.files![0]!, 44100);
  const left = channels[0]!;
  const { stems, rtf } = await separate(hub, left, channels[1] ?? left, { model: "htdemucs-fast", onProgress: (p) => console.log(`segment ${p.done} of ${p.total}`) });
  console.log(`vocals ${stems.vocals.left.length} samples, ${rtf.toFixed(2)}x realtime`);
};
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- You import onnxruntime-web at the top of the file. Pass `loadOrt()` from @hackbuild/devices as the `runtime` of `ortProvider` and register its `.factory` with `hub.provide("ort", ...)` after `attachStems(hub)`; this package bundles no runtime.
- You fetch the htdemucs graph yourself. `ortProvider({ runtime, store })` fetches it once through `store.once` on the @hackbuild/weights store you open with `openWeightStore()`, and the hub states the licence from the record on first load.
- You pass a 48 kHz or mono buffer to `separate`. It takes 44.1 kHz (`SAMPLE_RATE`) left and right channels: decode with `decodeAudio(file, 44100)` from @hackbuild/media and pass the left channel twice for a mono file.
- You load another htdemucs ONNX export and get `this htdemucs export needs a spectrogram input`. Only waveform only exports with one input run here; use the `htdemucs-fast` or `htdemucs-slow` records from StemSplitio.
- You expect `htdemucs-slow` to be a bigger model. Every tier is the same network and overlap is the speed control: pass `overlap` from 0 to 0.6, lower is faster, and treat the AbortError `separation stopped` from your `signal` as a cancel.

## Errors this package throws

- `this htdemucs export needs a spectrogram input; use a waveform only export (StemSplitio htdemucs-onnx)` (the graph has two inputs): use the StemSplitio waveform only export
- `this model has no time domain output tensor` (no output of shape [1, tracks, 2, samples]): use the StemSplitio export
- `this model returns N stems, the pipeline expects 4` (the graph is not a four stem model): use a four stem htdemucs export
- `separation stopped` (AbortError) (the `signal` you passed aborted): expected; start again when you want stems
- `no factory for provider ort; call hub.provide("ort", ...)` (the hub has no ort factory): call `hub.provide("ort", ortProvider(...).factory)`

---

# @hackbuild/structured

> Get a tool decision or tagged text out of a small model in the tab, in the format that model and runtime can keep to.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/structured/

## Purpose

- Asks a `@hackbuild/chat` engine for one tool decision in five modes: constrained JSON, a Hermes prompt, native tools, inline tags, or THOUGHT and ACTION lines.
- Sanitizes JSON Schemas for grammar mode and falls back from a strict schema to a loose one, then to free text.
- Repairs broken JSON and reads the tool call shapes small models drift to.
- Stops a run on repeated parse failures, loops, garbage replies or too many pushbacks.
- Parses inline tags from a stream with their offsets in the visible text, and reads line tagged formats.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/structured @hackbuild/chat
```

It depends on `@hackbuild/chat`, which installs with it. No peers; the runtime that runs the model is the one your chat engine loads.

## Exports

### @hackbuild/structured

```ts
interface AgentSchemaOptions {
  respond?: boolean;
  thought?: boolean;
}
```

Whether the agent schemas add the `respond_to_user` pseudo tool and ask for a thought first.

```ts
function buildAgentSchema(tools: readonly ToolSpec[], o?: AgentSchemaOptions): JsonSchema
```

Root anyOf, one variant per tool: { thought, tool_call: { name: enum[one], arguments } }.

```ts
function buildLooseAgentSchema(tools: readonly ToolSpec[], o?: AgentSchemaOptions): JsonSchema
```

One variant with an enum over every tool name and arguments of any object.

```ts
function call(chat: ChatEngine, messages: readonly ChatMessage[], o: CallOptions): Promise<Decision>
```

Ask a chat engine for one tool decision in the chosen mode, with the strict to loose to text fallbacks in constrained mode.

```ts
interface CallOptions {
  guards?: Guards;
  maxTokens?: number;
  mode?: Mode | "auto";
  quirks?: CallQuirks;
  respond?: boolean;
  signal?: AbortSignal;
  temperature?: number;
  tools: readonly ToolSpec[];
}
```

The tools, mode, quirks, guards and sampling settings for one `call`.

```ts
interface CallQuirks {
  maxTokensAction?: number;
  nativeTools?: boolean;
  toolCallTags?: boolean;
}
```

What a runtime is known to do: native tool calls, `<tool_call>` tags, and a token cap for actions.

```ts
function createGuards(o?: GuardOptions): Guards
```

Make guards with the defaults 3 parse failures, the same call 3 times in the last 6, 2 garbage replies in a row, and 3 pushbacks.

```ts
function createTagParser(g: TagGrammar): TagParser
```

Make a tag parser for the keys, synonyms and line keys you give.

```ts
interface Decision {
  fallback: "none" | "loose" | "text";
  mode: Mode;
  raw: string;
  say: string;
  stop: StopReason | null;
  thought: string;
  tool: { args: Record<string, unknown>; name: string } | null;
}
```

The result of one `call`: the mode used, thought, tool and arguments, text for the user, raw reply, fallback taken and any guard that tripped.

```ts
function fingerprint(name: string, args: unknown): string
```

Stable fingerprint of a call: name plus arguments with sorted keys.

```ts
function grabCode(value: string): { code: string; lang: string | null }
```

The body of a fenced block when there is one, else the text trimmed.

```ts
interface GuardOptions {
  garbage?: { consecutive: number; ratio: number };
  parseFails?: number;
  pushbacks?: number;
  repeat?: { count: number; window: number };
}
```

Turn guards for small models: stop after 3 parse failures, when the same call repeats 3 times in the last 6, or after 2 garbage replies in a row; cap pushbacks at 3.

```ts
interface Guards {
  readonly stopped: StopReason | null;
  call(name: string, args: unknown): StopReason | null;
  parseFail(): StopReason | null;
  pushback(): StopReason | null;
  reply(text: string): StopReason | null;
  reset(): void;
}
```

Counters over one agent run that return a `StopReason` when a limit is reached.

```ts
function hermesToolPrompt(tools: readonly ToolSpec[]): string
```

The system text that lists the tools in `<tools>` and asks for one `<tool_call>` reply, in the Hermes and Qwen format.

```ts
function jsonCharRatio(text: string): number
```

Share of characters that are JSON punctuation.

```ts
function keywordActions(text: string, synonyms: Record<string, string>, o?: { max?: number; maxRepeat?: number }): string[]
```

Keyword fallback when no ACTION line parses (vision sandbox ACTION_SYNS): words to actions, capped.

```ts
interface LinesOptions {
  tags: readonly string[];
}
```

Line tagged formats: THOUGHT / ACTION ReAct with multi line bodies (PATH, CONTENT, CODE), the vision sandbox's short Thought / Action, and the three line SAW / THOUGHT / GOAL cortex.

```ts
function looksLikeGarbage(text: string, ratio?: number): boolean
```

True when a reply is empty, repeats a short run six times or more, or has a JSON punctuation share above `ratio`.

```ts
type Mode = "constrained" | "prompt" | "native" | "tags" | "lines"
```

How `call` asks the model for a tool: constrained JSON, a Hermes prompt, native tools, inline tags, or THOUGHT and ACTION lines.

```ts
function parseAction(value: string, known?: readonly string[]): ParsedAction | null
```

Parse an ACTION value: `look(mug)`, `look mug`, `pick_up(red mug, table)`, `["look", "mug"]`.

```ts
interface ParsedAction {
  args: string[];
  name: string;
  raw: string;
}
```

An action read from an ACTION line: the tool name, its positional arguments, and the text as written.

```ts
function parseLines(text: string, o: LinesOptions): Record<string, string>
```

First value per tag, keyed by the tag as given in `tags`.

```ts
function parseLooseJSON(raw: string): unknown
```

Parse after repair; then the balanced `{...}` spans, the one that ends last and starts first tried first, at most 64 of them.

```ts
function parseToolDecision(raw: unknown): ToolDecision | null
```

Read `{ thought, tool_call: { name, arguments } }` and the shapes small models drift to: arguments as a JSON string (double encoded), `tool` or `action` for the name, `args` or `parameters` for the arguments, and a flat `{ name, arguments }`.

```ts
function pickMode(chat: ChatEngine, q?: CallQuirks): Mode
```

The mode `auto` uses: native when the quirks and engine allow tools, constrained when the engine takes schemas, prompt for tool call tag models, else lines.

```ts
function repairJSON(raw: string): string
```

Close what the model left open and drop trailing commas.

```ts
function resolveValue(value: string, vocab: readonly string[], synonyms?: Record<string, string>): string | null
```

Resolve a value against a vocabulary: exact, synonym, substring, then token overlap.

```ts
const RESPOND: "respond_to_user"
```

The name of the pseudo tool a model calls to answer the user in words.

```ts
function sanitizeSchema(schema: JsonSchema, opts?: { strip?: readonly string[] }): JsonSchema
```

Copy a schema without the keywords grammar compilers refuse, keeping property names, and add a root `type: "object"` when the root has no type.

```ts
type StopReason = "parse-fails" | "repeat" | "garbage" | "pushbacks"
```

Which guard tripped: too many parse failures, a repeated call, garbage replies or too many pushbacks.

```ts
const STRIPPED_KEYWORDS: readonly ["minItems", "maxItems", "multipleOf", "$schema", "$id", "examples", "default", "title", "minLength", "maxLength", "pattern"]
```

The JSON Schema keywords `sanitizeSchema` removes, because grammar compilers refuse them.

```ts
interface Tag {
  at: number;
  key: string;
  raw: string;
  value: string;
}
```

One tag found in model text: its key, resolved value, the text as written, and its offset in the visible text.

```ts
interface TagGrammar {
  keys: Record<string, readonly string[] | null>;
  lineKeys?: readonly string[];
  maxTag?: number;
  plain?: boolean;
  stripUnresolved?: boolean;
  synonyms?: Record<string, string>;
}
```

Streaming inline tag parser.

```ts
interface TagParser {
  end(): { tags: Tag[]; text: string };
  feed(chunk: string): { tags: Tag[]; text: string };
  parse(text: string): { tags: Tag[]; text: string };
  strip(text: string): string;
}
```

A streaming tag parser: `feed` chunks, `end` the stream, `parse` whole text, or `strip` text for speech.

```ts
interface ToolDecision {
  args: Record<string, unknown>;
  name: string;
  thought: string;
}
```

A tool choice read from model JSON: the thought, the tool name and its arguments object.

```ts
function withRespond(tools: readonly ToolSpec[], on?: boolean): ToolSpec[]
```

The tool list with `respond_to_user` added at the end, unless it is there already or `on` is false.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { scripted } from "@hackbuild/chat";
import { call, createGuards } from "@hackbuild/structured";

// any ChatEngine from @hackbuild/chat fits; the scripted one runs no model and takes schemas
const chat = scripted({ replies: ['{"thought": "it is dark", "tool_call": {"name": "lamp", "arguments": {"state": "on"}}}'] });
const tools = [{ name: "lamp", description: "switch the lamp", parameters: { type: "object", properties: { state: { type: "string" } } } }];

// guards stop a run after repeated parse failures, loops or garbage
const guards = createGuards();

// one tool decision; "auto" picks constrained JSON for an engine that takes schemas
const d = await call(chat, [{ role: "user", content: "it is dark in here" }], { tools, mode: "auto", guards });
console.log(d.mode, d.tool?.name, d.tool?.args, d.say, d.stop);
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- This package loads no runtime and no weights. Pass a `ChatEngine` from `@hackbuild/chat` to `call`; the runtime and the weight licence belong to that engine.
- `call` does not throw on a reply it cannot parse. Check `d.tool`, which is `null` when nothing usable came back, and `d.fallback`, which says `loose` or `text` when the strict schema was refused.
- Create one `createGuards()` per run and pass the same object to every `call`. Stop the loop when `d.stop` is set; it names `parse-fails`, `repeat`, `garbage` or `pushbacks`, and `guards.reset()` starts over.
- `mode: "auto"` picks native only when you pass `quirks.nativeTools` and the engine has tools, then constrained when the engine takes schemas, then prompt with `quirks.toolCallTags`, else lines. Pass the model's quirks or name the mode.
- A reply with no tool becomes the `respond_to_user` tool with `{ message }`, and its text is in `d.say`. Handle that tool name instead of treating it as a missing tool, or pass `respond: false` to leave it out.

## Errors this package throws

- `stop: "parse-fails"` (3 replies in a run held no tool the parser read): try another mode, or a larger model
- `stop: "repeat"` (the same call 3 times in the last 6): end the run, or tell the model the result already came back
- `stop: "garbage"` (2 replies in a row were mostly JSON punctuation or one repeated run): end the run and reset the guards
- `stop: "pushbacks"` (more than 3 pushbacks): end the run
- `fallback: "loose"` (the runtime refused the strict schema): expected on some grammars; the loose schema allows any tool name
- `fallback: "text"` (both schemas were refused and free text was parsed): use prompt or lines mode for this engine
- `tool: null` (nothing usable came back): count it as a parse failure and ask again

---

# @hackbuild/transcribe

> Turn a recording into timed text in the tab, with Whisper or Moonshine behind a front end that finds quiet speech and drops the lines a model writes over silence.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/transcribe/

## Purpose

- Cleans and levels 16 kHz audio, gates out the silence and packs the speech into reels of at most 26 s, with a source map back to file time.
- Runs one Whisper or Moonshine call per reel through the models hub, then drops watermark, outro, loop and repeat lines the model wrote over silence.
- Cuts live microphone blocks into segments and wraps the browser's own speech recognizer.
- Queues dropped files, offers the languages a model takes, and draws a level rail you can regate without a model run.
- Writes txt, srt, vtt and json, a zip of them with a manifest, and reads json, srt and vtt back for editing.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/transcribe @hackbuild/media @hackbuild/weights
```

It depends on @hackbuild/ai-env, @hackbuild/models, @hackbuild/devices and @hackbuild/audio-dsp, and has no peers. transformers.js is not a dependency: `loadTransformers()` from @hackbuild/devices imports the pinned build (`@huggingface/transformers@4.3.2`) at run time. Use @hackbuild/media to decode files and @hackbuild/weights to cache weights.

## Exports

### @hackbuild/transcribe

```ts
function acceptsFile(f: Pick<FileLike, "name" | "type">): boolean
```

```ts
  gain: number;
  noise: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike> | null;
  sig: Float32Array;
  stats: { density: number; dur: number; forced: boolean; gainDb: number; loudDb: number; noiseDb: number; snrDb: number; speechDb: number; thrDb: number };
```


The zip of every document: txt, srt, vtt and json per source, and `manifest.json` first.

```ts
function cleanup<T extends Seg>(segs: readonly T[], vad: readonly Region[], on?: boolean, sampleRate?: number): { dropped: Dropped[]; kept: T[] }
```

The phantom text filter: splits lines into kept and dropped, using the gate's speech regions to tell a real outro from one written over silence.


```ts
function defaultTranscribeId(webgpu: boolean): string
```

```ts
interface Dropped extends Seg {
  confidence?: number;
  edited?: boolean;
  end: number;
  speaker?: string;
  start: number;
  text: string;
  why: DropReason;
  words?: Word[];
}
```

A line the phantom filter dropped, with the reason.

```ts
type DropReason = "empty" | "watermark" | "outro" | "phantom" | "loop" | "repeat"
```

```ts
function englishOnly(model: string | Pick<ModelRecord, "notes" | "source">): boolean
```

True for a record or repo id that only takes english: a note says so, or the id ends in `.en`.

```ts
interface FileLike {
  name: string;
```


Live segmentation: audio arrives in blocks, is decimated to 16 kHz, and is cut into segments either when a gate closes for 500 ms (squelch mode), at a fixed window (8 s with the squelch off, 2 to 12 s in spirit box mode), or at 24 s, since Whisper pads to 30 s.

```ts
  flush(): void;

}
```

Cuts live audio blocks into 16 kHz speech segments, by the gate closing or by a fixed window, and hands each to `onSegment`.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { probe } from "@hackbuild/ai-env";
import { loadDsp } from "@hackbuild/audio-dsp";
import { AUDIO_DSP_WASM_BASE64 } from "@hackbuild/audio-dsp/inline";
import { loadTransformers, tjsProvider } from "@hackbuild/devices";
import { decodeAudio } from "@hackbuild/media";
import { createHub } from "@hackbuild/models";
import { asSrt, attachTranscribe, defaultTranscribeId, toMono, transcribe, TRANSCRIBE_RECORDS } from "@hackbuild/transcribe";
import { openWeightStore, transformersCache } from "@hackbuild/weights";

// a hub with the whisper and moonshine records; transformers.js comes in through the devices loader, weights through the store with each record's licence
const hub = createHub({ env: await probe() });
attachTranscribe(hub);
hub.provide("tjs", tjsProvider({ runtime: loadTransformers(), cache: transformersCache(await openWeightStore(), { licenceFor: (url) => TRANSCRIBE_RECORDS.find((r) => r.source.modelId && url.includes(r.source.modelId))?.licence ?? null }) }).factory);
const dsp = await loadDsp({ base64: AUDIO_DSP_WASM_BASE64 });
const input = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("input[type=file]")!;
input.onchange = async () => { // 16 kHz mono from the picked file, then whisper: large-v3-turbo with webgpu, base.en without
  const { channels } = await decodeAudio(input.files![0]!, 16000);
  const out = await transcribe(hub, dsp, toMono(channels), { model: defaultTranscribeId(hub.env?.webgpu ?? false), language: "en" });
  console.log(asSrt(out.segments), out.dropped.length, "lines dropped");
};
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- You import @huggingface/transformers at the top of the file. Pass `loadTransformers()` from @hackbuild/devices as the `runtime` of `tjsProvider` and register it with `hub.provide("tjs", ...)` after `attachTranscribe(hub)`; this package bundles no runtime.
- You let transformers.js fetch weights on its own. Pass `cache: transformersCache(store, { licenceFor })` from @hackbuild/weights to `tjsProvider`, with `licenceFor` reading `licence` off the matching record in `TRANSCRIBE_RECORDS`, never a string you type.
- You hand `transcribe` a decoded buffer at 44.1 or 48 kHz. It takes 16 kHz mono: decode with `decodeAudio(file, 16000)` from @hackbuild/media, then `toMono(channels)`, and pass the audio-dsp core from `loadDsp` as the second argument.
- You pass `task` or `language` for an english only model such as `whisper-base.en`. transformers.js rejects them; `transcribe` already leaves them out for those records, and `languagesFor(record, wanted)` tells you the language is locked.
- You hard code a model id. `defaultTranscribeId(webgpu)` gives large-v3-turbo with a webgpu adapter and base.en without; a stop through `signal` rejects with an AbortError whose message is `transcription stopped`; treat it as a cancel and show no error.

## Errors this package throws

- `<name> is not a transcript this tool reads. drop a json, srt or vtt file.` (`importTranscript` got another kind of file): drop a json, srt or vtt
- `this is not a vtt file. it must start with WEBVTT.` (a vtt without its header): add the WEBVTT line or export again
- `no cues in this srt file. each cue needs a line like 00:00:01,000 --> 00:00:02,000.` (srt with no cue times): fix the cue time lines
- `this json file does not parse. it may be cut short.` (broken json): export the json again
- `this json file has no segments list. import a transcript json exported from this tool.` (json from elsewhere): use json from `asJson` or `toJson`
- `"<s>" is not a time stamp.` (`parseStamp` got a bad stamp): use hh:mm:ss,mmm, hh:mm:ss.mmm or mm:ss.mmm
- `no web speech recognition in this browser. use a whisper model.` (no SpeechRecognition): check `webSpeechAvailable()` first and offer Whisper
- `transcription stopped` (AbortError) (the signal aborted): nothing; the model is released
- `could not decode <name>. convert it to wav or mp3 and drop it again.` (the queue's decoder failed): convert the file
- `the run failed: <message>. press run to try again.` (the queue's run threw): read the message, then retry the job
- `bad input rate <n>` / `sample rates must be positive` (RangeError) (`toSixteenK` or `StreamResampler` got a rate of 0 or less): pass the AudioContext rate

---

# @hackbuild/vision

> Get depth, objects, masks, landmarks and captions from an image or a webcam in your tab, through one models hub that shares the GPU with your scene.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/vision/

## Purpose

- Runs depth, detection, segmentation, face, hand and pose landmarks, captions and questions through the `@hackbuild/models` hub.
- Falls through a chain of landmark models when one fails, and says which failed.
- Keeps image embeddings so later point and box prompts on the same image skip the encoder, and gives mask operations and PNG, SVG and run length export.
- Runs depth in a worker and schedules calls around your render loop so the scene keeps its frames.
- Turns face and hand landmarks into steady presence, expression and gesture signals for a character.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/vision
```

It depends on [@hackbuild/ai-env](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/ai-env/llms.md), [@hackbuild/models](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/models/llms.md), [@hackbuild/devices](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/devices/llms.md) and [@hackbuild/weights](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/weights/llms.md). The model runtimes are not bundled; they load at run time from pinned URLs, and each is optional:

| subpath | runtime | pin |
|---|---|---|
| `.` (depth, segment, caption, ask) | @huggingface/transformers, through `loadTransformers` from @hackbuild/devices | 4.3.2 |
| `.` (detect, segment.person, landmarks) | @mediapipe/tasks-vision, through `loadTasksVision` | 1.2.3 |
| `.` (YOLO, optional) | onnxruntime-web, through `loadOrt` from @hackbuild/devices | 1.27.0 |
| `.` (face fallback, optional) | face-api.js, a runtime you pass to `faceApiProvider` | unknown |

```ts
function depth(hub: Hub, image: unknown, o?: CallOptions): Promise<DepthMap>
```

A depth map of an image from the routed depth model (Depth Anything V2 small by default), loaded and released through the hub.

```ts
const DEPTH_WORKER_SOURCE: "\nlet pipe = null;\nlet RawImage = null;\nconst norm = (out) => {\n  const pd = out.predicted_depth;\n  if (pd && pd.data && pd.dims && pd.dims.length >= 2) {\n    const h = pd.dims[pd.dims.length - 2], w = pd.dims[pd.dims.length - 1];\n    let mn = Infinity, mx = -Infinity;\n    for (let i = 0; i < w * h; i++) { const v = pd.data[i]; if (v < mn) mn = v; if (v > mx) mx = v; }\n    const inv = mx > mn ? 1 / (mx - mn) : 0;\n    const data = new Float32Array(w * h);\n    for (let i = 0; i < w * h; i++) data[i] = (pd.data[i] - mn) * inv;\n    return { width: w, height: h, data, range: [mn, mx] };\n  }\n  const d = out.depth;\n  if (!d) throw new Error(\"depth pipeline returned neither predicted_depth nor depth\");\n  const ch = d.channels || 1;\n  const data = new Float32Array(d.width * d.height);\n  for (let i = 0; i < data.length; i++) data[i] = d.data[i * ch] / 255;\n  return { width: d.width, height: d.height, data, range: [0, 255] };\n};\nself.onmessage = async (ev) => {\n  const m = ev.data;\n  if (!m || typeof m !== \"object\" || !(\"op\" in m)) return;\n  try {\n    if (m.op === \"load\") {\n      let tjs = null, err = null;\n      const load = self.__import || ((u) => import(u));\n      for (const u of m.urls) { try { tjs = await load(u); break; } catch (e) { err = e; } }\n      if (!tjs) throw err || new Error(\"no transformers.js url loaded\");\n      RawImage = tjs.RawImage;\n      pipe = await tjs.pipeline(\"depth-estimation\", m.modelId, { device: m.device, dtype: m.dtype, revision: m.revision });\n      self.postMessage({ id: m.id, ok: true });\n    } else if (m.op === \"run\") {\n      if (!pipe) throw new Error(\"depth worker is not loaded\");\n      const img = new RawImage(new Uint8ClampedArray(m.data), m.width, m.height, 4);\n      const d = norm(await pipe(img));\n      self.postMessage({ id: m.id, ok: true, depth: d }, [d.data.buffer]);\n    }\n  } catch (e) {\n    self.postMessage({ id: m.id, ok: false, error: String((e && e.message) || e) });\n  }\n};\n"
```

The worker's source.

```ts
function depthFromOutput(out: { depth?: RawImageLike; predicted_depth?: TensorLike }): DepthMap
```

Normalize a depth pipeline result.

```ts
function depthLoader(ctx: TjsLoadContext): Promise<DepthModel>
```

The transformers.js loader for depth records: a depth-estimation pipeline wrapped as a DepthModel.

```ts
interface DepthMap {
  data: Float32Array;
  height: number;
  range: [min: number, max: number];
  width: number;
}
```

A depth map: width, height, 0 to 1 per pixel with larger nearer, and the raw output range.

```ts
interface DepthModel {
  dispose?(): unknown;
  estimate(image: unknown): Promise<DepthMap>;
}
```

A loaded depth model: `estimate` returns a DepthMap for an image.

```ts
function depthToRgba(d: { data: Float32Array; height: number; width: number }): Uint8ClampedArray
```

A depth map as an 8 bit grey RGBA buffer, for a canvas or a PNG (store it as a PNG data URL to keep it with a design).


```ts
interface DepthWorker {

}
```

```ts

  urls: readonly string[];
}
```

```ts
interface Loop {
  readonly busy: boolean;
  readonly lastLatencyMs: number;
  readonly running: boolean;
  readonly steps: number;

}
```

A running loop: `stop`, whether it runs or is busy, the last step's latency and the step count.

```ts
interface LoopOptions<T> {
  interval?: (lastLatencyMs: number) => number;
  now?: () => number;
  onBusy?: () => void;
  onError?: (e: unknown) => void;
  onResult?: (r: T, latencyMs: number) => void;
  schedule?: (fn: () => void) => void;
  signal?: AbortSignal;
  step: (tick: number) => Promise<T>;
}
```

A perception loop beside a render loop: one step at a time (a busy guard), each step started no sooner than `interval(lastLatency)` after the previous one began (an adaptive cadence or a fixed period), stopped by `stop()` or an abort signal.

```ts

  data: Uint8Array;

}
```


Inside pixels (128 and up).


Grow by a disc of radius `r` pixels (expand).


Shrink by a disc of radius `r` pixels; the image border does not count as outside.


Soft edges: a gaussian of radius `r` with sigma r / 2 (a smooth without a rethreshold), edges clamped.

Pixels inside both masks, the smaller value of each.

Keep only the largest connected piece (8 connected by default).

Outline loops along pixel edges, inside on the right going clockwise in image space (y down); holes run the other way.

```ts
}
```

COCO style uncompressed run length: column major, the first run counts outside pixels.
