## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { probe } from "@hackbuild/ai-env";
import { loadTransformers, tjsProvider } from "@hackbuild/devices";
import { createHub } from "@hackbuild/models";
import { attachVision, caption, depth, detect, loadTasksVision, mediapipeProvider } from "@hackbuild/vision";

// one hub; transformers.js and MediaPipe tasks-vision load at run time from pinned urls
const tjs = tjsProvider({ runtime: loadTransformers() });
const hub = createHub({ env: await probe() });
attachVision(hub, tjs); // the vision records plus the transformers.js loaders
hub.provide("tjs", tjs.factory);
hub.provide("mediapipe", mediapipeProvider({ runtime: loadTasksVision() }));

// each call loads its model on first use, runs it under the gpu lock, and releases it
const video = document.querySelector("video")!;
video.srcObject = await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({ video: true }); // the webcam
await video.play();
const map = await depth(hub, video); // Depth Anything V2 small, weights Apache-2.0
const boxes = await detect(hub, video, { scoreThreshold: 0.4 }); // MediaPipe EfficientDet lite0, Apache-2.0
const line = await caption(hub, video); // SmolVLM 256M, Apache-2.0
console.log(map.width, map.height, boxes.map((b) => b.label), line);
```

### from the concepts

```ts
import { createHub, stubFactory } from "@hackbuild/models";
import { tjsProvider, loadTransformers } from "@hackbuild/devices";
import { attachVision, mediapipeProvider, loadTasksVision, visionStubs, depth, detect, landmarks, caption } from "@hackbuild/vision";

const tjs = tjsProvider({ runtime: loadTransformers() });
const hub = createHub({ env, stub: new URLSearchParams(location.search).has("stub") });
attachVision(hub, tjs);                    // records plus transformers.js loaders
hub.provide("tjs", tjs.factory);
hub.provide("mediapipe", mediapipeProvider({ runtime: loadTasksVision() }));
hub.provide("stub", stubFactory(visionStubs()));

const map = await depth(hub, imageOrCanvas);           // 0 to 1, larger is nearer, plus the raw range
const boxes = await detect(hub, video, { scoreThreshold: 0.4 });
const face = await landmarks(hub, "face", video);      // falls through the chain, face.failures says what failed
const line = await caption(hub, frame);                // serialized on the vlm chain
```

### from the concepts

```ts
hub.onBusy((n) => (pill.textContent = n ? "model busy" : ""));
await depth(hub, frame, { size: "tiny", schedule: { minIntervalMs: 1200, frameBudgetMs: 20, when: "skip" } });
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- You import `@huggingface/transformers` or `@mediapipe/tasks-vision` at the top of your file. Pass the loaders instead: `tjsProvider({ runtime: loadTransformers() })` from @hackbuild/devices and `mediapipeProvider({ runtime: loadTasksVision() })`, and each runtime loads at run time from its pinned URL.
- You call `attachVision(hub, tjs)` and expect models to load. It adds the records and the transformers.js loaders only; also call `hub.provide("tjs", tjs.factory)` and `hub.provide("mediapipe", mediapipeProvider(...))`.
- You expect MediaPipe weights to go through the weight store on their own. They load by URL from `MP_MODELS`; pass `store` to `mediapipeProvider` to read them through @hackbuild/weights with resume, sha-256 and the licence line.
- You expect YOLO or a model from `PICKER_RECORDS` to answer `detect` or a `model` id. None is registered by default; build YOLO with `yoloRecord({ url })` for an export you supply (licence AGPL-3.0 unless you pass `licence`) and add it, or any picker record, with `hub.registry.add`.
- You run `depth` on the main thread beside a render loop and trust `schedule` to keep the frames. Run `depthWorker({ urls: transformersUrls(), device })` instead; it loads only registered depth records and throws "is not a registered depth record" unless you pass `record` with its licence named.

## Errors this package throws

- `no face landmark model loaded: ID (ERROR); ...` (every record in the landmark chain failed; `failures` lists each): read `failures`; add `faceApiRecord(url)` as a fallback, or check the provider is registered
- `maskUnion: masks are W x H and W2 x H2` (and the other two mask operations) (masks of different sizes): resize one mask to the other first
- `cutoutRgba: image is W x H, mask W2 x H2` (image and mask differ in size): pass the mask made from this image
- `encodePng: N bytes for W x H x C` (data shorter than width times height times channels): pass the full buffer
- `maskFromRle: counts cover N pixels of M` (the run length does not match its size): check `size` is `[height, width]`
- `a prompt needs at least one point or a box` (a prompted segmenter got an empty prompt): pass points or a box, or call `segment` with no prompt for a person mask
- `ID: no mediapipe task for CAPABILITY` (the record's capability has no MediaPipe task): use detect, segment.person or a landmarks capability
- `ID: a mediapipe record needs source.url` (the record names no model file): set `source.url`
- `the transformers.js module has none of NAMES` (the runtime lacks the model class): use the pinned transformers.js 4.3.2
- `depth pipeline returned neither predicted_depth nor depth` (the pipeline gave another output): use a depth-estimation model
- `depth worker: ID is not a registered depth record; pass record with its licence named` (`modelId` is not one of the depth records): pass `record` with its licence
- `depth worker is not loaded` / `no transformers.js url loaded` (the worker could not import transformers.js): check the `urls`; use `transformersUrls()`

---

# @hackbuild/weights

> Download model weights once, resume them when the download breaks, check their SHA-256, and keep them on the machine for the next visit.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-browser-ai. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-browser-ai/docs/weights/

## Purpose

- Stores weight files over OPFS, Cache Storage, IndexedDB parts or memory, picking the first that opens.
- Resumes a broken download with a Range request guarded by If-Range, and hashes the bytes as they arrive.
- Reports progress even when the server sends no Content-Length, lists downloads in flight, and cancels one for every caller.
- Shares one download per key across callers, tabs and pages of one origin.
- Fetches multi file models (ONNX external data, transformers.js repos, GGUF splits) and serves as the transformers.js cache.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/weights @hackbuild/models
```

No dependencies and no peers. The quick start also installs @hackbuild/models for its model records and pinned hashes; the store does not need it. No weights ship with this package; each file keeps its own licence.

## Exports

### @hackbuild/weights

```ts
interface Backend {
  readonly name: BackendName;
  getMeta(key: string): Promise<Meta | null>;
  getPart(key: string, n: number): Promise<Blob | null>;
  keys(): Promise<string[]>;
  putMeta(meta: Meta): Promise<void>;
  putPart(key: string, n: number, part: Blob): Promise<void>;
  remove(key: string): Promise<void>;
}
```

A storage backend that keeps each weight file as numbered parts plus one meta record.

```ts
type BackendName = "opfs" | "cache" | "idb" | "memory"
```

Storage backends.

```ts
function cacheBackend(opts?: { cache?: string; caches?: CacheStorage; origin?: string }): Backend
```

Cache Storage parts at synthetic URLs.

```ts
interface DirLike {
  getDirectoryHandle(name: string, o?: { create?: boolean }): Promise<DirLike>;
  getFileHandle(name: string, o?: { create?: boolean }): Promise<{ createWritable(): Promise<{ close(): Promise<void>; write(d: string | Blob): Promise<void> }>; getFile(): Promise<Blob> }>;
  keys?(): AsyncIterable<string>;
  removeEntry(name: string, o?: { recursive?: boolean }): Promise<void>;
}
```

The parts of FileSystemDirectoryHandle the OPFS backend uses.

```ts
interface DownloadRow {
  fraction: number | null;
  key: string;
  loaded: number;
  total: number | null;
  url: string;
  waiters: number;
}
```

One download in flight, for a row with its own bar and cancel.

```ts
interface Estimate {
  quota: number | null;
  used: number | null;
  fits(bytes: number): boolean;
}
```

Used and quota bytes of this origin's storage, and whether a file of a given size fits.

```ts
interface GetOptions {
  onProgress?: (p: Progress) => void;
  resume?: boolean;
  signal?: AbortSignal;
}
```

Options for one `get`: a progress callback, an abort signal, and whether to resume.

```ts
function getRepo(store: WeightStore, repo: RepoRef, opts?: Omit<GetOptions, "onProgress"> & { onProgress?: (p: RepoProgress) => void }): Promise<Map<string, Blob>>
```

Fetch every file of a repo in order.

```ts
function hfResolve(repo: string, revision?: string, host?: string): string
```

Hugging Face resolve URL base for a repo and revision.

```ts
function idbBackend(opts?: { db?: string; indexedDB?: IDBFactory }): Backend
```

IndexedDB parts: one `kv` store with `<key>:meta` and `<key>:<n>` records.

```ts
interface LocksLike {
  request<T>(name: string, opts: { signal?: AbortSignal }, fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
}
```

The part of navigator.locks the store uses.

```ts
function memoryBackend(): Backend
```

A backend that keeps parts in memory for this tab only.

```ts
interface Meta {
  complete: boolean;
  etag: string | null;
  key: string;
  lastModified: string | null;
  licence: string;
  parts: number[];
  sha256: string | null;
  total: number | null;
  updated: number;
  url: string | null;
}
```

The stored record of one weight file: URL, licence, total, part sizes, validators and the SHA-256 once complete.

```ts
function openWeightStore(opts?: StoreOptions): Promise<WeightStore>
```

Open a store.

```ts
function opfsBackend(opts?: { dir?: string; root?: () => Promise<DirLike> }): Backend
```

Origin private file system: one directory per key, files `meta.json` and `<n>.part`.

```ts
function ortExternalData(files: Map<string, Blob>, graphPath: string): Promise<{ data: Uint8Array; path: string }[]>
```

onnxruntime-web `externalData` entries for a graph whose weights sit in side files (model.onnx plus model.onnx_data).

```ts
interface Progress {
  fraction: number | null;
  key: string;
  loaded: number;
  resuming: boolean;
  total: number | null;
}
```

Download progress of one file; `total` and `fraction` are null when the server sent no length.

```ts
interface RepoFile {
  optional?: boolean;
  path: string;
  sha256?: string;
}
```

One file of a multi file repo, by its path in the repo, with an optional SHA-256.

```ts
interface RepoProgress {
  count: number;
  file: string;
  fileProgress: Progress;
  index: number;
  loaded: number;
  total: number | null;
}
```

Progress over a whole repo: the current file, bytes so far and the known total.

```ts
interface RepoRef {
  base: string;
  files: readonly RepoFile[];
  keyPrefix?: string;
  licence: string;
}
```

A multi file model: base URL, file list, weight licence and key prefix.

```ts
class Sha256 {
  constructor();
  digestHex(): string;
  update(data: Uint8Array): this;
}
```

Incremental SHA-256: call `update` with each chunk as it arrives, then `digestHex` once, so a file of several GB is never held in one buffer.

```ts
function sha256Hex(data: Uint8Array): string
```

Lowercase hex SHA-256 of a byte array.

```ts
interface StoreOptions {
  backends?: "auto" | readonly (BackendName | Backend)[];
  estimate?: () => Promise<{ quota?: number; usage?: number }>;
  fetch?: (input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>;
  locks?: false | LocksLike;
  now?: () => number;
  onNotice?: (line: string) => void;
  partBytes?: number;
  persist?: () => Promise<boolean>;
  persisted?: () => Promise<boolean>;
  protocol?: string;
}
```

Options for `openWeightStore`: backend order, part size, fetch, the licence notice, storage estimate, persistence and Web Locks.

```ts
function transformersCache(store: WeightStore, opts: { licenceFor: (url: string) => string | null; onProgress?: (p: Progress) => void; sha256For?: (url: string) => string | undefined }): { match(req: string | Request): Promise<Response | undefined>; put(req: string | Request, res: Response): Promise<void> }
```

A cache object for transformers.js (`env.useCustomCache = true; env.customCache = transformersCache(store, ...)`).

```ts
class WeightError extends Error {
  constructor(code: "http" | "sha256" | "quota" | "abort" | "range", message: string);
  readonly code: "http" | "sha256" | "quota" | "abort" | "range";
}
```

The error the store throws, with a `code` of "http", "sha256", "quota", "abort" or "range".

```ts
interface WeightRef {
  key?: string;
  licence: string;
  sha256?: string;
  url: string;
}
```

A weight file to fetch: URL, cache key, SHA-256 when known, and the weight licence.

```ts
interface WeightStore {
  readonly backend: Backend;
  cancel(key: string): boolean;
  downloads(): DownloadRow[];
  estimate(): Promise<Estimate>;
  evict(key: string): Promise<void>;
  get(ref: WeightRef, opts?: GetOptions): Promise<Blob>;
  has(key: string): Promise<boolean>;
  keys(): Promise<string[]>;
  meta(key: string): Promise<Meta | null>;
  once(ref: WeightRef, opts?: GetOptions): Promise<Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>>;
  onDownloads(fn: (rows: DownloadRow[]) => void): () => void;
  persist(): Promise<boolean>;
  persisted(): Promise<boolean | null>;
  put(ref: Omit<WeightRef, "url"> & { key: string; url?: string }, data: Blob | ArrayBuffer | Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>): Promise<Blob>;
  release(key: string): void;
}
```

A weight store: get with resume, put files the user supplied, list, evict, cancel, track downloads and estimate space.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { CATALOG, pinnedBase, pinnedSha } from "@hackbuild/models";
import { openWeightStore, WeightError } from "@hackbuild/weights";

// one store over opfs, indexeddb parts, cache storage or memory, the first that opens
const store = await openWeightStore();
console.log("stored in", store.backend.name, (await store.estimate()).quota, "bytes of quota");

// Qwen2.5 0.5B Instruct q4_k_m GGUF: the record names the repo, the file and the weight licence (Apache-2.0)
const rec = CATALOG.find((r) => r.id === "qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-gguf")!;
const url = pinnedBase(rec.source!.repo!) + rec.source!.file!;
const sha256 = pinnedSha(url);
try {
  // an interrupted download resumes on the next get; the bytes are checked against the pinned sha-256
  const ref = { url, key: `gguf:${rec.id}`, licence: rec.licence, ...(sha256 ? { sha256 } : {}) };
  const gguf = await store.get(ref, { onProgress: (p) => console.log(p.fraction === null ? `${(p.loaded / 1e6).toFixed(0)} MB` : `${(p.fraction * 100).toFixed(0)}%`) });
  console.log(gguf.size, "bytes, cached for the next visit");
} catch (e) {
  // code is http, sha256, quota, abort or range
  if (e instanceof WeightError) console.log(e.code, e.message);
}
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- You `fetch` weight URLs yourself or bundle the files. Open one store with `openWeightStore()` and call `store.get({ url, key, licence })`; it resumes a broken download with a Range request and keeps the bytes for the next visit.
- You write the licence as a string in your code. Take it from the model record, `licence: rec.licence` from @hackbuild/models, and pass `sha256: pinnedSha(url)` when the file is pinned; a mismatch removes the parts and throws `WeightError` code `sha256`.
- You call `store.get` once per session attempt when a runtime tries several sessions on one file. Use `store.once(ref)` so every attempt reads one download, and `release(key)` when you are done.
- You hand transformers.js its own cache and lose resume and the licence line. Set `env.customCache` to `transformersCache(store, { licenceFor, sha256For: pinnedSha })`, where `licenceFor(url)` returns the `licence` of the model record whose repo the URL names, or null for files the store should not fetch itself.
- You expect OPFS or Cache Storage on a file:// page. `auto` leaves both out there and the store lands on IndexedDB parts, then memory.
- You treat `WeightError` code `quota` as a failed download. It is thrown before the body is read when free space is under 1.2 times the file; evict other keys or call `store.persist()`, and catch code `http` to call `get` again, which resumes.

## Errors this package throws

- `fetch <url> failed: ...` (code `http`) (network, CORS or a wrong URL): check the URL and that the host allows the page's origin
- `http <status> for <url>` (code `http`) (the server answered with an error): check the URL and revision
- `download of <key> broke at <n> bytes, parts kept for resume: ...` (code `http`) (the stream broke): call `get` again; it resumes
- `download of <key> ended at <n> of <total> bytes; parts kept for resume` (code `http`) (the server closed early): call `get` again
- `parts of <key> went missing after the download` (code `http`) (the browser cleared storage mid download): call `store.persist()`, then `get` again
- `server resumed <key> at <start>, expected <offset>` (code `range`) (the 206 started at the wrong byte): `store.evict(key)` and download again
- `sha256 of <key> is <digest>, expected <sha256>; the parts were removed` (code `sha256`) (the file differs from the pinned hash): pin the revision the hash belongs to, or update the hash
- `not enough storage for <key>: needs <total> bytes plus a 20 percent margin, <free> free` (code `quota`) (less free space than 1.2 times the file): evict other keys, or call `store.persist()`
- `download of <key> aborted ...` (code `abort`) (the signal aborted or `cancel` ran): none; the parts are kept
- `sha256: update after digest`, `sha256: digest called twice` (a `Sha256` used after `digestHex`): make a new `Sha256` per file
